articles.title: And the Crown Goes to... Indiana! Hoosiers Win at the Big House for the First Time Since 1967
articles.byline: Mallory Penhallow, The Indiana Fanatic
articles.matchup: Indiana 13, Michigan 6 (final, OT), Sat., Oct. 24, Michigan Stadium
articles.text:
Good morning, America. I'd like to thank the judges, the Big House, and every single Hoosier who stood in the cold until overtime. Mallory Penhallow here, former Miss Monroe County runner-up, and darlings, I finally have a crown. Indiana 13, Michigan 6, in overtime, in front of 111,276 people. The AP says it's Indiana's first win at Michigan Stadium since 1967. Fifty-nine years! My sash is soaked in happy tears.

Now, the talent portion was not pretty. Through four quarters, Indiana had two field goals from Nico Radicic, from 22 and 34 yards. Michigan had two field goals. Michigan's last one came as time expired, after the Wolverines reached our 3 and our defense sacked Tommy Carr for a fourth time to force the kick. Tied 6-6. Into the evening gown round we went.

Overtime, first snap: Josh Hoover, who is banged up and nearly got benched, threw a 21-yard pass to Brock Schott. Then he ran it in himself from 4 yards out. Michigan got the ball back, reached our 13, and Carr's last pass hit the turf in front of Salesi Moa just outside the end zone. I screamed so loud I lost my pageant voice.

Hero: the defense, which kept Michigan out of the end zone all day and held the Wolverines to 57 rushing yards. Rolijah Hardy made nine tackles with two sacks. Amare Ferrell intercepted a pass, and Michigan lost a fumble too. Hoover gets the crown jewel for gutting it out. The goat, affectionately: our passing game, 8 of 18 for 81 yards. Nobody wins Miss Congeniality every year.

What it means: Indiana is 7-1 and 4-1 in the Big Ten and jumped from No. 6 to No. 4 in the AP poll released Oct. 25. After coming up inches short against Ohio State, the Hoosiers still have never lost two straight in Curt Cignetti's three years, per the AP. Poise, posture and a defense that won't let you breathe.

Next up: Minnesota visits Memorial Stadium in Bloomington on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS. Halloween at home. I'm going as a 1967 Hoosier, which is to say, a winner in Ann Arbor.

Thank you, thank you. Wave from the elbow, and go Hoosiers!

articles.title: Hallelujah, Pass the Biscuits: Terrence Brown Runs Wild, Bourgeois Goes 4-for-4, and the Blue Raiders Kneel It Out in Miami
articles.byline: Opal Stonebriar, The Middle Tennessee Fanatic
articles.matchup: Middle Tennessee 26, Florida International 23 (final), Tue. Oct. 20, Pitbull Stadium
articles.text:
Well, hey there, sugar. Opal Stonebriar, front-row grandma of Murfreesboro, still humming the closing hymn from Tuesday night. Take a biscuit and sit down, because Middle Tennessee went to Pitbull Stadium and won 26-23, and baby, I have not sat down since.

I'm a choir director, so here's the service in three hymns.

Hymn one: the double portion. With one second left in the first half, FIU lined up a 46-yard field goal. J. Williams blocked it, but we were offside, so they tried again. Ashton Taylor blocked that one too. Same kick, blocked twice, in one second. In my church we call that a double portion.

Hymn two: the shout. FIU tied it 16-16 late in the third quarter. Four plays later, Terrence Brown went 54 yards up the middle for a touchdown, and Rutherford County felt the floor shake. Terrence finished with 158 yards on 18 carries.

Hymn three: the benediction. FIU scored with 6:06 left to make it 26-23. Our boys took the ball at our own 25 and never gave it back. Eleven plays, 71 yards, every last second. Then we knelt down twice at the FIU doorstep. We were close enough to score. We chose mercy. That's Christian football.

My heroes: Terrence, and Dominic Bourgeois, who made field goals of 51, 39, 50 and 28 yards. Four tries, four makes. When the offering plate comes by, that young man will put it through the uprights from midfield. Roman Gagliano threw for 200 yards with no turnovers, and we held the ball for 33:13. Heavy and lasting, the way Grandma likes her pound cake.

My affectionate goat is the penalty flag: nine for 57 yards, including a holding call on that last drive that gave me the vapors.

What it means: the Blue Raiders are 4-3 and 2-1 in Conference USA, right behind 3-0 Liberty and Jacksonville State. Our bus has gas in it.

Next up, Kennesaw State visits Floyd Stadium on Wednesday, Oct. 28, at 7 p.m. ET on CBS Sports Network. Bring a casserole and wear that true blue. I'll save you a seat on the front row, sugar. Grandma always does.

articles.title: Ay, Abuela, the Sugar Packets Blinked: FIU Rallies Back Twice, Then Watches Middle Tennessee Keep the Ball for the Last 6:06
articles.byline: Lourdes Ibarguen-Tate, The Florida International Fanatic
articles.matchup: Middle Tennessee 26, Florida International 23 (final), Tue. Oct. 20, Pitbull Stadium
articles.text:
¡Hola, Panther people! Lourdes Ibarguen-Tate, back at the kitchen table in Sweetwater, where abuela has knocked every domino onto the floor. Middle Tennessee beat us 26-23 on Tuesday night at Pitbull Stadium. Abuela says a loss told honestly is still a story worth telling, so here it is. Then I'm eating a pastelito.

The good first. JJ Kohl threw three touchdown passes: 49 yards to Kyle McNeal, 1 yard to Kevin Schaeffer, and 21 yards to Sterling Joseph. Down 16-8 in the third, Devonte Lyons ran in the two-point try to tie it 16-16, and I knocked my cafecito over. Worth it. Devonte had 115 yards on 19 carries. He runs like he's late for Sunday dinner at abuela's, which is the fastest a human being can move.

Now the plays that hurt. At the end of the first half, our 46-yard field goal got blocked, a penalty gave us a do-over, and it got blocked again. Twice! In one second! Four plays after we tied it, Terrence Brown went 54 yards for a touchdown. And after Kohl hit Joseph to make it 26-23 with 6:06 left, we never saw the ball again. Middle Tennessee ran 11 plays and knelt down at our doorstep. Abuela says keeping the dominoes for six straight minutes is not a strategy, it's a hostage situation.

My hero is Wesley Miller. Sixteen tackles, 13 of them solo. Abuela asked if he was twins. He is just everywhere, like a cousin at a quinceañera.

My goat, with love: the field goal gremlins. Block it the third time and see what happens, abuela says.

What it means: FIU is 3-4 and 1-2 in Conference USA, with back-to-back losses by exactly three points, at Jacksonville State and now at home. Abuela says, "Mija, a team that keeps losing by three is about to start winning by three." I wrote it on a napkin.

To Opal and the Blue Raider folks: congratulations. Enjoy the biscuits. We had croquetas, and we're fine emotionally, thank you.

Next up, FIU visits 6-1 Liberty at Williams Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS Sports Network. It's Halloween, so I'm dressing the sugar packets up as a brick wall. Bring a colada. ¡Vamos, Panthers!

articles.title: Rapids Ahead: Isaiah Myers Goes for 242, but the Bears Flip the Canoe in Newark
articles.byline: Clementine Bilyeu, The Missouri State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Delaware 61, Missouri State 38 (final), Tue. Oct. 20, Delaware Stadium
articles.text:
Howdy from the Ozarks. Clementine Bilyeu here, wringing out my socks on the bank of the James River. I guide float trips for a living, and Tuesday night in Newark was one of those floats where the first hour is glorious and then you meet a rock with your name on it. Delaware beat us 61-38.

The glorious part was real. J.J. O'Neal grabbed a Delaware pass and took it back 47 yards for a touchdown, and we led 14-7 after one quarter. Henry Belin IV found Isaiah Myers twice for touchdowns, the second with 14 seconds left in the half, and the Bears went to the locker room up 28-24. Connor Lair ran for two touchdowns, and we were still ahead 35-31 midway through the third.

Then came the rock. Down 38-35, Belin got sacked by Jawarren Corbin, the ball came loose, and B. Gorham returned it 59 yards to our 4. Delaware scored on the next play. After that, Corbin intercepted Belin, George Mullins intercepted Belin, and Delaware rattled off 30 straight points. That's not a rapid, friends. That's a waterfall.

My hero is Isaiah Myers: 11 catches, 242 yards, two touchdowns. He was a downstream current all night, and I'd let him steer my canoe anytime. Belin threw for 337 yards and kept chucking it, God bless him.

My affectionate goat is the yellow flag: 12 penalties for 100 yards. You can't paddle upstream with the anchor dragging, kids.

What it means: the Bears are 2-5 and 1-2 in Conference USA. That's a bumpy float, but there's a lot of river left, and the next stretch is calm water at home.

Next up, Sam Houston comes to Plaster Stadium on Tuesday, Oct. 27, at 8 p.m. ET on ESPN2. Plaster's been around since 1941, built as a WPA project, so it's seen worse nights than this one, and better ones coming. Pack a snack and a dry bag, Bears fans. We're putting back in.

articles.title: Overdue Notice Paid in Full: Minicucci Throws Five Touchdowns, Corbin Wrecks the Night, and the Blue Hens Drop 61
articles.byline: Hen Lofland, The Delaware Fanatic
articles.matchup: Delaware 61, Missouri State 38 (final), Tue. Oct. 20, Delaware Stadium
articles.text:
Good evening, and you may raise your voices. Hen Lofland here, from behind the circulation desk in Newark, where I am officially stamping the losing streak "RETURNED." Delaware beat Missouri State 61-38 on Tuesday night, ending a three-game skid, and I have not shushed a single soul since.

Let me footnote the turning points.

Footnote one: halftime. We trailed 28-24, and Missouri State's Isaiah Myers was having the night of his life. Then Nick Minicucci came out and threw a 12-yard touchdown pass to Jo Silver and a 3-yarder to Elijah Sessoms. We were back in front 38-35.

Footnote two: the chapter break. Jawarren Corbin sacked Henry Belin IV, the ball came loose, and B. Gorham scooped it and ran 59 yards to the Missouri State 4. Minicucci ran it in himself on the next snap. Corbin wasn't finished, either. He intercepted Belin in the fourth, George Mullins had one too, and we scored 30 straight points before the Bears kicked a late field goal. That's not a comeback. That's a sequel.

Footnote three: Bryson Graves, who returned five kickoffs for 160 yards, including runbacks of 42 and 63 in the third quarter. Every time Missouri State kicked to him, I heard a page turn.

My hero is Minicucci: 20 of 29 for 225 yards, five touchdown passes, plus a rushing touchdown. Six touchdowns in one night. I'd like to have that bound and shelved. Corbin is co-hero for a sack, a forced fumble and an interception. Jo Silver ran for 101 yards, and we went 5-for-5 on fourth down.

Goat? Fine, the defense gave up 242 receiving yards to one man. We'll call that a book we checked out but did not finish.

What it means: the Blue Hens are 3-4 and 1-2 in Conference USA. Delaware claims six national titles. Tuesday felt like chapter one of a seventh, and I'm only a little biased.

Next up, Delaware visits Western Kentucky on Tuesday, Oct. 27, at 7 p.m. ET on CBS Sports Network. Two Tuesdays in a row under the lights. Bring your library card and your loudest voice. Book club meets at kickoff.

articles.title: Float Stalled at the Judges' Stand: South Alabama Ties It Late, Then Watches Marshall Roll Past 20-13
articles.byline: Azalea Fairhope-Grice, The South Alabama Fanatic
articles.matchup: Marshall 20, South Alabama 13 (final), Tue. Oct. 20, Joan C. Edwards Stadium
articles.text:
Well, hey, y'all. Azalea Fairhope-Grice here, beads still around my neck and glue gun unplugged in mourning. I grade football like a Mardi Gras float: Is it bold? Does it move? Did the crowd scream? Tuesday night in Huntington, our float was gorgeous for three and a half quarters, then lost a wheel in front of the judges. Marshall won 20-13.

Here's how the parade went sideways.

First, the long stall. It was 6-6 at the half on four field goals, and our offense went 4-for-18 on third down. Jared Hollins completed 12 of 33. That's a float stuck at the corner of Government and Royal while the crowd checks its watch.

Second, the one bead we threw to the wrong side of the street. In the third quarter, Cole Funderburk intercepted Hollins at midfield, Marshall hit a 38-yard pass, and Zion Turner ran it in from the 3. Then Davis Little missed a 45-yarder.

Third, the gut punch. PJ Martin, bless him, ran 19 yards for the tying touchdown with 4:38 left, and I screamed so loud a krewe captain in Mobile turned around. Marshall answered with eight plays and 75 yards, and Judah Price scored from the 5 with 1:49 to go. Our last drive ended on a fourth-down incompletion at our own 34.

My hero is PJ Martin, plus a defense that held Marshall to 328 yards while Marshall's kicker missed from 49 and 27. And we went 5-for-6 on fourth down. That's a float with guts.

My affectionate goat is third down. Four for 18, darlin'. My volleyball girls convert more than that serving underhanded.

What it means: the Jaguars are 4-3 and still 2-1 in the Sun Belt. One bad parade doesn't cancel Carnival, and Mobile invented Carnival in this country, back in 1703. We know how to come back next year. Or next week.

Next up, Louisiana Tech comes to Hancock Whitney Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3 p.m. ET on ESPN+. Halloween at home. Dress up as a first down, y'all. Throw me 20.

articles.title: We Are... Clutch: Judah Price Punches It In With 1:49 Left, and the Herd Holds On at the Joan
articles.byline: Mercy Holderby, The Marshall Fanatic
articles.matchup: Marshall 20, South Alabama 13 (final), Tue. Oct. 20, Joan C. Edwards Stadium
articles.text:
How am I? We are. Mercy Holderby here, green ribbon on the microphone and a voice that is officially out of commission after Tuesday night. Marshall beat South Alabama 20-13 at Joan C. Edwards Stadium, and the night-shift nurses on my floor will have to communicate with me by sign language until Thursday.

Let me chart the vitals.

Vital sign one: patience. It was 6-6 at the half. Jorge Diaz Nicolas hit field goals from 47 and 48 yards, and our defense kept South Alabama's offense in triage.

Vital sign two: the takeaway. In the third quarter, Cole Funderburk intercepted Jared Hollins at midfield. Soon after, Zion Turner threw a 38-yard dart to Adrian Norton, and then Turner ran it in from 3 yards out. Thirteen to six, and the Joan was rocking.

Vital sign three: the code. South Alabama tied it at 13 with 4:38 left, and my heart rate did something I'd chart as "concerning." Then the Herd went 75 yards in eight plays. Khalil Wilkins ripped off 14 yards to the 9, and Judah Price bulled in from the 5 with 1:49 left. On South Alabama's last chance, B. Ward hurried Hollins into a fourth-down incompletion. Patient stable. Discharge papers signed.

My hero is Zion Turner: 21 of 33 for 181 yards, a rushing touchdown, and zero turnovers. After six turnovers against Coastal earlier this month, a clean chart is beautiful. Funderburk and Ward are co-heroes. The defense held the Jaguars to 4-of-18 on third down.

My affectionate goat: the kicking game, which also missed from 49 and 27 yards. Jorge, honey, I love you. Next time, aim for the middle.

What it means: Marshall is 4-3 and 1-2 in the Sun Belt, and that sour taste from the Coastal loss is finally gone. We needed a win at home, and the Herd brought one.

Next up, Marshall visits Old Dominion at S.B. Ballard Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 1 p.m. ET on ESPN+. Halloween in Norfolk. I'm going as a nurse, which is not a costume, it's a lifestyle. Herd up, friends. How are we? We are... Marshall!

articles.title: Hatch Hot in Huntsville: James Jones Runs for 178, the Defense Slams the Goal-Line Door, and the Aggies Win on the Road
articles.byline: Esperanza Lujan-Tafoya, The New Mexico State Fanatic
articles.matchup: New Mexico State 30, Sam Houston 24 (final), Wed. Oct. 21, Elliott T. Bowers Stadium
articles.text:
¡Buenas noches, Aggies! Esperanza Lujan-Tafoya here, a chile farmer's daughter from Las Cruces, still fanning my mouth after Wednesday night. New Mexico State beat Sam Houston 30-24 at Bowers Stadium. Our first road win of the season, and it came roasted.

On my chile scale, here are the moments that decided it.

Josiah Charles' interception: Hatch hot. In the second quarter, we trailed 7-0 after a blocked punt was returned for a touchdown, which on my scale is a jalapeño in the eye. Then Josiah picked off Landyn Locke and ran it back 25 yards to the 1. James Jones walked in on the next play.

The third quarter: ghost-pepper hot. We trailed 17-14 after an 81-yard touchdown pass. Then Adam Damante hit AJ Williams III from 5 yards out, Kyah Francone kicked a 25-yard field goal, K. Roberts-Day recovered a fumble, and TJ Washington Jr. scored from the 7. Sixteen points in one quarter. Somebody get me a glass of milk.

The goal-line stand: so hot I needed a minute alone. Early in the fourth, Sam Houston drove deep into our end. Our defense held, and their fourth-down pass into the end zone fell incomplete. Then, after the Bearkats made it 30-24 with 4:00 left, our offense ran six plays and never gave the ball back. James Jones moved the chains on a 2-yard run, we took a knee in spirit, and the clock hit zero.

My hero is James Jones: 27 carries, 178 yards and a touchdown. He ran like a man carrying a sack of fresh-roasted chile to the farmers market before it sells out. AJ Williams caught two touchdown passes. Our defense held Sam Houston to 11 rushing yards. Eleven!

My affectionate goat: third down. We went 2-for-12. That's a mild salsa, mijo, and we serve hot food in this house.

What it means: the Aggies are 3-4 and 2-1 in Conference USA, tied in the loss column with Middle Tennessee and WKU behind the 3-0 teams. The green chile is in season, and so are we.

Next up, Jacksonville State comes to Aggie Memorial Stadium on Wednesday, Oct. 28, at 8 p.m. ET on ESPN2. The Gamecocks are 3-0 in the league. Grab your green chile stew, Aggies. It's going to be a spicy Wednesday.

articles.title: A Ballad With a Sad Third Verse: Railyn Adams Shines, Tim Burns Goes 81, but the Aggies Ride Out of Huntsville With a 30-24 Win
articles.byline: Lem Coxwell, The Sam Houston Fanatic
articles.matchup: New Mexico State 30, Sam Houston 24 (final), Wed. Oct. 21, Elliott T. Bowers Stadium
articles.text:
Evenin', folks. Pull up a stump. Lem Coxwell here, Walker County born, history teacher by trade and keeper of Texas folklore by calling. Wednesday night's tale at Bowers Stadium had a hero, a villain and a sad third verse. New Mexico State won 30-24.

Verse one is a good one. Early in the first quarter, our special teams blocked a punt and Railyn Adams scooped it into the end zone. Seven to nothing before anybody found their seat. Later, Sam Carpenter hit a 38-yard field goal, and we led 10-7.

Verse two had a lightning bolt. To open the second half, Landyn Locke threw it to Tim Burns Jr., and Tim ran 81 yards for a touchdown. We led 17-14. If General Houston had a man that fast at San Jacinto, the battle would've been over in nine minutes instead of 18.

Verse three is where the ballad turns sad. New Mexico State scored 16 straight points in the third quarter, helped by a lateral that came loose on our end. Then, early in the fourth, we drove deep into Aggie territory and came away with nothing after a fourth-down throw into the end zone fell incomplete. MJ Dowdy finally scored from the 1 with 4:00 left after Railyn Adams intercepted Adam Damante, but the Aggies ran out the clock.

My hero is Railyn Adams: a blocked-punt touchdown and an interception. Tim Burns Jr. had 117 receiving yards. Our defense held the Aggies to 2-of-12 on third down.

My affectionate goat is the penalty flag. Thirteen of them for 118 yards. In Sam Houston's day, a man with 13 infractions got sent to the territories. We also ran for 11 yards on 20 carries. Our run game needs a revival tent.

What it means: the Bearkats are 1-6 and 0-3 in Conference USA. That's a hard chapter. But General Houston lost a few skirmishes before San Jacinto, and Huntsville still built him a 67-foot statue.

Next up, Sam Houston visits Missouri State at Plaster Stadium on Tuesday, Oct. 27, at 8 p.m. ET on ESPN2. Both teams are looking for a better verse. Bring a lawn chair and a story, folks. I'll bring the history.

articles.title: Up the Mountain, Down Again: The Dukes' Perfect Season Slips Away in Overtime in Boone, 34-31
articles.byline: Lila Shenandoah, The James Madison Fanatic
articles.matchup: App State 34, James Madison 31 (final, OT), Thu. Oct. 22, Kidd Brewer Stadium
articles.text:
Ready? Okay... actually, give me a second. Lila Shenandoah here, pom-poms drooping, glitter going everywhere, and my voice left somewhere on the side of Howard's Knob. Thursday night at Kidd Brewer Stadium, App State beat James Madison 34-31 in overtime. The zero in our loss column is gone, y'all. I'm going to cheer anyway, because that's what cheerleaders do.

Here are the three plays that broke my heart.

Play one: the interception. It was 24-24 with just over six minutes left. Colton Phares picked off Camden Coleman and returned it 21 yards to our 14. Moments later, Henry Hasselbeck threw a 4-yard touchdown pass to Luke Douglas. Thirty-one to 24, and 33,322 Mountaineer fans made a noise I'll hear in my dreams.

Play two: the comeback. Dukes don't quit, honey. Camden drove us down the field, and with three seconds left, he ran it in from 6 yards out himself. Thirty-one all! I did a toe-touch so high I may have entered North Carolina airspace.

Play three: overtime. We had the ball first, lost 11 yards on a run, and Morgan Suarez's 47-yard kick missed. Then James London kicked a 40-yarder for App State, and that was that.

My hero is Braeden Wisloski, who caught a 70-yard touchdown pass from JC Evans that had me shrieking. Camden also deserves a cartwheel: 232 passing yards, a touchdown pass and the tying score.

My affectionate goat is the kicking game. Suarez went 1-for-3 and had one blocked. Morgan, sweetie, it's okay. We still love you. We also went 2-for-15 on third down, which is not a cheer, it's a cry for help.

What it means: the Dukes are 7-1 and 4-1 in the Sun Belt. One loss, on the road, in overtime, on a mountain. That's a stumble, not a fall. Harrisonburg has the best food in Virginia, and we'll eat our feelings downtown this weekend.

Next up, Troy comes to Bridgeforth Stadium on Thursday, Oct. 29, at 7:30 p.m. ET on ESPN2. Home sweet home. Ready? Okay! "Purple! Reign! Shake it off and win again!"

articles.title: The View Was Worth the Climb: James London Splits It in Overtime, and App State Knocks Off Unbeaten JMU in Overtime
articles.byline: Zebulon 'Zeb' Coldiron, The App State Fanatic
articles.matchup: App State 34, James Madison 31 (final, OT), Thu. Oct. 22, Kidd Brewer Stadium
articles.text:
Mornin' from the porch. Zeb Coldiron here, notebook open, coffee long gone cold, and voice gone hoarse from Thursday night. Kidd Brewer Stadium, 33,322 strong, wind off the ridge, and a 7-0 James Madison team came up our mountain. They left with a loss. App State won 34-31 in overtime. Let's take this hike one switchback at a time.

Switchback one: the takeaway. It was 24-24 with about six minutes left when Colton Phares picked off Camden Coleman and returned it 21 yards to the JMU 14. Moments later, Henry Hasselbeck hit Luke Douglas for a 4-yard touchdown. Hasselbeck also threw the earlier touchdown pass to Chris Lofton that, with Malachi Singleton's two-point pass to Sam Pickett III, tied it at 21. Not bad for a backup.

Switchback two: the loose gravel. JMU drove the length of the field and scored with three seconds left. Thirty-one all. I said a word on the porch my mama wouldn't have approved of.

Switchback three: the summit. JMU had the ball first in overtime and lost 11 yards on a run. Their 47-yard kick missed. Then we ran two plays, set it up in the middle, and James London split it from 40.

My hero is James London. Four field goals on four tries, including the winner, plus two extra points. That's 14 points from a kicker. Malachi Singleton deserves a nod too: 26 of 40 for 271 yards and two touchdowns. And the defense blocked a field goal and held JMU to 2-of-15 on third down.

My affectionate goat: the late lead we let slip. Up seven with under six minutes left, and we gave up a tying drive. That one made my blood pressure climb faster than the road up from Blowing Rock.

What it means: App State is 5-2 and 2-1 in the Sun Belt after its second straight win, and we just beat the conference's last unbeaten team. Boone sits at 3,333 feet, and the view from up here looks mighty fine.

Next up, App State visits Georgia Southern at Allen E. Paulson Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 6:30 p.m. ET on ESPN+. Halloween in Statesboro. Bring a jacket, Mountaineers. Slow down, the view's worth the wait.

articles.title: Sixth Straight Blessing: Jaylon Coleman Scores Twice, the Defense Steals Two, and Liberty Rolls at Kennesaw State, 34-6
articles.byline: Gideon Fairweather, The Liberty Fanatic
articles.matchup: Liberty 34, Kennesaw State 6 (final), Thu. Oct. 22, Walens Family Field at Fifth Third Stadium
articles.text:
Well, praise the Lord and pass the program! Gideon Fairweather here, youth pastor, middle-school coach, and a man who drove home from Georgia on Thursday night humming hymns at highway speed. Liberty beat Kennesaw State 34-6 at Fifth Third Stadium. Revenge for two years of losses to the Owls, served with grace and a big ol' side of rushing yards.

Here's the sermon in three points.

Point one: the early fire. Kam Davis punched in a 1-yard touchdown run in the first quarter. Then, late in the quarter, Deshawn Purdie threw a 56-yard touchdown pass to Jaylon Coleman. Fourteen to nothing. My middle schoolers would say that's "bussin'." I would say it's righteous.

Point two: the fourth-down stands. Kennesaw State went for it on fourth down at our 23 in the first quarter, and E. Hopkins broke up the pass. Our defense also stopped Boogie Woods III for no gain on fourth down late in the third quarter. Brothers and sisters, that's how you hold the fort.

Point three: the turnovers. Early in the third quarter, Derrell Farrar intercepted Rickie Collins at the Kennesaw State 12, and Chase Reeves kicked a field goal. Later, Ashton McShane picked off another pass, and before the quarter ended, Jaylon Coleman ran it in from the 9 for his second touchdown. Twenty-four to 3, and the Flames were cooking.

My hero is Jaylon Coleman: a 56-yard touchdown catch and a 9-yard touchdown run. The run game also piled up 215 yards, and we held the ball for over 37 minutes. That's a sermon that runs long, and nobody minds.

My affectionate goat: the penalty flags. Twelve of them for 85 yards. Fellas, we talked about self-control in Bible study.

What it means: Liberty is 6-1, 3-0 in Conference USA, and tied at the top with Jacksonville State. That's six straight wins. Lynchburg has been here since 1757, and Thomas Jefferson called it "the most interesting spot in the state." He hadn't seen this defense.

Next up, FIU comes to Williams Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBSSN. Bless these young men on both sidelines. Play hard, play fair, and let's see the joy on their faces.

articles.title: Bug Report: Liberty Crashes the Owls' System, 34-6, and Kennesaw State Needs a Major Patch
articles.byline: Ximena Holcombe-Reyes, The Kennesaw State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Liberty 34, Kennesaw State 6 (final), Thu. Oct. 22, Walens Family Field at Fifth Third Stadium
articles.text:
Hey, Owl Nation. Ximena Holcombe-Reyes here, logging in from Marietta. Today's post is a bug report, and it's a long one. Liberty beat Kennesaw State 34-6 on Thursday night at Fifth Third Stadium. I've run diagnostics, and here's the log.

Bug one: early crash. Liberty scored twice in the first quarter, including a 56-yard touchdown pass from Deshawn Purdie to Jaylon Coleman. In between, we went for it on fourth down at the Liberty 23, and the pass was broken up. Error 404: points not found.

Bug two: the turnovers. Early in the third quarter, Derrell Farrar intercepted Rickie Collins at our 12, and Liberty kicked a field goal. A few minutes later, Ashton McShane picked off Collins again, and Coleman ran in from the 9 to make it 24-3. Two interceptions, and Liberty put up 10 points in that quarter. That's a memory leak.

Bug three: the run defense. Liberty ran 41 times for 215 yards and held the ball for over 37 minutes. Our defense spent so long on the field that I started to worry about overheating.

My heroes are Daniel Kinney, who went 2-for-2 on field goals, and Landon Varnes, who came in and completed 9 of 15 passes for 111 yards. Our offense also put together a 12-play, 65-yard drive in the fourth quarter. Small features, but they shipped.

My affectionate goat: the scoreboard. Six points against a team we beat in 2024 and 2025. I'm not mad, Owls. I'm just running git blame.

What it means: Kennesaw State is 1-6 and 0-3 in Conference USA, and the losing streak is at six. That's a rough build. But this program only started playing football in 2015 and won the Conference USA title last year. We've debugged worse.

Next up, the Owls visit Middle Tennessee at Johnny "Red" Floyd Stadium on Wednesday, Oct. 28, at 7 p.m. ET on CBSSN. Wear your gold, Owl Nation. Bugs happen. We patch them, and we ship again.

articles.title: Scuttled in Overtime: The Pirates Lead by 14, Tie It With 90 Seconds Left, and Still Sink in Memphis, 41-34
articles.byline: Bartholomew 'Bart' Quidley, The East Carolina Fanatic
articles.matchup: Memphis 41, East Carolina 34 (final, OT), Thu. Oct. 22, Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium
articles.text:
Ahoy, mateys. Bart Quidley here, and the purple tricorn hat is back in its box with a tear stain on the brim. I wore it to Memphis on Thursday night. For three quarters, it was the luckiest hat in Pitt County. Then Memphis beat East Carolina 41-34 in overtime, and now it's just a hat.

Here's how the ship went down.

First, the plunder. We led 16-3 at halftime. Noah Perez kicked four field goals on the night, including a 49-yarder as the first half ended, after D. Speer forced a punt-return fumble and B. Shirley recovered it. Early in the third, TJ Engleman Jr. ran it in from 4 yards out, and Mitch Griffis hit Landon Sides for two. Pirates 24, Tigers 10. I was ordering the grog.

Second, the mutiny. Marcus Stokes threw three touchdown passes and ran for two more after halftime. Memphis took a 34-27 lead with 3:31 left.

Third, the last broadside. Griffis drove us down the field and threw a 20-yard touchdown pass to Landon Sides with 1:30 left. Thirty-four all! I nearly threw the tricorn into the Mississippi. But in overtime, Memphis scored in two plays. We drove to the Memphis 4, and Ellis Ellis Jr. intercepted Griffis in the end zone. Down to Davy Jones' locker.

My hero is Landon Sides: seven catches, 130 yards, the tying touchdown and a two-point catch. Noah Perez went 4-for-4 on field goals and scored 14 points. Engleman ran for 92 yards.

My affectionate goat: the second half. We gave up 38 points after the break. Matey, that's not a defense, that's a plank.

What it means: the Pirates are 3-4 and 1-2 in the American after back-to-back losses, both on the road and both in overtime. Two heartbreakers in a row is a rough voyage, but Greenville has weathered worse storms. Dowdy-Ficklen holds 51,000, and it's time to fill it.

Next up, Temple comes to Dowdy-Ficklen Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3 p.m. ET on ESPN+. Halloween at home. Wear your best pirate costume, which in Greenville is just regular clothes. Hoist the colors, mateys. The tricorn is coming back out.

articles.title: The Comeback Blues: Marcus Stokes Scores Five Times After Halftime, and Memphis Rallies Past East Carolina in Overtime, 41-34
articles.byline: Otis Delaney-Crum, The Memphis Fanatic
articles.matchup: Memphis 41, East Carolina 34 (final, OT), Thu. Oct. 22, Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium
articles.text:
Well, good evening, Bluff City. Otis Delaney-Crum here, guitar on my knee, rib sauce on my sleeve, and a voice that cracked on the high notes Thursday night. Memphis beat East Carolina 41-34 in overtime at Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium. That wasn't a football game, friends. That was a blues song with a happy ending.

Verse one: the sad part. At halftime, we trailed 16-3. Early in the third, East Carolina made it 24-10. The crowd went quiet like a juke joint at closing time.

Verse two: the comeback. Marcus Stokes picked up his guitar. First, a 59-yard touchdown pass to Jermane Hayes. Then a 20-yarder to Jemyri Davis. Philippe Laforge kicked a field goal. Then Stokes hit Davis again from 4 yards out to tie it at 27, and with 3:31 left, he ran it in from 2 himself. Tigers 34, Pirates 27. The whole stadium was keeping time.

Verse three: the encore. East Carolina tied it with 1:30 left, which hurt like a broken string. But in overtime, Stokes found Davis for 20 yards, then ran in from the 5. East Carolina drove to our 4, and Ellis Ellis Jr. intercepted Mitch Griffis in the end zone. Curtain down, house lights up.

My hero is Marcus Stokes: 29 of 43 for 320 yards, three touchdown passes and two rushing touchdowns, all after halftime. Jemyri Davis caught seven passes for 91 yards and two scores. Ellis Ellis Jr. had the game-ending interception, and Chauncey Logan Jr. had another.

My affectionate goat: the first half. Three points, a punt-return fumble and some sour notes. Even B.B. King tuned up before the show, fellas.

What it means: Memphis is 6-2 and 3-1 in the American, and the bad taste from the Tulane loss is gone. We're right behind UTSA, North Texas and Army in the race. Beale Street is a national historic landmark, and on Thursday night it heard a real Memphis comeback.

Next up, Army comes to the Liberty Bowl on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 8 p.m. ET on ESPNU. Halloween night against the Black Knights. Get there early, fire up the smoker and bring your loudest Go Tigers Go.

articles.title: A Dispatch From the Front: The Minutemen Fall at East Hartford, 35-16, and the Streak of Losses Reaches Four
articles.byline: Abner Kettleworth, The Massachusetts Fanatic
articles.matchup: UConn 35, Massachusetts 16 (final), Fri. Oct. 23, Pratt & Whitney Stadium
articles.text:
Hear ye, hear ye, patriots of the Pioneer Valley. Abner Kettleworth here, tricorn hat askew, musket-shaped umbrella drooping and tea gone cold on the hearth. I bring grim news from the Connecticut front. UConn beat UMass 35-16 on Friday night at Pratt & Whitney Stadium, and this dispatch is written in a trembling hand.

The battle unfolded in three acts.

Act one: the early skirmish. Derek Morris kicked a 24-yard field goal, and for a few glorious minutes, UMass led 3-0. I composed a victory ode. I should not have.

Act two: the ambush. Late in the second quarter, UConn struck twice in 32 seconds. First, Kalieb Osborne threw a 20-yard touchdown pass to JD Willoughby. Then Cyncir Bowers ran 70 yards for another. Twenty-one to 3 at halftime. The redcoats themselves never moved that fast.

Act three: the blocked punt. In the third quarter, UConn blocked our punt, and Shamar Porter fell on it in the end zone. Twenty-eight to 3. A rout, friends, though our boys fought on. William Watson III threw a touchdown pass to Curtis Kimmons IV, and Justin Williams-Thomas ran one in late.

My hero is Joseph Griffin Jr., who caught four passes for 77 yards, including a 41-yard grab. William Watson III also threw for 205 yards and didn't commit a turnover.

My affectionate goat: third down. We converted two of 14. Even the Minutemen at Lexington had better luck holding a position. We also ran for just 53 yards and committed 10 penalties for 100 yards.

What it means: UMass is 4-4 and 1-3 in the MAC, and the losing streak has reached four after a 4-0 start. The campaign has stalled, but Amherst is the home of Emily Dickinson, and she knew a thing or two about hope. It's "the thing with feathers," patriots. Let's find some.

Next up, Ball State comes to McGuirk Alumni Stadium on Wednesday, Nov. 4. The kickoff time and TV are still to be announced. Onward, Minutemen. We regroup, we reload, and we march again.

articles.title: Fast Break, Helmets On: Osborne Scores Three Ways, Bowers Goes 70, and UConn Runs Away From UMass, 35-16
articles.byline: Jo Ferrante, The UConn Fanatic
articles.matchup: UConn 35, Massachusetts 16 (final), Fri. Oct. 23, Pratt & Whitney Stadium
articles.text:
Listen up, Husky Nation. Jo Ferrante here, still wearing my whistle from practice, still grinning from Friday night. UConn beat UMass 35-16 at Pratt & Whitney Stadium in front of 32,106 people. And if you tell me "nobody watches UConn football," I've got a stadium full of people who'd like a word.

Here's the game film.

Possession one: the two-minute flurry. Late in the second quarter, Kalieb Osborne threw a 20-yard touchdown pass to JD Willoughby. Thirty-two seconds later, Cyncir Bowers took a handoff 70 yards to the house. That's a fast break, folks. Get the stop, push the ball, finish at the rim. Twenty-one to 3 at halftime.

Possession two: the hustle play. In the third quarter, we blocked a UMass punt, and Shamar Porter scooped it up in the end zone. That's diving for a loose ball on the hardwood. Porter also caught a 5-yard touchdown pass in the first quarter. The man is everywhere.

Possession three: the dagger. Osborne ran it in from 13 yards out with 3:04 left. Thirty-five to 9. Ballgame.

My hero is Kalieb Osborne: 14 of 19 for 173 yards, two touchdown passes, a rushing touchdown and no turnovers. If my high school quarterbacks completed that many passes, I'd buy pizza for the whole team. Bowers ran for 131 yards on 15 carries. The run game piled up 265 yards.

My affectionate goat is the penalty flag. Eleven of them for 100 yards. Fellas, that's a lot of free throws for the other team. We also missed a 47-yard field goal. Coach Jo wants those back.

What it means: UConn is 4-3 with two straight wins, and the Huskies own New England bragging rights again. The stadium sits on Pratt & Whitney's old airfield, and the Huskies took flight on Friday night.

Next up, UConn visits Air Force at Falcon Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3 p.m. ET on MW+. Halloween at altitude. Push the pace, protect the ball, and stop the penalties, Huskies. Let's go to work.

articles.title: Mission Accomplished at the Gun: Kloska Blocks a Punt, Hellums Scores Three Times, and Dawson Jones Drills a 50-Yarder to Beat Tulsa, 38-35
articles.byline: Capt. (Ret.) Thaddeus Rourke, The Army Fanatic
articles.matchup: Army 38, Tulsa 35 (final), Fri. Oct. 23, H. A. Chapman Stadium
articles.text:
Attention on deck. Capt. Thaddeus Rourke, retired, reporting from my recliner in a state of high alert. My laminated clipboard has a dent in it, and that dent is the exact shape of my fist. Friday night at H. A. Chapman Stadium, Army beat Tulsa 38-35 on a 50-yard field goal as time expired. Field report follows.

Phase one: the setback. Tulsa scored three straight touchdowns, including a 59-yard run by Trequan Jones, and took a 35-28 lead early in the fourth quarter. Mission in jeopardy. My coffee went cold, against regulations.

Phase two: special operations. Tulsa missed a 40-yard field goal. Then, with 3:52 left, T. Kloska blocked a Tulsa punt and recovered it at the Tulsa 13. Five plays later, Cale Hellums pushed in from the 1 on third down. Thirty-five all. Hooah!

Phase three: the final objective. Our defense forced a three-and-out. Julian Porter broke up a pass, and K. Harris-Miller and J. Bousum sacked Baylor Hayes. Army got the ball back at our 37 with 45 seconds left and moved 27 yards in seven plays. Then Dawson Jones stepped up and hit a 50-yarder as the clock struck zero. Target neutralized.

My heroes: Dawson Jones went 3-for-3 on field goals, from 51, 34 and 50 yards. In a game decided by three points, that's the whole margin. Cale Hellums ran 30 times for 121 yards and three touchdowns. Godspower Nwawuihe ran 12 times for 135 yards, including a 66-yard touchdown. Kloska gets a medal for the block.

My affectionate goat: the run defense in the third quarter. We gave up two long touchdown runs in four minutes. Soldiers, we will be running drills.

What it means: Army is 5-2 and 4-1 in the American after three straight wins. Last year, Tulsa beat us by one point at West Point. This year, we returned the favor on their field. Michie Stadium has stood since 1924, and the Corps has been settling accounts much longer than that.

Next up, Army visits Memphis at Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 8 p.m. ET on ESPNU. Thank God for every man and woman who serves, and pack a jacket. Copy that, and beat Navy.

articles.title: Dry Well at the Buzzer: Tulsa Strikes Oil With a 35-28 Lead, Then Army Caps the Gusher With a Last-Second 50-Yarder, 38-35
articles.byline: Wiley Pettibone, The Tulsa Fanatic
articles.matchup: Army 38, Tulsa 35 (final), Fri. Oct. 23, H. A. Chapman Stadium
articles.text:
Howdy from the Oil Capital of the World. Wiley Pettibone here, petroleum geology grad, and the only man in Tulsa who reads a box score like a well log. Friday night's log at Chapman Stadium starts with a gusher and ends with a dry hole. Army beat Tulsa 38-35 on a 50-yard field goal as time expired.

Let me walk you through the core samples.

Sample one: the gusher. Down 28-14 in the third quarter, we struck oil. David Wells Jr. ran in from 11 yards out. Then Trequan Jones broke a 59-yard touchdown run. Early in the fourth, Baylor Hayes hit Jimmy Calloway for 13 yards and a touchdown. Thirty-five to 28, Tulsa. I was pricing derricks.

Sample two: the pressure drop. Owen Carey missed a 40-yard field goal that would've put us up 10. Then, with 3:52 left, Army blocked our punt and recovered it at our 13. Army tied it from the 1 with 1:50 left.

Sample three: the dry hole. We went three-and-out, with a broken-up pass and a sack. Army got the ball at its 37 with 45 seconds left, moved 27 yards, and Dawson Jones made a 50-yarder at the gun.

My hero is Jimmy Calloway, who caught 10 passes for 88 yards and a touchdown. Baylor Hayes went 23 of 34 for 262 yards and two touchdowns, and Javon Ross scored twice, one rushing and one receiving. Trequan Jones ran five times for 66 yards. That's high yield per barrel.

My affectionate goat: the punt team. A blocked punt with 3:52 left is a blowout preventer that blew out. We also gave up 275 rushing yards to Army, which, to be fair, is what Army does.

What it means: Tulsa is 4-4 and 1-3 in the American after its third loss in four games. That stings, especially after we won at West Point last season. But the Golden Driller has stood 76 feet tall since 1966, and he's seen plenty of dry wells before the next gusher.

Next up, Tulsa gets a week off, then visits Tulane at Yulman Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7. The kickoff time and TV are still to be announced. Wave at the Golden Driller on your way out of town. He can wait one more week for a win.

articles.title: Mission Grade: Scrubbed. Three Lost Fumbles Ground the Falcons in Laramie, 28-14
articles.byline: Lt. Col. (Ret.) Marissa Okonkwo-Hale, The Air Force Fanatic
articles.matchup: Wyoming 28, Air Force 14 (final), Fri. Oct. 23, War Memorial Stadium
articles.text:
Good morning, wingmen. Lt. Col. Marissa Okonkwo-Hale, retired, reporting from the lawn chair with a thermos of coffee and a clipboard full of red ink. Before kickoff, I gave Wyoming the call sign "Summit," because War Memorial Stadium sits at 7,222 feet, the highest in FBS. On Friday night, Wyoming beat Air Force 28-14, and our offense ran out of oxygen.

Debrief, in three parts.

Part one: the launch failure. On Wyoming's second play from scrimmage, Tyler Hughes ran 68 yards for a touchdown. Then, on our first drive, Evan Medders fumbled, and Wyoming recovered at our 44.

Part two: the halftime deficit. Hughes threw touchdown passes to Jake Wilson and Samuel Harris, the second with 38 seconds left in the half. We trailed 21-6 despite moving the ball. Medders cut it to 21-14 in the third with a 5-yard touchdown pass to Grant Wayne and a two-point run of his own.

Part three: the fumbles. Early in the fourth, we drove to the Wyoming 14, and the ball came loose. Wyoming recovered. Four minutes later, we fumbled again near midfield, and Wyoming drove 49 yards for the clinching touchdown. Three lost fumbles, wingmen. In my day, losing equipment meant paperwork.

My hero is Evan Medders: 21 carries, 115 yards, a touchdown pass and a two-point run. The offense ran 63 times for 304 yards and held the ball for 37:45. Carter Cremascoli went 2-for-2 on field goals.

My affectionate goat: ball security. We outgained Wyoming 387 to 301 and lost by 14. That's a mission that reached the target, then forgot to release the payload.

What it means: Air Force is 5-2 and 3-2 in the Mountain West, two losses behind league-unbeaten New Mexico and still chasing. The streak of four straight wins is over. Colorado Springs sits at 6,035 feet, which is lower than Laramie, and I'm happy to be home.

Next up, UConn comes to Falcon Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3 p.m. ET on MW+. Call sign: "Fast Break." Hold on to the football, Falcons. Call sign: correct.

articles.title: Yep. Tyler Hughes Goes 68 Yards on Play Two, the Defense Takes the Ball Three Times, and Wyoming Grounds Air Force, 28-14
articles.byline: Colter Sprague, The Wyoming Fanatic
articles.matchup: Wyoming 28, Air Force 14 (final), Fri. Oct. 23, War Memorial Stadium
articles.text:
Colter Sprague. Laramie. Friday night, Wyoming beat Air Force 28-14 at War Memorial Stadium. Yep.

My editor says that's not enough. Pull up a hay bale.

Second play of the game. Tyler Hughes kept it and ran 68 yards for a touchdown. Seven-nothing, 50 seconds in. I spilled my coffee. Didn't mind.

Second, the turnovers. Air Force runs the ball like a cattle drive: slow, steady, all day. They ran 63 times for 304 yards and held it for over 37 minutes. But E. Bogar recovered two fumbles, including one early in the fourth after G. Rutherford knocked it loose at our 14. Air Force was driving to tie it. Didn't happen. Yep.

Third, the clincher. About four minutes later, J. Redfern forced another fumble, and S. Perez fell on it at midfield. We drove 49 yards in eight plays, and Markell Holman scored from the 1 with 3:04 left. Twenty-eight to 14. I said "yep" twice.

My hero is Tyler Hughes. He ran 12 times for 146 yards and a touchdown, and threw touchdown passes to Jake Wilson and Samuel Harris. Ran like an antelope crossing Highway 287. Bogar gets a nod. Two fumble recoveries.

My affectionate goat is our kicker, Erik Sandvik. Missed a 38-yarder. It happens. Air at 7,222 feet is light. Ball goes where it wants.

What it means: Wyoming is 5-3 and 4-1 in the Mountain West, one game behind New Mexico. Three straight wins. And we did it against Air Force, at the highest stadium in FBS. In 1870, Laramie put the first women in the world on a jury. This town has been doing big things quietly for a long time.

Next up, Wyoming gets a week off, then visits UNLV at Allegiant Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7, at 10:30 p.m. ET on CBSSN. Late kickoff. Bring coffee.

That's about all I've got. Yep.

articles.title: Peer Review Rejected: Gael Ochoa Runs for 259 Yards and Five Touchdowns, but FAU Survives the Owl-on-Owl Shootout, 51-49
articles.byline: Odalys Chen-Moreau, The Rice Fanatic
articles.matchup: Florida Atlantic 51, Rice 49 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Flagler Credit Union Stadium
articles.text:
Good morning from the live oaks. Odalys Chen-Moreau here, bioengineering Ph.D., stats-cop badge on the lanyard, and a lab notebook that now contains the words "WHAT" and "HOW" in very large letters. Saturday in Boca Raton, Florida Atlantic beat Rice 51-49. Both teams are the Owls. Only one is the real Owls. The scoreboard disagreed with me.

Here's my lab report.

Observation one: Gael Ochoa is a statistical outlier. He ran 12 times for 259 yards and four touchdowns, from 55, 52, 74 and 69 yards. He also threw a 71-yard touchdown pass to Braylen Walker. That's 21.6 yards per carry. In a clinical trial, I'd ask for a second sample. In football, I'd just ask for more carries.

Observation two: the control group failed. FAU scored seven touchdowns, and Easton Messer was involved in five of them, including an 82-yard punt return with 3:37 left that made it 51-42. Our punt coverage has been placed on academic probation.

Observation three: the final experiment. Ochoa's touchdown pass to Walker cut it to 51-49 with 2:51 left. Our defense forced a three-and-out. We got the ball back at our 31 with two minutes left and moved to the FAU 37. Then Tommy Bauchiero's 55-yard field goal missed with 45 seconds left. Hypothesis: rejected.

My hero is Gael Ochoa, obviously. Max Mosey also ran for a 41-yard touchdown, and Tyvonn Byars added 93 rushing yards. Rice ran for 499 yards and gained 608 in all. Kyren Condoll had an interception.

My affectionate goat: the defense. We gave up 51 points and 339 passing yards to Caden Veltkamp. Peer review would call that a methods problem.

What it means: Rice is 1-7 and 0-4 in the American, and the losing streak is at seven. Two of those losses came by a combined four points, and this offense just showed it can score with anyone. JFK gave his Moon speech in Rice Stadium in 1962. We choose to do these things not because they are easy. Clearly.

Next up, Rice gets a week off, then visits North Texas at DATCU Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7. Kickoff and TV are still to be announced. Go Owls. The real ones.

articles.title: Easton Messer Rides Five Waves: Two Catches, Two Runs and an 82-Yard Punt Return Carry FAU Past Rice, 51-49
articles.byline: Kaia Brightwater, The Florida Atlantic Fanatic
articles.matchup: Florida Atlantic 51, Rice 49 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Flagler Credit Union Stadium
articles.text:
Hey, babe. Kaia Brightwater here, sunglasses on, salt in my hair and my heart rate still recovering from Saturday in Boca Raton. FAU beat Rice 51-49 at Flagler Credit Union Stadium. Owls versus Owls. Nine touchdowns of 30 yards or more. That wasn't a football game, babe. That was a hurricane swell.

Here are the waves that decided it.

Wave one: the comeback set. Rice hit us with touchdown runs of 55 and 52 yards and led 14-0 in the first quarter. Pure closeout. Then Caden Veltkamp found Branden Hoch for 30 yards, the defense got a safety, and Easton Messer scored twice. Twenty-three to 14. Clean surf, babe.

Wave two: the punt return. It was 44-42 with 3:37 left. Rice punted, and Easton Messer caught it and ran 82 yards for a touchdown. That's paddling into a monster wave, popping up and riding it all the way to the sand.

Wave three: the wipeout that wasn't. Rice scored to make it 51-49. We went three-and-out. Rice drove to our 37, and their 55-yard field goal missed with 45 seconds left. Then we knelt twice and paddled in.

My hero is Easton Messer, obviously. Twelve catches for 162 yards and two touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns and the punt-return touchdown. Five touchdowns, babe. Caden Veltkamp completed 29 of 37 passes for 339 yards and three touchdowns. A. Ware forced and recovered a fumble.

My affectionate goat: the run defense. Rice ran for 499 yards, and Gael Ochoa ran for 259 on 12 carries. Babe, that's a riptide. We need to talk about tackling.

What it means: FAU is 5-2 and 2-1 in the American, still in the race. Boca Raton is the birthplace of IBM's first personal computer, and our offense is running on the latest software.

Next up, FAU visits North Texas at DATCU Stadium on Thursday, Oct. 29, at 7:30 p.m. ET on ESPN. North Texas is 3-0 in the league, so this is a big swell. Wax the board. Surf's up on tempo, babe.

articles.title: Short Stack, Cold Syrup: The Broncos Rally From 17 Down to Tie Toledo, Then Fall at the Glass Bowl, 45-38
articles.byline: Corwin Dahlquist, The Western Michigan Fanatic
articles.matchup: Toledo 45, Western Michigan 38 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Glass Bowl
articles.text:
Good morning, Broncos. Corwin Dahlquist here, at my usual Kalamazoo diner booth, with a syrup bottle, a pencil and a placemat full of arrows that go nowhere. Saturday at the Glass Bowl, Toledo beat Western Michigan 45-38. Our first MAC loss. The waitress brought me a refill without asking. She knew.

Here's how breakfast went.

The burnt first batch: Toledo jumped out to a 17-0 lead and led 31-14 at halftime. Our defense gave up 595 yards on the day. Pancakes that flat belong on the floor.

The fresh batch: to start the second half, Joshua Franklin returned the kickoff 92 yards for a touchdown. I hit the table so hard the creamer jumped. Broc Lowry ran one in from the 2. After Toledo scored, Lowry threw a 41-yard touchdown pass to Baylin Brooks. Then Dieter Kelly kicked a 23-yard field goal with 9:19 left. Thirty-eight all! A full stack with butter and blueberries!

The cold syrup: Toledo's CJ Miller ran 11 yards for a touchdown with 4:23 left. We got the ball back at our 23 with 1:46 left, but Israel Petite intercepted Lowry at our 48. Toledo knelt it out. Check, please.

My hero is Joshua Franklin, who returned a kickoff for a touchdown and recovered a fumble. Aveion Chenault caught six passes for 105 yards and a touchdown, including a 49-yarder. And the comeback from 17 down showed real guts. That sticks to your ribs.

My affectionate goat: the run defense. CJ Miller carried 33 times for 183 yards. That's a man eating the whole buffet. Lowry also threw two interceptions, and we went 3-for-12 on third down.

What it means: Western Michigan is 5-3 and 3-1 in the MAC, one game behind Ohio. Still in the hunt. Kalamazoo built the country's first outdoor pedestrian mall in 1959. This town knows how to keep walking forward.

Next up, Bowling Green comes to Waldo Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at noon ET on CBSSN. Halloween brunch at home. Row the boat, Broncos. Next week, we order the full stack.

articles.title: Bald Tires on the Wagon Wheel: Jordan Gant Runs for 162, but 15 Penalties and a Late Collapse Send Akron Home Empty, 35-20
articles.byline: Hollister 'Zip' Grubbs, The Akron Fanatic
articles.matchup: Kent State 35, Akron 20 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Zoeller Field at Dix Stadium
articles.text:
Greetings from the lab, Zips fans. Hollister "Zip" Grubbs here, tread-depth gauge in my pocket and a heavy heart in my chest. Saturday at Dix Stadium, Kent State beat Akron 35-20, and the Wagon Wheel stays in Kent. Legend says John R. Buchtel's wagon got stuck in the mud right where Kent State sits today. On Saturday, the Zips got stuck there too.

Here's my inspection report.

Good tread: we led for most of the day. Jordan Gant scored on runs of 6 and 5 yards, and Aidan Stire kicked a 40-yard field goal for a 17-14 lead late in the third quarter. Gant carried 28 times for 162 yards. That's premium all-season rubber.

The blowout: Kent State answered with a 52-yard catch and a 2-yard touchdown pass to retake the lead, 21-17. Early in the fourth, we had a chance to go ahead, but Norey Johnson intercepted Brayden Roggow at the Kent 15 and returned it 37 yards.

The flat: down 21-17 with about 7:40 left, we tried a fourth-down fake at our own 22 and came up short. Three plays later, Wayne Harris caught a 19-yard touchdown pass. Kent then got the ball back at our 13, and Dru DeShields ran it in. Four minutes, 14 points, and the wheels came off.

My hero is Jordan Gant. Kyan Mason also caught seven passes for 129 yards, and Stire hit a 50-yarder late. Our offense outgained Kent, 422 yards to 376, and held the ball for 34 minutes.

My affectionate goat: the penalty flag. Fifteen penalties for 165 yards. That's not a tire problem, friends, that's an alignment problem. Get it to the shop.

What it means: Akron is 1-7 and 0-4 in the MAC, with six straight losses. It's a bald season. But Akron is the Rubber Capital of the World, and it has hosted the All-American Soap Box Derby since 1936. We know a thing or two about rolling downhill and climbing back up.

Next up, Ohio comes to InfoCision Stadium on Tuesday, Nov. 3, at 7 p.m. ET. Ohio is 4-0 in the MAC, so check the pressure, Zips. Check the tread, too.

articles.title: I Expected This (Honestly, I Didn't): Dru DeShields Throws Four Touchdowns, Wayne Harris Catches Three, and the Wagon Wheel Stays in Kent
articles.byline: Ozzie Brannigan, The Kent State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Kent State 35, Akron 20 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Zoeller Field at Dix Stadium
articles.text:
Hello. It's Ozzie Brannigan, on my bench near Brady's Leap. Saturday at Dix Stadium, Kent State beat Akron 35-20 and kept the Wagon Wheel. I expected this. I always expect this. That's not entirely true. After last week's 29-2 loss, I expected a blizzard of sadness. Instead, we scored 35 points. I've adjusted my scarf to an 8 out of 10.

Here's what happened, as calmly as I can manage.

First, the comeback. We trailed 7-0, 14-7 and 17-14. Each time, Dru DeShields answered. He hit Wayne Harris for a 1-yard touchdown before halftime, then for 55 yards in the third. Then Brandon White caught a 52-yard pass, and Hunter Hopperton caught a 2-yard touchdown. Twenty-one to 17, Flashes. I expected... no. I didn't.

Second, the interception. Early in the fourth, Akron was driving to take the lead. Norey Johnson intercepted Brayden Roggow at our 15 and ran it back 37 yards. I stood up. Nobody on my bench stood up. I'm usually alone on my bench.

Third, the knockout. Akron tried a fourth-down fake at its own 22 and came up short. Three plays later, DeShields hit Harris for a 19-yard touchdown. Then we got the ball right back at the Akron 13, and DeShields ran it in himself. Thirty-five to 17. That's 14 points in about two minutes. Good.

My hero is Dru DeShields: 294 passing yards, four touchdown passes, a rushing touchdown and no turnovers. Wayne Harris caught nine passes for 156 yards and three scores. We also committed only three penalties.

My affectionate goat: the run defense, which let Jordan Gant run for 162 yards. Also Tommy Newcomb's missed 32-yard field goal. I expected that one. Sorry, Tommy.

What it means: Kent State is 3-5 and 2-2 in the MAC, and we've won the Wagon Wheel two years running. Kent is called the Tree City, and this team just grew a new branch.

Next up, Kent State visits Sacramento State at Hornet Stadium on Friday, Oct. 30, at 10:30 p.m. ET on ESPN2. Do I think we'll win? I expected you to ask that. Here's the honest answer: I'm staying up to find out.

articles.title: Darlings, What a Finish: D'Shawntae Jones Scores With 1:41 Left, and Miami Steals One in Mount Pleasant, 28-27
articles.byline: Cordelia Van Doren, The Miami (OH) Fanatic
articles.matchup: Miami (OH) 28, Central Michigan 27 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Kelly/Shorts Stadium
articles.text:
Hello, darlings. Cordelia Van Doren here, back on my bench in Uptown Oxford, tea gone cold, red scarf wrapped twice around my neck for emotional support. Saturday at Kelly/Shorts Stadium, Miami beat Central Michigan 28-27. One point, darlings. I aged a decade, and I'm wearing it beautifully.

Here's the drama in three acts.

Act one: the plot twist. Early in the third, Justin Taylor intercepted Caleb Heavner and returned it 46 yards for a touchdown. Central Michigan led 17-14. I clutched my pearls so hard one popped off. Heavner answered with a 27-yard touchdown run. Very Cradle of Coaches of him.

Act two: the deficit. Central Michigan scored a touchdown and a field goal, and with 4:17 left, we trailed 27-21. I put my tea down. Things were serious.

Act three: the triumph. Our offense drove 75 yards in eight plays. Heavner threw a 27-yard pass to Maleek Huggins at the CMU 10. Then the Chippewas were flagged for pass interference twice in a row, and D'Shawntae Jones bulled in from the 2 with 1:41 left. Twenty-eight to 27. Then our defense held on downs, Jones picked up a first down, and we knelt. Curtain. Roses. Bows.

My hero is Maleek Huggins: seven catches for 122 yards, including the big one on the winning drive. Heavner ran for a touchdown and threw for 221 yards. Roosevelt Andrews III had a sack and a half.

My affectionate goat: interceptions. Heavner threw two, and one went the other way for a touchdown. Caleb, darling, we pass to the red jerseys. It's in the brochure.

What it means: Miami is 5-3 and 3-1 in the MAC after three straight wins, one game behind Ohio. And we've now beaten Central Michigan six straight times. Paul Brown, Woody Hayes, Bo Schembechler, Ara Parseghian and Sean McVay all came through Miami. Saturday, we saw why this place makes winners.

Next up, Buffalo comes to Yager Stadium on Tuesday, Nov. 3, at 7 p.m. ET. A Tuesday night, darlings. Bring a blanket and your best red. Ta-ta, darlings. Love and Hawks.

articles.title: Tags Filled, Heart Broken: Four Sacks and an Interception Return Aren't Enough as Miami Steals One From CMU, 28-27
articles.byline: Brynn Haverkamp, The Central Michigan Fanatic
articles.matchup: Miami (OH) 28, Central Michigan 27 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Kelly/Shorts Stadium
articles.text:
Hey there, Chippewas. Brynn Haverkamp here, blaze-orange beanie on, and four sack tags filled on the kitchen table. Usually that's a happy week at my house. Saturday at Kelly/Shorts Stadium, Miami beat Central Michigan 28-27, and I'm sitting in the deer stand of sadness.

Here's what happened.

First, the big hunt. Early in the third, Justin Taylor intercepted Caleb Heavner and returned it 46 yards for a touchdown. Seventeen to 14, Chips. Ope, interception! Then, late in the third, Jadyn Glasser hit Langston Lewis for a 9-yard touchdown, and with 4:17 left, Caden VanHuis kicked a 22-yard field goal. Central Michigan 27, Miami 21. I started loading the snowmobile for a victory lap.

Second, the miss. Miami drove 75 yards in eight plays. We were flagged for pass interference twice in a row near the goal line, and D'Shawntae Jones scored from the 2 with 1:41 left. Twenty-eight to 27. Ope.

Third, the last chance. A holding penalty wiped out Glasser's 21-yard run, and our fourth-down pass fell incomplete with 53 seconds left. Season's over on that trail.

My hero is Langston Lewis: 10 catches for 163 yards and a touchdown, including a 47-yarder. Justin Taylor scored on the interception return, and Brett McCalla had another interception. Our defense filled four sack tags, with JJ Douglas, Antonio Cherry Jr. and Nathan VanTimmeren each getting one. Glasser threw for 221 yards without a turnover.

My affectionate goat: the penalty flags. Ten of them for 83 yards, including two on the winning drive. You can't shoot before legal hunting hours, fellas.

What it means: Central Michigan is 3-5 and 1-3 in the MAC after three straight losses, two of them by a touchdown or less. That stings. But Mount Pleasant struck oil in 1928, so this town knows good things are buried underneath.

Next up, Central Michigan faces Eastern Michigan at Ford Field on Wednesday, Nov. 4. Kickoff time and TV are still to be announced. Ope, sack. Fire up, Chips.

articles.title: Too Many Shots on Goal: Messiah Burch Runs for 184 and Three Scores, and Bowling Green Falls at Buffalo, 31-24
articles.byline: Darcy Fenwick, The Bowling Green Fanatic
articles.matchup: Buffalo 31, Bowling Green 24 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Broadview Stadium
articles.text:
Darcy Fenwick here, former club goalie, and the only person in Wood County who grades run defense by how many times I yelled "Skate back!" at the TV. On Saturday at Broadview Stadium, Buffalo beat Bowling Green 31-24. I yelled a lot.

Honestly, our net-minding was fine through the air. Jason Wright threw 21 passes and only completed 13, so that's eight saves. The problem is that Buffalo didn't need to shoot. They skated it straight in.

Here's the game tape.

The good period: Jay Kastantin threw three touchdown passes, including an 18-yarder to Isaiah Dawson, a 40-yarder to Trey Johnson and a 13-yarder to Nakai Amachree. We led 14-7 and 21-14. Myles Bradley sacked Wright and forced a fumble that E. George recovered. That's a big glove save.

The breakaway: tied 21-21, Buffalo kicked a field goal on the first play of the fourth. Then Messiah Burch broke a 73-yard touchdown run. Thirty-one to 21. That's a breakaway, folks, and nobody was back.

The pulled goalie: Kastantin threw an interception on the next drive, but Buffalo missed a 47-yard field goal. We drove for a Travis Kenner field goal, and then our defense stopped Buffalo on downs at our 38 with 1:02 left. We got to the Buffalo 39 when time ran out. So close. That's hitting the post at the buzzer.

My hero is Kastantin: 19 of 27 for 217 yards and three touchdowns. Our offense also held the ball for almost 36 minutes.

My affectionate goat: the run defense. Burch ran 33 times for 184 yards, and Buffalo ran for 251. You can't stop pucks you never see coming.

What it means: Bowling Green is 2-6 and 2-2 in the MAC, after two losses in a row by a combined eight points. Bowling Green sits on land that used to be the Great Black Swamp, and right now, this season feels pretty swampy. But we drained that swamp once. We'll do it again.

Next up, Bowling Green visits Western Michigan at Waldo Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at noon ET on CBSSN. Halloween at Waldo. Wear a mask, and maybe a cup. Lace 'em up, Falcons.

articles.matchup: Buffalo 31, Bowling Green 24 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Broadview Stadium
articles.text:
Good morning, Western New York. Kendra Woolcott with your Bulls weather report. Current conditions: 5-3, 3-1 in the MAC, three straight wins, and a warm front parked over Broadview Stadium. On Saturday, Buffalo beat Bowling Green 31-24. Today's forecast: smiles, with scattered high-fives.

Here's the radar.

Morning showers: Bowling Green's Jay Kastantin threw three touchdown passes, and we trailed 14-7 and 21-14. I had the umbrella out. But Jason Wright ran 39 yards to set up his own 14-yard touchdown pass to Clint Walker just before halftime, and Messiah Burch's 2-yard run tied it at 21 in the third.

Afternoon clearing: Oliver Hautanen kicked a 31-yard field goal on the first play of the fourth quarter. Then, at 12:18, Burch broke through the middle and ran 73 yards for a touchdown. Thirty-one to 21. That's what meteorologists call a high-pressure system.

Evening calm: Miles Greer intercepted Kastantin at the BG 40 on the next drive. Sedrick Vessah had another interception in the third quarter. Bowling Green kicked a late field goal, and our final drive was stopped on downs, but they ran out of time at our 39.

My hero is Messiah Burch, who ran 33 times for a career-high 184 yards and three touchdowns. Will Clark had a sack and a half, too.

And get this: Buffalo had zero penalties. None. Not one flag all afternoon. That's a clear sky, folks.

My affectionate goat: the end of the game. Up a touchdown with about two minutes left, we didn't get the first down, and Bowling Green got the ball back. A little late-day turbulence. Next time, let's land the plane.

What it means: Buffalo is 5-3 and 3-1 in the MAC, part of a three-way tie for second, one game behind Ohio. Buffalo was the end of the Erie Canal in 1825. This team keeps going farther than that.

Next up, Buffalo visits Miami at Yager Stadium on Tuesday, Nov. 3, at 7 p.m. ET. A November night in Oxford. Stay warm, Bulls fans. Bring a thermos, bring a friend, bring the whole family, and bring your loudest voice, because this team has earned a crowd that sounds like it believes.

articles.title: Worth Setting the Alarm For: Micah Alejado Throws Three Touchdowns, DeVon Rice Runs for Three, and Hawai'i Rolls in DeKalb, 56-21
articles.byline: Kainoa Akana-Baird, The Hawai'i Fanatic
articles.matchup: Hawai'i 56, Northern Illinois 21 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Huskie Stadium
articles.text:
Aloha kakou. Kainoa Akana-Baird here, on the lanai with a plate lunch and a whiteboard full of time-zone math. Saturday's kickoff in DeKalb was 9:30 a.m. in Honolulu. By the time I'd finished my second cup of coffee, Hawai'i had beaten Northern Illinois 56-21. Best breakfast of the year.

Here's how the morning went.

First, the swell builds. The game was tied 14-14 early in the second quarter. Then DeVon Rice broke a 33-yard touchdown run, and the waves started rolling. Micah Alejado hit Cam Barfield on a 62-yard catch-and-run to the NIU 3, and Barfield punched it in from the 1 soon after. After Jeremiah Hughes intercepted Taron Dickens, Alejado found Audric Harris for 44 yards and then Frank Abreu for a 12-yard touchdown with 23 seconds left in the half. Thirty-five to 14.

Second, the wave doesn't stop. Elijah Palmer recovered a fumble early in the third, and Rice scored again from the 5. Then Alejado hit Josiah Fetui for a 44-yard touchdown. That made it 35 straight points. Shaka, brah.

Third, the clean finish. Kydel Stone intercepted Dickens late, and TJ Fo'ilefutu added a 6-yard touchdown. Northern Illinois turned it over five times.

My hero is Micah Alejado, who threw for 323 yards and three touchdowns. DeVon Rice ran for three scores, and Frank Abreu caught two touchdown passes.

My affectionate goat: Alejado's fourth-quarter interception. Brah, we were up 35. You can take the rest of the morning off.

What it means: Hawai'i is 2-6 and 1-4 in the Mountain West, and it snapped a four-game losing streak. We scored 56 points, which is more than our previous two games combined. Hawai'i is the westernmost state, but on Saturday, the Rainbow Warriors made themselves right at home in the Midwest.

Next up, Hawai'i visits UTEP at the Sun Bowl on Saturday, Nov. 7. Kickoff time and TV are still to be announced, so the whiteboard is ready and the marker is uncapped. Island time, but on schedule.

articles.title: Rough Harvest: DeAree Rogers Catches Two Touchdowns, but Five Turnovers Bury Northern Illinois Against Hawai'i, 56-21
articles.byline: Nola Brandvik, The Northern Illinois Fanatic
articles.matchup: Hawai'i 56, Northern Illinois 21 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Huskie Stadium
articles.text:
Hi there, Huskie fans. Nola Brandvik here, on the tailgate of my pickup outside DeKalb, watching the combines finish the bean fields. Everybody around here is bringing in a crop. On Saturday at Huskie Stadium, Hawai'i harvested ours. The Rainbow Warriors beat Northern Illinois 56-21.

I'm not going to sugarcoat it. Hawai'i flew across an ocean and played like it was a home game.

Here's how it went.

First, the good seed. Taron Dickens hit DeAree Rogers for a 49-yard touchdown in the first quarter and a 25-yard touchdown early in the second. Fourteen to 14. I said, "Maybe this is the year." I always say that in October.

Second, the hailstorm. Hawai'i scored the next 35 points. DeVon Rice ran 33 yards for a touchdown. Cam Barfield took a short pass 62 yards. Then Jeremiah Hughes intercepted Dickens late in the half, and Hawai'i scored again with 23 seconds left. By halftime, it was 35-14. Early in the third, Telly Johnson Jr. fumbled after a 12-yard run, and Rice scored from the 5.

Third, the stubble. Elijah Porter ran in a 3-yard touchdown in the fourth, and Yassine Falke intercepted Micah Alejado. Good for them. Those are the little things you gather off the field after the combine goes through.

My hero is DeAree Rogers: eight catches, 115 yards and two touchdowns. Dickens threw for 171 yards and two scores, and Johnson ran for 63 yards.

My affectionate goat: ball security. Five turnovers, fellas. Joseph Glidden patented barbed wire here in 1874. Hold on to the ball like you're holding barbed wire... wait, no. Hold on to it tighter than that.

What it means: Northern Illinois is 0-7 and 0-3 in the Mountain West. It's a rough year in the field. But DeKalb hybrid corn was once planted by more farmers than any other brand, so this town knows how to grow something.

Next up, Northern Illinois visits UNLV at Allegiant Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 10:30 p.m. ET on CBSSN. Halloween in the desert. Lights, costumes and maybe a first win. Knee-high by the Fourth of July. A win by the end of October.

articles.title: Seven-Eight Time in Annapolis: Justin Stevenson Catches 209 Yards, Jahiem White Seals It, and North Texas Outlasts Navy, 49-39
articles.byline: Grady Mayhew-Ochoa, The North Texas Fanatic
articles.matchup: North Texas 49, Navy 39 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium
articles.text:
Mean Green, baby. Grady Mayhew-Ochoa here, sticks in my back pocket and my heart still doing a drum solo. Saturday at Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium, North Texas beat Navy 49-39. That wasn't a football game. That was a 60-minute jam session where both bands refused to stop playing.

Here's the setlist.

Track one, the big hits. Tayven Jackson found Justin Stevenson for a 45-yard touchdown on our first drive and a 53-yarder in the third. Stevenson caught eight passes for 209 yards. That's a solo, baby. Crash cymbal on every catch.

Track two, the special guests. Dalton Carnes returned a punt 76 yards for a touchdown in the second quarter. Then, in the third, Zakye Barker scooped up a Navy fumble and ran 63 yards for another score. When your defense and special teams both take a solo, you know the band is cooking.

Track three, the closer. Navy kept coming, and after Michael Barrow's 4-yard run with 10:49 left, it was 42-39. My hi-hat was shaking. On our very next drive, Jahiem White ran 59 yards to the end zone. Forty-nine to 39. Then we held the ball for the final 6:32 with a 12-play drive. That's a fade-out, baby. The crowd goes home.

My hero is Justin Stevenson, but Jahiem White deserves an encore: 174 rushing yards, two touchdowns and four catches. Jackson threw for 305 yards and three touchdowns on 17-of-23 passing.

My affectionate goat: the run defense. Navy ran 65 times for 363 yards. Jackson Gutierrez alone ran for 228. My drummer brain needs a nap.

What it means: North Texas is 5-2 and 3-0 in the American after four straight wins. Denton's College of Music was the first school to offer a jazz studies degree, and Saturday, this team played like it graduated with honors.

Next up, Florida Atlantic comes to DATCU Stadium on Thursday, Oct. 29, at 7:30 p.m. ET on ESPN. Thursday night, national TV, home crowd. Count it off. Seven-eight time, baby.

articles.title: Logbook Entry: 506 Yards, 228 From Jackson Gutierrez, and a Comeback That Fell Three Points Short as North Texas Beats Navy, 49-39
articles.byline: Cmdr. (Ret.) Annabel Merriweather, The Navy Fanatic
articles.matchup: North Texas 49, Navy 39 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium
articles.text:
Good morning, shipmates. Commander Annabel Merriweather, retired, reporting from the seawall in Annapolis. I've been keeping my logbook for a long time, and I'll record Saturday honestly: North Texas beat Navy 49-39 at Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium. We ran for 363 yards and still lost. The logbook has a few water stains this morning.

Entry one: the leaks. Our defense couldn't stop the deep passes. Justin Stevenson caught 209 yards worth of them. Worse, two special-teams plays sank us. A fumbled snap led to a punt, and Dalton Carnes returned it 76 yards for a touchdown, and Zakye Barker returned a fumble 63 yards for a touchdown in the third.

Entry two: the counterattack. Jackson Gutierrez ran for an 18-yard touchdown, a 1-yarder and a 43-yarder, then threw a two-point conversion pass to Jake Norris. Irabonoise Oniha intercepted Tayven Jackson, and Gutierrez hit Michael Barrow for a 15-yard touchdown pass late in the third. Barrow ran in from the 4 early in the fourth. Forty-two to 39. I was on my feet on the seawall. Full speed ahead.

Entry three: the torpedo. On North Texas' very next drive, Jahiem White ran 59 yards for a touchdown. Then they held the ball for the last 6:32. We never got it back.

My hero is Jackson Gutierrez: 26 carries, 228 yards, three rushing touchdowns and a touchdown pass. Barrow ran for 92 yards and scored twice, and the team committed only one penalty all day. That's a disciplined crew.

My affectionate goat: the deep pass defense, which let Stevenson catch passes of 45, 46 and 53 yards. Fellas, we need more sailors in the deep water.

What it means: Navy is 2-5 and 1-4 in the American, with two straight losses in shootouts. George Washington resigned his commission in Annapolis, but this team doesn't quit.

Next up, Navy plays Notre Dame at Gillette Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at noon ET on ABC. One of college football's oldest series, on Halloween, on national TV. Brace for heavy seas. Steady as she goes.

articles.title: Overcooked in Muncie: Jace Wilson's 65-Yard Score and Boogsie Silvera's Two Interceptions Can't Save the Dish as Ball State Wins, 34-17
articles.byline: Mateo Villaseñor, The Sacramento State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Ball State 34, Sacramento State 17 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Scheumann Stadium
articles.text:
Welcome to the kitchen, Hornets. Mateo Villaseñor here, apron on, smoke alarm going off. On Saturday at Scheumann Stadium, Ball State beat Sacramento State 34-17. We had good ingredients. We left it in the oven a little too long.

Here's tonight's recipe review.

The appetizer was delicious. Grant Meadors kicked a 47-yard field goal, and after Ball State answered, Jackson Sharman threw a 65-yard touchdown pass to Jace Wilson. Ten to 7, Hornets. Chef's kiss.

The main course burned. Less than a minute after Wilson's score, Keldric Luster hit Jamarion McDougle for 55 yards and a touchdown. Then, with 38 seconds left in the half, Sharman was sacked and fumbled at our 26. TJ Horton scored a 1-yard touchdown. Twenty to 10 at halftime. Luster ran for another score early in the third. That's a kitchen fire, chefs.

The dessert was worth saving. Boogsie Silvera intercepted Luster twice. The second came at the goal line late in the third, and he returned it 24 yards. Sharman also threw a 4-yard touchdown pass to Matt Coleman. That's how you save a dish.

My hero is Boogsie Silvera: two interceptions and 11 tackles. Sharman threw for 187 yards and two touchdowns without an interception. Hamish Adams also punted six times for a 45.3-yard average.

My affectionate goat: the run game. We ran 27 times for 54 yards. That's not a recipe, friends. That's a garnish.

What it means: Sacramento State is 1-7 and 0-5 in its first season in the MAC. It's a hard first year in FBS. But Sacramento is America's Farm-to-Fork Capital. We know good food takes time to grow.

Next up, Kent State comes to Hornet Stadium on Friday, Oct. 30, at 10:30 p.m. ET on ESPN2. Friday night lights, home cooking and a national TV audience. Preheat the oven. Plate it up, Hornets.

articles.title: Four Punts, Four Dad Jokes, One Big Win: Keldric Luster Accounts for Three Touchdowns as Ball State Beats Sac State, 34-17
articles.byline: Gus Ponder, The Ball State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Ball State 34, Sacramento State 17 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Scheumann Stadium
articles.text:
Gus Ponder here, coming to you from the garage, where the whiteboard is full of arrows and the punt chart says four. On Saturday at Scheumann Stadium, Ball State beat Sacramento State 34-17. That's two wins in a row, folks. I'm so happy I alphabetized my socket set.

Rules are rules, though. Four punts, four dad jokes. Here we go.

Joke one: Why did the Cardinal sit in the garage? He was waiting for a big play. Well, he didn't have to wait long. Down 3-0 in the second, Keldric Luster threw a 65-yard touchdown pass to Isaiah Thacker.
