articles.title: Thirteen Seconds of Heartbreak: A 98-Yard Drive Puts EMU Ahead, a 100-Yard Kickoff Return Takes It Away, and Ohio Wins, 24-20
articles.byline: Imogen Tremblay, The Eastern Michigan Fanatic
articles.matchup: Ohio 24, Eastern Michigan 20 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Peden Stadium
articles.text:
Hi, everybody. Imogen Tremblay here, at my corner table in Depot Town, with a coffee that went cold around 3:53 left in the fourth quarter. On Saturday at Peden Stadium, Ohio beat Eastern Michigan 24-20. We led at halftime, and we led with 3:40 left. Then we didn't.

Here's how it went.

First, the scrappy start. Ohio scored first on a 78-yard pass. Then Aaron Kearse scooped up a fumble and ran 25 yards for a touchdown. Quincy Byas recovered a muffed punt, and Rudy Kessinger kicked field goals of 31 and 41 yards, the second as time expired in the half. Thirteen to 10, Eagles.

Second, the drive of the year. Down 17-13 in the fourth, we started at our own 2. Brogan McCaughey hit Tanner Lemaster for 34 yards, and eight plays and 98 yards later, he hit Joey Mattord for a 24-yard touchdown. Twenty to 17 with 3:53 left. I screamed in a coffee shop. Depot Town will recover.

Third, the 13 seconds. On the kickoff, Darren James-Hamilton returned it 100 yards for a touchdown. Our final drive went 13 plays to the Ohio 16, and the last pass fell incomplete at the goal line with five seconds left.

My hero is Joey Mattord, with seven catches, a touchdown and 24 rushing yards. McCaughey completed 27 of 39 passes, Kessinger made both field goals, and Bryce Llewellyn had 11 tackles. And our defense held Ohio to 90 rushing yards.

My affectionate goat: kickoff coverage, obviously. Also third downs: we converted only two of 15. Fellas, that's not how we do it on the gray turf.

What it means: Eastern Michigan is 4-5 and 3-2 in the MAC. Ypsilanti built more than 8,500 B-24 bombers at Willow Run, so this town knows how to rebuild things fast.

Next up, Eastern Michigan faces Central Michigan at Ford Field on Wednesday, Nov. 4. Kickoff time and TV are still to be announced. Michigan rivals, an NFL stadium and our pride at stake. Gray turf, bright future.

articles.title: Brick by Brick, Then 100 Yards at Once: Darren James-Hamilton's Kickoff Return Lifts Ohio Over Eastern Michigan, 24-20
articles.byline: Penny Trautman, The Ohio Fanatic
articles.matchup: Ohio 24, Eastern Michigan 20 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Peden Stadium
articles.text:
Well, hello from Court Street! Penny Trautman here, standing on the bricks and shaking a little. On Saturday at Peden Stadium, Ohio beat Eastern Michigan 24-20, and the Bobcats are 4-0 in the MAC. I usually build my wins one brick at a time. Saturday, Darren James-Hamilton laid 100 yards of them in 13 seconds.

Here's how we built it.

The first brick: Nick Poulos hit Dom Dorwart for a 78-yard touchdown in the first quarter. Dorwart caught four passes for 125 yards. That's a load-bearing wall.

The wobbly bricks: Eastern Michigan returned a fumble for a touchdown, and James-Hamilton fumbled a punt return. We trailed 13-10 at halftime. Poulos ran in from the 1 late in the third to put us ahead 17-13, but the Eagles drove 98 yards for a 20-17 lead with 3:53 left.

The keystone: James-Hamilton took the next kickoff at the goal line and ran 100 yards for a touchdown. Earlier, he also intercepted a pass. Then our defense took over. Eastern Michigan drove to our 17, Michael Molnar forced an intentional grounding penalty, and the final pass fell incomplete at the goal line with five seconds left. Mortar set!

My hero is Darren James-Hamilton: an interception, a fumble and a 100-yard kickoff return touchdown. That's a whole season of emotions in one game. Molnar made 18 tackles and had a sack, and Jack Fries had two sacks.

My affectionate goat: third downs. We converted three of 11. And our run game only got 90 yards. Bricks are supposed to be heavy, fellas. Put some weight behind it.

What it means: Ohio is 6-2 and 4-0 in the MAC after five straight wins, alone at the top of the standings. Peden Stadium has been our home since 1929, and it hasn't seen many finishes better than that one.

Next up, Ohio visits Akron at InfoCision Stadium on Tuesday, Nov. 3, at 7 p.m. ET. Tuesday night MACtion. Brick by brick, Bobcats.

articles.title: Counter: 1,000! ULM Scores 18 Points in the Final 2:34, Billy Pullen Scores on the Last Play, and the Warhawks Get Their First Win at Troy, 21-14
articles.byline: Darnell Vidrine, The UL Monroe Fanatic
articles.matchup: UL Monroe 21, Troy 14 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Veterans Memorial Stadium (AL)
articles.text:
Good evening, night owls, and welcome back to the overnight show. Darnell Vidrine here, and friends, I need you to turn the radio up. On Saturday at Veterans Memorial Stadium, UL Monroe beat Troy 21-14. That's our first win of the season. The optimism counter just broke. It's at 1,000. I might need a new counter.

Here's how it went down.

For most of the night, it looked like another reset. Troy led 7-3 at halftime and 14-3 after Gavin Griffin's 1-yard touchdown with 6:16 left. But DJ Jester intercepted a pass in the end zone in the second quarter, right after Troy recovered our muffed punt at our 21. Hope was still on the air.

First hit: Aidan Armenta threw a 12-yard touchdown pass to Bryce Anderson with 2:34 left. Fourteen to 9. Our defense forced a three-and-out, and James Smith sacked Tucker Kilcrease. A holding penalty put us at our 14 with 1:40 left.

Second hit: 86 yards in six plays. Zach Palmer-Smith ran 14 yards, and a Troy personal foul added 15 more. Armenta hit P. Fulghum for 19 yards, then Darrion Gilliam for a 16-yard touchdown with 15 seconds left. Fifteen to 14!

Third hit: on the final play, the ball came loose, and Billy Pullen fell on it in the end zone. Twenty-one to 14. Friends, I spilled my coffee on the soundboard. Worth it.

My hero is Aidan Armenta: 13 of 22 for 147 yards and two late touchdowns. Billy Pullen had the winning touchdown, Kevontay Wells had a sack and a half, and Noah Flemmings had 15 tackles. Our defense held Troy to 47 passing yards.

My affectionate goat: two failed two-point tries. They made my heart skip beats. Our hearts are fine now. Mostly.

What it means: UL Monroe is 1-6 and 1-2 in the Sun Belt. Monroe is where the crop-dusting company that became Delta got started. Tonight, the Warhawks took off.

Next up, Southern Miss comes to Malone Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3:30 p.m. ET on ESPN+. Halloween at home. Counter: reset to 100. Keep the faith, Warhawks.

articles.title: Upside Down and Inside Out: Troy Leads 14-3 With 6:16 Left, Then Gives Up 18 Points as ULM Steals One, 21-14
articles.byline: Marlo Pickens, The Troy Fanatic
articles.matchup: UL Monroe 21, Troy 14 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Veterans Memorial Stadium (AL)
articles.text:
Hey there, buddy. Marlo Pickens, former Trojan long snapper, peanut farmer's son, and a man staring at the world upside down. On Saturday at Veterans Memorial Stadium, UL Monroe beat Troy 21-14. I flipped that game over every way I know, and it still looks bad. ULM hadn't won a game all year.

Here's the row-by-row count.

The planting: our defense was stout for 57 minutes. Gavin Griffin caught a 5-yard touchdown pass from Tucker Kilcrease in the first quarter and ran in from the 1 with 6:16 left. Fourteen to 3. I started counting my peanuts before they were boiled.

The weeds: Aidan Armenta threw a 12-yard touchdown with 2:34 left. We went three-and-out, and Kilcrease got sacked. Then, with 1:40 left, ULM drove 86 yards, helped by our 15-yard personal foul, and Armenta threw a 16-yard touchdown with 15 seconds left. Fifteen to 14.

The hailstorm: on the final play, we fumbled, and Billy Pullen fell on it in the end zone. Twenty-one to 14. I sat on the tailgate for an hour.

Earlier, we wasted a gift. We recovered a muffed punt at the ULM 21 in the second quarter, and moments later, our pass was intercepted in the end zone. That's a whole row of peanuts left in the field.

My hero is Jordan Lovett, who ran 17 times for 70 yards. Keno Jones had 12 tackles, and Ty Clemons and Donnie Smith had sacks.

My affectionate goat: the passing game. Forty-seven yards, fellas. I've thrown farther than that... well, backwards, between my legs.

What it means: Troy is 3-4 and 1-2 in the Sun Belt, with its first home loss of the season. Troy used to be called Deer Stand Hill, and right now, we're sitting in that deer stand waiting for something good to walk by.

Next up, Troy visits James Madison at Bridgeforth Stadium on Thursday, Oct. 29, at 7:30 p.m. ET on ESPN2. A short week, a tough road trip and a national TV crowd. Come early, buddy. Bring a sack of boiled peanuts. Bring two. I'll bring the puns.

articles.title: The Ledger Doesn't Balance: Lunch Winfield Throws for 299, but Jamarice Wilder's Late Touchdown Sends Louisiana Home Short, 35-31
articles.byline: Amélie 'Mimi' Fontenot, The Louisiana Fanatic
articles.matchup: Southern Miss 35, Louisiana 31 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Renasant Stadium
articles.text:
Allons danser, mes amis... slowly, tonight. Mimi Fontenot here, ledger open, accordion on low. On Saturday in Hattiesburg, Southern Miss beat Louisiana 35-31. I've audited this one three times. The numbers are correct, and I don't like them.

Here's the accounting.

Credits: Lunch Winfield ran for a touchdown, threw a 4-yard touchdown to Trenton Chaney with 31 seconds left in the first half and then threw a 31-yard touchdown pass to Anthony Reagan Jr. late in the third. JJ Garner broke a 42-yard touchdown run. We led 28-21 going into the fourth. That was a beautiful two-step.

Debits: early in the fourth, Kolby Peavy intercepted Winfield and scored. Twenty-eight to 28. A double-entry error if I've ever seen one.

The final balance: Tony Sterner kicked a 22-yard field goal with 2:51 left. Thirty-one to 28, Cajuns. But Southern Miss drove 75 yards in eight plays. Jamarice Wilder ran 28 yards and then 16 yards for the winning touchdown with 58 seconds left. We got a nice kickoff return to midfield, but after one short completion, three straight passes fell incomplete. The dance floor went dark.

My hero is Lunch Winfield: 299 passing yards, two touchdown passes and a rushing touchdown. Jake St. Andre had 11 tackles and a sack, and Maxie Baudoin IV added another sack. Our offense held the ball for over 34 minutes.

My affectionate goat: the run defense. Southern Miss ran for 286 yards, and Steven Robinson scored three times. Also fourth downs: we went zero for three. That's a write-off.

What it means: Louisiana is 5-3 and 2-2 in the Sun Belt. Lafayette is the Heart of Acadiana, and hearts can take a hit. Ours will start dancing again soon.

Next up, South Alabama comes to Our Lady of Lourdes Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7. Kickoff time and TV are still to be announced. That gives us an open week to rest up, rebalance the books and polish the two-step shoes. Laissez les bons stats rouler!

articles.title: Sweet Tea and Sweeter Finishes: Steven Robinson Scores Three Times, Jamarice Wilder Wins It Late, and Southern Miss Tops Louisiana, 35-31
articles.byline: Delphine 'Dee' Broussard, The Southern Miss Fanatic
articles.matchup: Southern Miss 35, Louisiana 31 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Renasant Stadium
articles.text:
Well, hey there, sugar. Dee Broussard, on my porch in the Pine Belt, and this week, my sweet tea and my disposition are equally sweet. On Saturday in Hattiesburg, Southern Miss beat Louisiana 35-31. That's our first win since the season opener, sugar, and it was worth every gray hair.

Here's the tea.

Pour one: Steven Robinson ran for three touchdowns in the first half, from 8, 4 and 10 yards. He carried 22 times for 145 yards. Bless that young man's legs.

Pour two: we trailed 28-21 heading into the fourth. Then Kolby Peavy intercepted Lunch Winfield and scored. Tied, 28-28. I spilled my tea all over my bow. Worth it.

Pour three: Louisiana kicked a field goal with 2:51 left to take a 31-28 lead. Our offense drove 75 yards in eight plays, and Jamarice Wilder ran 28 yards and then 16 yards for the touchdown with 58 seconds left. articles.title: The Court Is Not Amused: Old Dominion Is Held to Minus-13 Rushing Yards in a 26-0 Loss at Louisiana Tech
articles.byline: Winifred 'Winnie' Pocklington, The Old Dominion Fanatic
articles.matchup: Louisiana Tech 26, Old Dominion 0 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Joe Aillet Stadium
articles.text:
Hear ye, hear ye! The royal court of Old Dominion is now in session, and I'm sorry to report that the crown is crooked for a reason. Winnie Pocklington presiding. On Saturday at Joe Aillet Stadium, Louisiana Tech beat Old Dominion 26-0. We didn't score a single point. The royal scribe has nothing to write.

Here's the court record.

Exhibit A: the slow start. Louisiana Tech scored two touchdowns in the first quarter. Blake Baker ran in from the 4, and Trey Kukuk ran in from the 5. Fourteen to zero in the first quarter.

Exhibit B: the missed chance. Our defense did hold firm at the goal line before halftime, stopping Louisiana Tech on downs at our 10. Then, in the third quarter, we drove for a 40-yard field goal, and Nathanial Eichner missed. That would've been our only points, your honor.

Exhibit C: the lockdown. Louisiana Tech's defense sacked Jaxon Potter six times, and we ran for minus-13 yards on 22 carries. Amari Butler intercepted Potter in the fourth quarter. The castle walls held for them, not us.

My hero is Ja'Mez Drummer: 15 tackles. Koa Naotala had two sacks, and DeAndre Lynch had another. Our defense kept it to 26, which is something. Leon Haughton Jr. and Josh Rodriguez caught four passes each.

My affectionate goat: the running game. Negative 13 yards. In Norfolk, we have the world's largest naval base. On Saturday, we couldn't find a little room to run.

What it means: Old Dominion is 2-6 and 1-4 in the Sun Belt. It's a hard year at court. But this program went 9-2 in its first season back in 2009. Monarchs always reclaim the throne.

Next up, Marshall comes to S.B. Ballard Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 1 p.m. ET on ESPN+. Halloween at home. Bring your crown, your cape and your loudest voice. Long live the Monarchs. Hear ye, hear ye: the court is adjourned.

articles.title: Two Shutouts, One Orchard: Blake Baker Completes 28 of 34, the Defense Sacks ODU Six Times, and Louisiana Tech Wins 26-0
articles.byline: Booker 'Champ' Tullos, The Louisiana Tech Fanatic
articles.matchup: Louisiana Tech 26, Old Dominion 0 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Joe Aillet Stadium
articles.text:
Well, howdy, and welcome to the orchard. Champ Tullos here, former fullback and full-time peach man. On Saturday at Joe Aillet Stadium, Louisiana Tech beat Old Dominion 26-0. That's two straight shutouts, folks. Our defense hasn't allowed a point in eight quarters. These peaches are ripe.

Here's how we picked the crop. Well, harvested it. You know what I mean.

First, the fast start. We scored two touchdowns in the first quarter. Blake Baker ran in from the 4, and Trey Kukuk ran in from the 5. That's my kind of football, right up the middle, fullback style.

Second, the air show. Baker completed 28 of 34 passes for 303 yards. Eli Finley caught 10 passes for 128 yards, including a 2-yard touchdown in the third quarter. Jalen Mickens caught eight for 110, including a 36-yarder to set up a Hunter Rioux 49-yard field goal.

Third, the brick wall. Our defense sacked Jaxon Potter six times. Jadon Mayfield had two, and Alonzo Jackson Jr. and Justice Williams had one and a half each. Old Dominion ran for minus-13 yards. Amari Butler intercepted Potter in the fourth quarter, and we stopped them on fourth down twice.

My hero is the whole defense, but Jadon Mayfield gets the first peach. Baker gets the second, for throwing and running for touchdowns. And Kaegan Kent added a 25-yard field goal.

My affectionate goat: penalties. Nine for 75 yards. And we got stuffed on a fourth down at the 10 before halftime. A fullback would've scored there, I'm just saying.

What it means: Louisiana Tech is 5-2 and 3-0 in the Sun Belt, in our first year in the league. We've played football since 1901, and Saturday felt like one of the good ones. Ruston has a Peach Festival every June, but we're celebrating early this year.

Next up, Louisiana Tech visits South Alabama at Hancock Whitney Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3 p.m. ET on ESPN+. A Halloween trip to Mobile. Come early, bring a lawn chair, and if anybody offers you a peach, say yes ma'am.

articles.title: Release Notes: Third Downs Broken, Kickoff Coverage Broken, and San José State Falls at Nevada, 28-13
articles.byline: Tessa Nakagawa-Ruiz, The San José State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Nevada 28, San José State 13 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Mackay Stadium
articles.text:
Hey, team. Tessa Nakagawa-Ruiz here, at my standing desk in downtown San Jose, staring at a whiteboard full of red tickets. On Saturday at Mackay Stadium, Nevada beat San José State 28-13. This release did not pass QA.

Here's the retro.

Bug one: third downs. We converted one of 14. One! Nevada held the ball for more than 38 minutes, and our offense managed 204 yards. That's a blocker, team. Priority zero.

Bug two: the trick play. Down 14-3 early in the fourth, Nevada's Marshaun Brown, who'd already caught a touchdown pass, threw a 32-yard touchdown to Herschel Turner. Twenty-one to 3. Nobody had that one in the spec.

Bug three: kickoff coverage. Luke Weaver hit Dominique McKenzie for 47 yards, and Viliami Teu ran in an 11-yard touchdown. Twenty-one to 10, and we had a little momentum. Then K. Woods returned the kickoff 90 yards to our 8, and Nevada scored on the next play. That's what we call a regression.

What shipped: Trajan Sinatra made field goals of 38 and 41 yards. Jayden Robertson intercepted a pass, and Solomone Langi and Etu Finau had sacks. Tuli Tagovailoa-Amosa made 12 tackles, and Naseri Danielson made 11. Our offense also didn't turn it over.

My hero is Tuli Tagovailoa-Amosa, who also stopped Nevada on fourth down near midfield before halftime. Viliami Teu ran for our touchdown.

My affectionate goat: the penalty flags. Eight for 74 yards. Team, please stop filing bugs against yourselves.

What it means: San José State is 4-4 and 2-2 in the Mountain West. Our sprint velocity is down, but the roadmap still works. San Jose was California's first state capital. We know how to get things started.

Next up, New Mexico comes to CEFCU Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 4 p.m. ET on MW+. Halloween at home: costume optional, loud required. Ship it to prod.

articles.title: Happy 130th, Pack: Luke Duncan Throws Two Touchdowns, Marshaun Brown Throws One, and Nevada Beats San José State on Its Birthday, 28-13
articles.byline: Ridge Corbell, The Nevada Fanatic
articles.matchup: Nevada 28, San José State 13 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Mackay Stadium
articles.text:
Yo, Pack nation. Ridge Corbell here, on the tailgate of my truck outside Reno, board waxed and birthday cake in the cooler. On Saturday, Nevada football turned 130, and the Wolf Pack celebrated at Mackay Stadium by beating San José State 28-13. Fresh powder, baby. Nobody lost at their own party.

Here's the run, top to bottom.

The first turn: Luke Duncan hit Marshaun Brown for a 4-yard touchdown in the first quarter. Then Duncan threw a 25-yard touchdown pass to Trace Estes in the third. Fourteen to 3.

The trick: early in the fourth, Brown flipped the script and threw a 32-yard touchdown pass to Herschel Turner. A receiver touchdown pass on your 130th birthday? That's a backflip off the big kicker, dude.

The landing: SJSU scored to make it 21-10. Then K. Woods took the kickoff 90 yards to the SJSU 8, and after a penalty, Dominic Kelley ran in from the 4 on the next play. Twenty-eight to 10. Send it.

My hero is Marshaun Brown, with a touchdown catch, a touchdown pass and five catches. Duncan completed 18 of 29 for 178 yards and two scores. Kelley ran 24 times for 82 yards. Dylan LaBarbera had two sacks, and our defense held San José State to one third-down conversion in 14 tries. We also held the ball for over 38 minutes.

My affectionate goat: the second-quarter pass by Reeve Slone that got intercepted. Not every backflip lands, bro.

What it means: Nevada is 3-4 and 2-2 in the Mountain West. Mackay Stadium's field is at 4,610 feet, and on Saturday, the Pack were flying even higher than that.

Next up, Nevada visits UCLA at the Rose Bowl on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 4:15 p.m. ET on BTN. A Halloween trip to Pasadena, a big stage and a chance at a big run. Light the candles. Send it.

articles.title: Painted Blue in the Fourth: Dylan Riley Runs for 128 Yards and Two Late Touchdowns as Boise State Pulls Away at Washington State, 31-10
articles.byline: Thatcher Bluestem, The Boise State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Boise State 31, Washington State 10 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Gesa Field at Martin Stadium
articles.text:
Morning, Bronco Nation. Thatcher Bluestem here, on my back porch in the North End with my coffee and Turf the heeler, who I'm telling you is blue in spirit. On Saturday at Martin Stadium, Boise State beat Washington State 31-10. For three quarters, it was gray. In the fourth, we painted it blue.

Here's the brushwork.

First coat: it was 10-10 heading into the fourth. Sire Gaines had run in a 9-yard touchdown, and Canaan Moore hit a 28-yard field goal as the first half ended. But the Cougars hung around. Turf was pacing.

Second coat: early in the fourth, Maddux Madsen threw a 6-yard touchdown pass to Cam Bates. On Washington State's next drive, Boen Phelps intercepted Owen Eshelman and returned it to the WSU 33. Soon after, Dylan Riley ran 33 yards for a touchdown. Twenty-four to 10.

Third coat: from our own 10, Riley broke a 72-yard touchdown run. Thirty-one to 10. Then Washington State drove 13 plays to our goal line, and D. Ganter Jr. broke up the fourth-down pass at the goal line. That's the clear coat, folks. Shiny.

My hero is Dylan Riley: 13 carries, 128 yards and two touchdowns in the fourth quarter. Lopez Sanusi had two sacks, and Jayden Virgin-Morgan and Bol Bol each had one. Madsen threw a touchdown and still hasn't thrown an interception all season. We ran for 258 yards, too.

My affectionate goat: the first three quarters. Ten points for three quarters against a 1-6 team? Fellas, I almost switched to decaf.

What it means: Boise State is 6-1 and 3-0 in the Pac-12, and ranked. Our blue turf, installed in 1986, was the first non-green field in football history. Saturday, the Broncos brought a little of it to Pullman.

Next up, Texas State comes to Albertsons Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 10 p.m. ET on The CW. Halloween on the blue. Bring your costume, Bronco Nation. Wave the flag, Pullman. We'll paint it blue.

articles.title: Three Good Quarters on the Palouse: Washington State Ties Boise State 10-10, Then the Broncos Pull Away, 31-10
articles.byline: Hank Palouse, The Washington State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Boise State 31, Washington State 10 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Gesa Field at Martin Stadium
articles.text:
Howdy, Cougs. Hank Palouse here, in the cab of my pickup outside town, looking out at the wheat stubble. On Saturday at Martin Stadium, Boise State beat Washington State 31-10. I'll be honest with you: for three quarters, we went toe to toe with a ranked team. Then the fourth quarter showed up like a combine.

Here's the harvest report.

The good soil: Kirby Vorhees ran in a 1-yard touchdown just before halftime to tie it 7-7. Jack Stevens booted a 47-yard field goal in the third, and it was 10-10 entering the fourth quarter. I honked my horn. The cows looked at me funny.

The hailstorm: early in the fourth, Boise State scored on a 6-yard pass. On our next drive, Boen Phelps intercepted Owen Eshelman and set up a 33-yard touchdown run by Dylan Riley. Then Riley broke a 72-yard touchdown run from his own 10. Twenty-one points in about seven minutes.

The last row: we drove 13 plays, 72 yards to the Boise goal line. On fourth down, Eshelman's pass to Branden Ganashamoorthy was broken up at the goal line. So close, Cougs.

My hero is Owen Eshelman, who threw for 191 yards and ran 23 times. He took some hits and kept getting up. Ganashamoorthy caught four passes for 58 yards, Keith Brown had nine tackles, and we converted four of five fourth downs.

My affectionate goat: the run game. We ran 33 times for 53 yards. That's less than two yards a carry, fellas. Lentils grow faster.

What it means: Washington State is 1-7 and 0-4 in the Pac-12. That's a tough season to look at. But Ol' Crimson has flown at every College GameDay since 2003, and we Cougs don't stop waving.

Next up, Washington State visits San Diego State at Snapdragon Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 7 p.m. ET on CBSSN. A Halloween road trip to sunshine country. I know the record. I know who's coming. I'm waving it anyway.

My affectionate goat: the run game. We ran 33 times for 53 yards. That's less than two yards a carry, fellas. Lentils grow faster.

Next up, Washington State visits San Diego State at Snapdragon Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 7 p.m. ET on CBSSN. A Halloween road trip to sunshine country. I know the record. I know who's coming. I'm waving it anyway.

articles.title: Big Waves, Wipeout Ending: Stone Saunders Throws for 369 Yards, but San Diego State Falls at Colorado State, 56-49
articles.byline: Kai Delgado-Sorensen, The San Diego State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Colorado State 56, San Diego State 49 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Canvas Stadium
articles.text:
What's up from Pacific Beach, Aztec nation. Kai Delgado-Sorensen here, wetsuit peeled down, fish taco half-eaten, still processing. On Saturday at Canvas Stadium, Colorado State beat San Diego State 56-49. Dude. That was a 105-point swell. We rode a lot of waves. We just wiped out on a few too many.

Here's the surf report.

Set one: Stone Saunders was carving. He threw for 369 yards, and Jaylon Hawkins caught six passes for 164, including a 43-yard touchdown. Javion Kinnard ran for touchdowns of 19 and 32 yards. It was 24-21 us in the second quarter. Glassy conditions, bro.

Set two: then the closeout. Colorado State scored twice late in the half, and the second one was a 38-yard interception return by Tre'Shawn Moore. Thirty-five to 24 at halftime. That's getting caught inside, dude.

Set three: the comeback swell. Down 56-42, Saunders threw an interception that D'Mon Brinson returned to our 3. But on the very next play, G. Lightfoot forced and recovered a Hauss Hejny fumble at our 1. Then our offense went 99 yards in 16 plays, and Lucky Sutton ran in from the 7 with 1:57 left. Fifty-six to 49! But Colorado State got the ball back and ran out the clock.

My hero is G. Lightfoot, for that fumble that gave us one last wave. Hawkins was a freak, Sutton ran for two scores, and Saunders also threw a 24-yard touchdown to Jordan Napier and a two-point conversion to Bert Emanuel Jr. Josh Hunter made 13 tackles.

My affectionate goat: the defense. Five hundred forty-nine yards allowed. Fellas, that's not a defense, that's a beach break with no lifeguard.

What it means: San Diego State is 3-5 and 2-2 in the Mountain West. San Diego is the Birthplace of California, and we can still be born again this season.

Next up, Washington State comes to Snapdragon Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 7 p.m. ET on CBSSN. Halloween by the ocean. Costumes encouraged, wetsuits optional. I'll be watching from the beach, then heading in when the sun drops. Gnarly, dude. Go Aztecs.

articles.title: Five-Touchdown Summit: Hauss Hejny Throws Three, Runs for Two, and Colorado State Survives San Diego State, 56-49
articles.byline: Ansel Rimrock, The Colorado State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Colorado State 56, San Diego State 49 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Canvas Stadium
articles.text:
Morning, Rams. Ansel Rimrock here, at the Horsetooth trailhead with my thermos and a green-and-gold beanie, legs still shaking from the hike. On Saturday at Canvas Stadium, Colorado State beat San Diego State 56-49. That's 105 points at altitude. Even the mountain goats needed oxygen.

Here's the trail map.

Switchback one: Hauss Hejny was simply elevated. He threw touchdown passes to Tommy Maher of 9 and 54 yards. M. Brown returned a kickoff 62 yards to set up a Durell Robinson touchdown. Robinson scored twice on the ground and caught a 28-yard touchdown.

Switchback two: Tre'Shawn Moore, ladies and gentlemen. With 1:33 left in the first half, he intercepted Stone Saunders and returned it 38 yards for a touchdown. Thirty-five to 24 at halftime. I yodeled. Somebody asked me to stop. I did not.

Switchback three: Hejny ran 30 yards for a touchdown to make it 56-42. Then D'Mon Brinson intercepted Saunders and returned it 49 yards to the SDSU 3. Hejny fumbled at the goal line, though, and San Diego State drove 99 yards to make it 56-49 with 1:57 left. Then we got the ball back at their 44, picked up a first down and Hejny took a knee. Summit reached.

My hero is Hauss Hejny: 24 of 31 for 333 yards, three touchdown passes and two rushing touchdowns. Maher caught six for 108. Oumar Diomande made 13 tackles. We converted nine of 12 third downs.

My affectionate goat: the defense. We allowed 565 yards. Mountain air, thick defense? Not Saturday, friends. Let's just say we needed thick skin.

What it means: Colorado State is 3-4 and 1-2 in the Mountain West, and we snapped a four-game losing streak. Fort Collins inspired Main Street, U.S.A., at Disney's parks, and Saturday felt like a ride.

Next up, Colorado State visits Utah State at Maverik Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3:30 p.m. ET on USA Network. Halloween in Logan. Pack layers. Mountain air, thick skin. That's this week's motto. Go Rams.

articles.title: Missed the Last Train: Qwantavius Wiggins Runs 77 Yards for a Touchdown, but Georgia State Falls at Arkansas State, 38-32
articles.byline: Malik Overstreet, The Georgia State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Arkansas State 38, Georgia State 32 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Centennial Bank Stadium
articles.text:
Next stop, heartbreak. Malik Overstreet here, MARTA card in one pocket, third-down chart in the other, riding the train home from the station of sadness. On Saturday in Jonesboro, Arkansas State beat Georgia State 38-32. We were one drive from making the connection. We missed it.

Here's the route map.

Stop one: Qwantavius Wiggins. He caught a 33-yard touchdown pass from Ayden Pereira with 26 seconds left in the first half to tie it 14-14. Then in the third quarter, right after Arkansas State took the lead, he ran 77 yards for a touchdown. Twenty-one to 21. That's express service.

Stop two: the delay. Arkansas State scored 17 straight points, with two touchdowns and a field goal. Thirty-eight to 21. That's the Downtown Connector at 5:15 on a Friday.

Stop three: the comeback. Pereira threw a 27-yard touchdown to Rodshaun Dorsey and found Derrick Avery Jr. for two. Then Pereira hit Dorsey for 37 yards, and Samer Layous kicked a 33-yard field goal. Thirty-eight to 32 with 4:25 left. We got the ball back at our 13 with 1:49 left and drove into Arkansas State territory. Then Makai Shahid intercepted Pereira at the 6 with 15 seconds left. Doors closing.

My hero is Qwantavius Wiggins: 99 rushing yards, five catches and two touchdowns. Dorsey caught three passes for 85 yards. Cameran Brown threw a touchdown to DJ Riles. Jaydon Hood made 10 tackles, and Tre Mittman and Coby Owens each had sacks.

My affectionate goat: the two interceptions. And three-for-12 on third down. You know I keep the chart, Panthers.

What it means: Georgia State is 4-3 and 1-2 in the Sun Belt. Center Parc Stadium was built for the 1996 Olympics, and we still have time to finish the race.

Next up, Coastal Carolina comes to Center Parc Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 2 p.m. ET on ESPN+. Halloween at home, Panthers. Take the train. Next stop, Center Parc. Mind the gap, and mind the Chanticleers.

articles.title: Let It Rip: Trey Owens Throws Two Touchdowns, Runs for Two More, and Arkansas State Holds Off Georgia State, 38-32
articles.byline: Ty Doucet-Harmon, The Arkansas State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Arkansas State 38, Georgia State 32 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Centennial Bank Stadium
articles.text:
Quaaack. Ty Doucet-Harmon here, Delta duck guide and Red Wolves lifer, with my duck call around my neck and my voice mostly gone. On Saturday at Centennial Bank Stadium, Arkansas State beat Georgia State 38-32. It came down to the final seconds, folks. I let it rip.

Here's the hunt.

Setting the decoys: Trey Owens threw a 12-yard touchdown pass to Jaylen Bonelli in the first quarter and ran in a 2-yard score in the second. Then early in the third, Brandon Greil intercepted Ayden Pereira, and on the next play Owens hit Nana Burris for a 54-yard touchdown. Twenty-one to 14.

The flock lands: Georgia State tied it on a 77-yard run. Then Owens hit Bonelli for 35 yards and ran in from the 1. Timothy Carter ran in a 2-yard touchdown to start the fourth, and Owens hit Bonelli for 38 yards to set up Clune Van Andel's 26-yard field goal. Thirty-eight to 21. Quaaack.

The last shot: Georgia State pulled within 38-32 and drove into our territory in the final minute. With 15 seconds left, Makai Shahid intercepted Ayden Pereira at our 6. Shahid had an interception called back by a roughing penalty just one play earlier. Second chance, good shot. Dinner's in the cooler, folks.

My hero is Trey Owens: 21 of 32 for 309 yards, two touchdown passes and two rushing touchdowns. Bonelli caught seven passes for 150, and Burris caught six for 114. Joe Drew made 10 tackles, and Tre Stevens and Shakai Woods had sacks. We didn't turn it over.

My affectionate goat: field goals. Van Andel missed from 44 and 48 yards before hitting from 26. And we went two for 10 on third downs.

What it means: Arkansas State is 4-4 and 2-2 in the Sun Belt. We've been the Red Wolves since 2008, and this pack knows how to hunt.

Next up, UL Monroe comes to Centennial Bank Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7, at 3 p.m. ET. TV is still to be announced. That means a week off first to rest the calls. Get in the blind early, keep your voice low until it counts, and when it counts, let it rip. Quaaack.

articles.title: One Scoop Short: Anthony Garcia Throws a Touchdown, Utah State Ties It Late, but Texas State Wins 20-17 on a Field Goal
articles.byline: Hyrum Tolleson, The Utah State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Texas State 20, Utah State 17 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, UFCU Stadium
articles.text:
Howdy, Aggies. Hyrum Tolleson here, in my booth at Aggie Ice Cream with a double scoop melting a little faster than usual. On Saturday in San Marcos, Texas State beat Utah State 20-17. We churned for four quarters, folks, and came up one scoop short.

Here's the batch.

The first pour: Kian Afrookhteh made a 43-yard field goal to put us up 3-0. On the ensuing kickoff, Jaylen Jenkins returned it 100 yards for a touchdown. That's the ice cream hitting the floor before you get your first lick.

The churn: Afrookhteh added field goals of 48 and 27 yards, and we led 9-7 at halftime. But Texas State scored 10 straight to go up 17-9.

The rally: we drove 75 yards in 10 plays, and receiver Anthony Garcia threw a 6-yard touchdown pass to Kaina Watson. Grady Brosterhous hit Javen Jacobs for the two-point conversion. Seventeen to 17 with 8:07 left! Texas State answered with a 37-yard field goal with 1:56 left. We drove 13 plays to their 25, but a delay of game pushed us back, and Afrookhteh's 48-yard try missed as time expired.

My hero is Anthony Garcia: eight catches for 87 yards and a touchdown pass. Our defense held the nation's top offense to 250 yards and sacked Brad Jackson four times, one each from Bronson Olevao Jr., Brevin Hamblin, Asher Cunningham and Tyree Morris. David Kabongo had eight tackles. We didn't turn it over.

My affectionate goat: the delay of game before the last kick. Five yards matter, Aggies. Also the run game: 73 yards on 32 carries.

What it means: Utah State is 2-5 and 1-2 in the Mountain West. Aggie Ice Cream has been around since 1888, and it didn't get great overnight either. Stay patient.

Next up, Colorado State comes to Maverik Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3:30 p.m. ET on USA Network. Halloween in Logan. Bring a jacket, Aggies. And save me a scoop.

articles.title: Float On, Bobcats: Jaylen Jenkins Returns a Kickoff 100 Yards, Jacob Bonilla Kicks the Winner, and Texas State Beats Utah State, 20-17
articles.byline: Yesenia Calderwood, The Texas State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Texas State 20, Utah State 17 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, UFCU Stadium
articles.text:
Hey, y'all. Yesenia Calderwood here, back in my inner tube at Sewell Park with my feet in the San Marcos River and my sweet tea finally sweet again. On Saturday at UFCU Stadium, Texas State beat Utah State 20-17. It wasn't a lazy float, y'all. It was rapids the whole way down.

Here's the river report.

First current: Utah State kicked a field goal, and Jaylen Jenkins took the ensuing kickoff 100 yards for a touchdown. I dropped my koozie in the river. Worth it.

Second current: we trailed 9-7 at halftime. Then Brad Jackson ran in a 3-yard touchdown in the third, and Jacob Bonilla booted a 51-yard field goal in the fourth. Seventeen to 9. Smooth water.

Third current: Utah State tied it 17-17 with 8:07 left. Our offense answered with a 13-play, 51-yard drive that took more than six minutes, and Bonilla kicked a 37-yarder with 1:56 left. Then Utah State drove to our 25, a delay of game backed them up, and their 48-yard try missed as time expired. I hugged my inner tube.

My hero is Jacob Bonilla, with the 51-yarder and the winner. Jenkins gets a medal too. Jackson completed 27 of 37 passes and ran in a score. Payne had nine tackles, and Trez Moore had eight. We converted 10 of 18 third downs and didn't turn it over.

My affectionate goat: the offense, which managed 250 yards after leading the country in yards per game. Y'all, that's like tubing in a drought. Also Bonilla's 49-yard miss before halftime. We still love you, Jacob.

What it means: Texas State is 4-3 and 2-1 in the Mountain West. The San Marcos River rises from springs that have flowed for thousands of years, and this team just keeps flowing too. Sorry. I warned you about the puns.

Next up, Texas State visits Boise State at Albertsons Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 10 p.m. ET on The CW. Halloween on the blue turf. Wear maroon. Eat 'em up, Cats! See y'all on the river.

articles.title: Another Medal for the Sash: A'Marion Peterson Scores Twice, Owen Pewee Gets Three Sacks, and UTSA Wins a Fifth Straight, 42-19 at Tulane
articles.byline: Marisol Ybarra, The UTSA Fanatic
articles.matchup: UTSA 42, Tulane 19 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Yulman Stadium
articles.text:
Birds up! Marisol Ybarra here, on a River Walk patio, with a sash so heavy I may need a third ribbon. On Saturday at Yulman Stadium, UTSA beat Tulane 42-19. That's five straight wins, Roadrunners. Somebody get me a needle and thread.

Here's how the medals got earned.

Medal one: the bounce back. Tulane's Anthony Rogers intercepted our very first pass and ran it back 22 yards for a touchdown. Not the start I wanted, mi gente. But A'Marion Peterson ran in from the 1 and then from the 16, and Owen McCown ran in a 4-yard touchdown. Twenty-one to 7.

Medal two: the defense, which forced six turnovers. J. Buxton forced a fumble at our 1 that went out the end zone for a touchback. Willie Nelson III and Zach Morris each intercepted Trace Johnson. Our defense recovered four fumbles. And Owen Pewee had three sacks.

Medal three: the knockout. Up 21-13 at halftime, Will Henderson III ran in a 9-yard touchdown, and Brandon High Jr. ran in from the 5. Thirty-five to 13. Mark Wiepert added a 1-yard touchdown late.

My hero is Owen Pewee, with three sacks. Henderson ran for 102 yards, and Peterson scored twice. We converted 12 of 16 third downs and held the ball for over 35 minutes.

My affectionate goat: our own turnovers. McCown threw two interceptions, and Peterson fumbled at the Tulane 3. Three giveaways in a blowout? Ay, Roadrunners, don't make me take a medal back.

What it means: UTSA is 7-1 and 4-0 in the American, and the Roadrunners are bowl eligible. San Antonio has held Fiesta every April since 1891, and right now it feels like Fiesta in October.

Next up, UTSA visits Florida Atlantic at Flagler Credit Union Stadium on Thursday, Nov. 5, at 8 p.m. ET. TV is still to be announced. A week off first, then a Thursday night under the lights. Birds up!

articles.title: Six Turnovers in the Gumbo: Anthony Rogers Returns an Interception for a Touchdown, but UTSA Beats Tulane, 42-19
articles.byline: Antoine 'Twan' Ducros-Labat, The Tulane Fanatic
articles.matchup: UTSA 42, Tulane 19 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Yulman Stadium
articles.text:
Roll Wave... quietly. Twan here, trumpet in the case, powdered sugar on my good shirt and a long face Uptown. On Saturday at Yulman Stadium, UTSA beat Tulane 42-19. We turned the ball over six times, y'all. That gumbo burned at the bottom of the pot.

Here's the recipe gone wrong.

The good start: on UTSA's first play, Anthony Rogers intercepted Owen McCown and ran it back 22 yards for a touchdown. I blew my trumpet so hard the neighbors called. Seven to nothing.

The burned roux: the turnovers piled up. Trace Johnson fumbled. Garrett Mmahat caught a 56-yard pass and fumbled at the UTSA 18. Johnnie Daniels fumbled at the 1, and it went out the end zone for a touchback. Then Z. Lewis Jr. fumbled. UTSA led 21-7. Cooper Helmke kicked field goals of 38 and 33 yards, the second as the half ended, to make it 21-13.

The cold pot: UTSA scored two touchdowns in the third quarter, and Johnson threw two second-half interceptions. Daniels broke an 81-yard run and scored from the 7 in the fourth. But that was it.

My hero is Anthony Rogers, with two interceptions and a touchdown. Daniels ran eight times for 104 yards. J. Tchienchou forced and recovered a fumble at our 3. Ed Smith IV had a sack and forced a fumble. Kevin Adams III and Dickson Agu each made eight tackles.

My affectionate goat: ball security. Six turnovers. Y'all, you can't serve gumbo if you keep dropping the bowl.

What it means: Tulane is 3-4 and 1-2 in the American. New Orleans was founded in 1718, and this city knows about hard times and brass bands. We'll be back on our feet.

Next up, Tulane visits Charlotte at Jerry Richardson Stadium on Friday, Oct. 30, at 7 p.m. ET on ESPN2. A Friday night trip, a short week and a chance to get the roux right. Roll Wave!

articles.title: Hotdish Left in the Oven Too Long: Nathan Hayes Throws Two Touchdowns, but an Interception Return Sinks North Dakota State at New Mexico, 21-16
articles.byline: Ingeborg 'Inga' Halvorsen, The North Dakota State Fanatic
articles.matchup: New Mexico 21, North Dakota State 16 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, University Stadium (NM)
articles.text:
Well, hi there. Inga Halvorsen here, in my kitchen in south Fargo, scraping the burnt bits off a tater tot hotdish. On Saturday night in Albuquerque, New Mexico beat North Dakota State 21-16. Oh, fer cryin' out loud. We were right there, dontcha know.

Here's the potluck report.

The first dish: New Mexico scored first, and then Nathan Hayes threw an interception. But Ray James Jr. intercepted Toa Fa'avae right back, and Jackson Williams caught a 41-yard pass to set up a Drew Klein field goal. Seven to 3.

The second dish: Hayes threw a 15-yard touchdown to Reis Kessel in the third quarter, and we trailed 14-9 after the extra point was blocked. Our defense was holding strong, and New Mexico missed field goals from 54 and 42 yards. I had my oven mitts on, ready to serve.

The dish that burned: early in the fourth, Austin Brawley intercepted Hayes and returned it 56 yards for a touchdown. Twenty-one to 9. Hayes threw a 4-yard touchdown to Mekhi Collins to make it 21-16 with 6:42 left. We got the ball back at our 9 with 2:10 left, but a 5-yard loss and a fourth-down incompletion ended it.

My hero is Ray James Jr.: 11 tackles, an interception and a sack. Gavin Sell had 10 tackles and a sack. Our defense held New Mexico to 279 yards and 92 passing. Williams caught four passes for 71 yards.

My affectionate goat: the run game. Fifty-three yards on 28 carries. That's like Jell-O salad without the Jell-O. And the two interceptions, ope.

What it means: North Dakota State is 6-2. Fargo has seen colder nights than this. The Bison have won 10 national championships, so we know a thing or two about bouncing back.

Next up, UTEP comes to the Fargodome on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3:30 p.m. ET on MW+. Halloween indoors, where it's warm. Bring a hotdish. Oh, for cute. Go Bison.

articles.title: Riding the Thermal: Austin Brawley's 56-Yard Interception Return Lifts New Mexico Past North Dakota State, 21-16, and the Lobos Are 6-1
articles.byline: Paloma Begaye-Ortiz, The New Mexico Fanatic
articles.matchup: New Mexico 21, North Dakota State 16 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, University Stadium (NM)
articles.text:
Buenos días, Lobo nation. Paloma Begaye-Ortiz here, tailgate down, breakfast burrito in hand, red and green. On Saturday night at University Stadium, New Mexico beat North Dakota State 21-16. We read the wind, we caught the thermal, and we landed it. Six and one, Lobos!

Here's the flight log.

Liftoff: Kiefer Sibley ran 29 yards for a touchdown in the first quarter. Then CJ McBean intercepted Nathan Hayes and returned it 20 yards to the NDSU 30. Seven to nothing, and the sky was blue.

Steady altitude: just before halftime, M. Beltran Jr. returned a punt 44 yards, and Scottre Humphrey ran in from the 2 with 10 seconds left. Fourteen to 3 at the break.

The gust: North Dakota State pulled within 14-9. Then early in the fourth, Austin Brawley intercepted Hayes and returned it 56 yards for a touchdown. Twenty-one to 9! I nearly let go of the burner. NDSU scored to make it 21-16, but on their last drive, D. Agu and F. Edwards dropped Myles Mitchell for a 5-yard loss, and Hayes' fourth-down pass fell incomplete. Fa'avae took three knees. Soft landing.

My hero is Austin Brawley, for the play of the night. Sibley ran for 91 yards, and we ran for 187 as a team against one of the best defenses in the country. Mercury Swaim made 11 tackles, and Brett Karhu had a sack. We forced two turnovers and gave up only one.

My affectionate goat: field goals. Grant Glasgow missed from 54 and 42 yards. And our passing game managed 92 yards. Some flights, you just have to trust the wind.

What it means: New Mexico is 6-1 and 3-0 in the Mountain West, and we're bowl eligible. Albuquerque hosts the largest balloon festival in the world, and right now, the Lobos are floating high above all of it.

Next up, New Mexico visits San José State at CEFCU Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 4 p.m. ET on MW+. Halloween in the Bay Area. Bring a jacket. Red or green? Both. Go Lobos.

articles.title: Graded on a Curve, Passed With Honors: Nate Sheppard's Trick-Play Touchdown Pass Lifts Duke at Virginia, 19-16
articles.byline: Harrison Wexley-Moore IV, The Duke Fanatic
articles.matchup: Duke 19, Virginia 16 (final), Fri., Oct. 23, Scott Stadium
articles.text:
Good evening, Blue Devil faithful. Harrison Wexley-Moore IV here, pre-law, pre-med, pre-astronaut and, as of Friday night, pre-quarterback-coach. Duke 19, Virginia 16, at Scott Stadium, and the winning touchdown was thrown by our running back. I have read every playbook ever written, and I still did not see it coming. Neither, crucially, did Virginia.

The setup was elegant. Virginia had just gone ahead 16-13 on a Will Bettridge field goal with three minutes left. Then, with 1:14 to go, Nate Sheppard, the ACC's leading rusher, took the ball, turned around and threw it 28 yards to Brody Keefe, who was so wide open he could have filed a dissertation. Per the AP, Virginia's defense had seen a similar look the play before and was caught by surprise. That's what we call a well-designed exam question.

Before that, the field-goal seminar. Sheppard opened with a 32-yard touchdown run on our first drive. Then the offense went quiet, punting on its final four possessions of the first half, and Virginia led 13-7 at the break. Gavin Strange kicked a 39-yarder in the third quarter and another 39-yarder to tie it with 8:50 left. Patrick Smith-Young sealed it by intercepting Virginia's last pass. Tyshon Reed recovered a fumble. Nick Morris Jr. made 11 tackles, and DaShawn Stone had nine.

Hero: Sheppard, obviously, on a degree-worthy throw. Honorable mention to Walker Eget, 211 passing yards, and Jonah Burton, four catches for 59. The goat, graded gently: we missed the extra point after the winning touchdown, so the margin stayed three, and Virginia held the ball almost 39 minutes. I'd give the offense an incomplete, with a chance to make it up.

What it means: per the AP, the win snaps a two-game slide, and Duke is 5-2 and 2-2 in the ACC, keeping alive its hopes of a return trip to the conference title game. Coach Manny Diaz said the team found a way to finish this time. An honest grade? B-plus, rounded up for creativity.

Next up: Boston College comes to Wallace Wade Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at noon ET on The CW. Halloween in Durham. I'll be dressed as a Nobel laureate. It's not a costume.

Class dismissed. Go Duke!

articles.title: A Fresh Nib for a Hard Entry: Virginia Falls to Duke's Late Trick Play at Scott Stadium, 19-16
articles.byline: Prescott Ashby-Lowell, The Virginia Fanatic
articles.matchup: Duke 19, Virginia 16 (final), Fri., Oct. 23, Scott Stadium
articles.text:
Good evening, and welcome to the Grounds. Prescott Ashby-Lowell, fourth-generation Wahoo, with a fresh nib in the fountain pen and a heavy heart in the waistcoat. Duke 19, Virginia 16, Friday night at Scott Stadium. Our first home loss of the season. Mr. Jefferson charted the weather at Monticello through storms, and so shall I.

The ledger entry reads as follows. With three minutes left, Will Bettridge kicked a 30-yard field goal, and Virginia led 16-13. I underlined it twice. Then, with 1:14 left, Duke handed the ball to Nate Sheppard, the ACC's leading rusher, and Sheppard turned and threw 28 yards to a wide-open Brody Keefe. Linebacker Kam Robinson said afterward, in essence, that the defense had played wonderfully until that one busted snap. Coach Tony Elliott pointed to a similar look the play before. I drew a small, sad sketch of it in the margin.

Our last chance ended when Beau Pribula's final pass was intercepted. I set the pen down. I lifted it again. A ledger must be complete.

And there is much to record with pride. Jekail Middlebrook ran 24 times for 117 yards and a touchdown, a 1-yard plunge in the first quarter. Bettridge kicked three field goals, including a 32-yarder as the first half ended to give us a 13-7 lead. Kam Robinson intercepted a pass. Christian Ellis made six tackles, and Maddox Marcellus had two tackles for loss. We outgained Duke 353 to 327 and held the ball for 38:47. John Rogers caught five passes for 65 yards.

The goat, recorded in the gentlest ink: the red zone and the scoreboard. Per the AP, the offense gained yards but couldn't turn them into points, and three field goals plus one touchdown will rarely be enough. That, and one trick play.

What it means: Virginia is 4-4 and 2-3 in the ACC, with three losses in four games, per the AP. Duke, which beat us in the ACC title game last season, has now done it again in October. Rivalries in the ledger tend to have long memories.

Next up: at Wake Forest on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3:45 p.m. ET on ESPN2, at Allegacy Federal Credit Union Stadium. Halloween in Winston-Salem. I'll be in a seersucker costume, which is just my clothing.

Wahoowa, and the Good Old Song, always.

articles.title: Lid Opened Too Early: NC State Rallies Late but Comes Up Three Short at Stanford
articles.byline: Rutherford 'Ruff' Pegram, The NC State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Stanford 31, NC State 28 (final), Fri., Oct. 23, Stanford Stadium
articles.text:
Well, howdy, Pack. Rutherford "Ruff" Pegram here, writing from a cold grill. Not a bye-week cold grill. A "we flew all the way to the Farm and came home three points light" cold grill. Stanford 31, NC State 28. Somebody opened the smoker lid too early.

First rule of the pit: don't let the fire get away from you early. Davis Warren threw touchdowns on Stanford's first two drives, and it was 14-0 before most of us back home found the channel. But this team adjusts the vents. CJ Bailey dropped a beauty to Deandre Desinor for a 58-yard touchdown, Will Wilson plowed in from 2 yards, and it was 14-14. I howled. That's my one howl. Discipline.

Then the flare-ups. We let Stanford go 90 yards in the last two minutes of the half for a 21-14 lead. Our opening drive of the third quarter ended in a touchdown, until a flag for offensive pass interference on Victor Snow took it away and we punted. Stanford went 90 more and scored on fourth-and-4. Wilson answered with his second 2-yard touchdown, and Bailey hit Keenan Jackson for 16 yards with 1:20 left to make it 31-28. Onside kick. Stanford recovered. Fire out.

Hero platter: Bailey, 17 of 30 for 256 yards, two touchdowns, no interceptions and 59 rushing yards. Ronnie Royal III made 10 tackles. We didn't turn it over once and went 8 of 14 on third down. That's temperature control. The goat, with love: the pass defense, which allowed 303 yards and four touchdown throws. When the other pitmaster serves four touchdowns, check your thermometer.

And credit to the Cardinal. The AP says this was only NC State's second game on the West Coast in 66 seasons, and our boys practiced late at night to fight the time change. Didn't quite take.

What it means: 3-4, 1-3 in the ACC, and the margin in the conference race is gone. But two of our four losses came by four points or fewer. Close fires can be fixed.

Next up: California comes to Carter-Finley on Saturday, Oct. 31, at noon ET on ACC Network. Halloween in Raleigh. Grill lit by 7 a.m.

Light the fire, Pack. We're not done cooking.

articles.title: The Pivot Worked: Davis Warren Ships Four Touchdowns and Stanford Holds Off NC State 31-28
articles.byline: Ignatius 'Iggy' Yamamoto-Ross, The Stanford Fanatic
articles.matchup: Stanford 31, NC State 28 (final), Fri., Oct. 23, Stanford Stadium
articles.text:
Greetings, stakeholders. Ignatius "Iggy" Yamamoto-Ross here, founder of three failed apps and, as of Friday night, one wildly successful product launch. Last week my deck said, "Let's pivot to the run game." Stanford pivoted to everything. Stanford 31, NC State 28. Please hold applause until the end of the slide.

The demo opened hot. Davis Warren threw touchdown passes on each of the first two drives, to Nico Brown and Sedrick Irvin, and Stanford racked up 234 yards in the first quarter, its most in an opening quarter since 2017. My houseplant social network gained 234 users in its entire lifetime, and most of them were my mother.

NC State tied it at 14, so Warren ran the two-minute drill like a seed round closing at midnight: 90 yards, capped by a 26-yard touchdown to Caden High with 25 seconds left in the half. Then, after a Wolfpack touchdown came off the board on an offensive pass interference flag, Stanford marched 90 more yards, and Warren hit Brown for 5 yards on fourth-and-4. Going for it on fourth down is what we in the Valley call disruption. NC State scored with 1:20 left to make it 31-28, tried the onside kick, and Stanford recovered. A stranger hugged me. I allowed it. Culture matters.

Hero: Warren, 22 of 37 for 303 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions. Co-founder: Micah Ford, 150 rushing yards on 22 carries, plus 58 receiving. Caden High caught nine for 103. Affectionate goat: the fourth quarter, when we let the Wolfpack score twice. Consider it a bug. We'll patch it.

What it means: Stanford is 4-4 and 2-3 in the ACC, with four wins in five home games. The road is the problem. The AP notes Stanford is 0-3 away from home, and the Cardinal must win at least one of their next three road games to have a shot at the program's first bowl since 2018.

Next up: at Louisville on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3:15 p.m. ET on ACC Network. I'm building a deck called "The Farm Travels Well." Slide one is a suitcase.

Go Card, stakeholders. Meeting adjourned.

articles.title: Two Signs, One Afternoon: Cal Leads at the Break, Then Gets Run Out of Dallas 59-20
articles.byline: Quentin Oyelaran-Fitch, The California Fanatic
articles.matchup: SMU 59, California 20 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Gerald J. Ford Stadium
articles.text:
Comrades in blue and gold, greetings. Quentin Oyelaran-Fitch here, with a hoarse voice and ink on my fingers. Saturday in Dallas I made two signs. The first said, in hand-lettered gold, "HALFTIME: CAL 20, SMU 17. THE PEOPLE ARE WINNING." The second, made in the fourth quarter with a borrowed marker, said, "WHY." Final: SMU 59, California 20.

Thesis: the first half was real. Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele, starting for the first time since his concussion on Oct. 3, hit Chase Hendricks for a 10-yard touchdown on the opening drive. Mason Mini plunged in from a yard out, and Towns McGough kicked field goals of 41 and 37 yards, the second as the half expired. Kant wrote of the sublime. I experienced it, briefly.

Antithesis: the second half also happened. SMU scored touchdowns on its first six drives after the break. Cal opened the half with three straight three-and-outs. Three and out, three times. That isn't a possession. That's a haiku. Worse, Kevin Jennings' touchdown to Derrick McFall was the 73rd of his career, an SMU record. We didn't just lose the half. We became someone else's footnote.

And then there's Kendrick Raphael, who scored the winning touchdown for us in last year's 38-35 win over SMU. On Saturday he ran for 104 yards and accounted for three touchdowns against us. I hold no grudge. I hold a sign: "WE RAISED HIM WELL."

Hero: Sagapolutele, 27 of 37 for 265 yards, a touchdown and no interceptions. That's courage. Hendricks caught seven passes for 83 yards, and Ian Strong added five for 71. The goat, gently: the yellow laundry. Eleven penalties for 107 yards, plus 40 rushing yards all day. That isn't a ground game. That's a ground suggestion.

Synthesis: Cal is 3-5 and 2-3 in the ACC, and the AP notes we've lost four of our last five. Honesty is the first virtue. Snacks are the second.

Next up: at NC State on Saturday, Oct. 31, at noon ET on ACC Network, the second of three straight road games. Raleigh takes barbecue seriously. I'll bring a sign that says "THE BEAR ALSO EATS."

Go Bears, comrades. The revolution resumes at noon.

articles.title: The Second-Half Costume Change: Kevin Jennings Breaks the Record as SMU Dresses Down Cal 59-20
articles.byline: Tatum Delacroix-Price, The SMU Fanatic
articles.matchup: SMU 59, California 20 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Gerald J. Ford Stadium
articles.text:
Well, hello, darlings. Tatum Delacroix-Price here, steamer in hand, because I spent all weekend pressing the wrinkles out of the first half. SMU 59, California 20. Yes, fifty-nine. And yes, we were losing at halftime. Every great runway show needs a costume change, sugar.

The first half was an outfit that didn't fit in the shoulders. Cal scored first, then went ahead again on a Mason Mini 1-yard run and two Towns McGough field goals, the last as the half expired. Cal 20, SMU 17. My assistant brought me sparkling water and backed away slowly.

Then, the reveal. SMU scored touchdowns on its first six drives of the second half while Cal opened with three straight three-and-outs. Freshman Christian Rhodes ran in from 5 and 3 yards, and EJ Kelly added the final bow from 10 out. The front-page moment: Kevin Jennings' 21-yard touchdown pass to Derrick McFall, his 73rd career touchdown pass, breaking Tanner Mordecai's school record of 72. Sew that number into the lining of a tailored blazer, please.

Best dressed: Jennings, 16 of 23 for 223 yards, three touchdowns, no interceptions. The glow-up of the season: Kendrick Raphael, 104 rushing yards and three touchdowns in all against Cal, the school he played for last year. When the Bears beat us 38-35 in last season's finale, Raphael scored their winning touchdown. This year, darling, he wore the right jersey. Our defense held Cal to 40 rushing yards, with sacks from Marques White and Brandon Miyazono.

The fashion emergency, said with love: 2 of 9 on third down. Thankfully we went 4 for 4 on fourth down, which is the football version of forgetting your belt and getting complimented on the suspenders.

What it means: SMU is 6-1 and 4-1 in the ACC and climbed from No. 23 to No. 19 in the AP poll released Oct. 25. The AP says we're 11-0 at home in ACC games since joining the league in 2024 and 24-2 in our last 26 home games. The Boulevard has never looked better.

Next up: at Syracuse on Saturday, Oct. 31, at noon ET on ESPN2, our only road game in a seven-week stretch. I'm packing layers and absolutely nothing orange.

Pony Up, darlings. The collection is coming together beautifully.

articles.title: Gumbo on the Plains: Sam Leavitt Cooks Up Four Touchdowns as LSU Rolls Auburn 38-17
articles.byline: Celestine 'Cece' Thibodeaux, The LSU Fanatic
articles.matchup: LSU 38, Auburn 17 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Jordan-Hare Stadium
articles.text:
Bonjour, Tiger fans! Ça va? Cece Thibodeaux here, and cher, I'm still licking the spoon. I drove home from Auburn with a pot of étouffée buckled into the passenger seat like a beloved child. LSU 38, Auburn 17, on the Plains, ending an eight-game road losing streak in SEC play. Mamère would have looked at that roux and said, now that's a color.

You build a gumbo in layers, and the Tigers built a 31-10 halftime lead the same way, scoring on five of six first-half possessions. Sam Leavitt hit Jackson Harris for a 10-yard touchdown, then capped a 95-yard drive with a 15-yarder to tight end Trey'Dez Green, back after missing four games with a sprained knee. Welcome home, baby. We saved you a bowl.

Auburn cut it to 17-10, and I put the lid on the pot for about a minute. Then Harris caught a 12-yard crossing route and turned it into a 70-yard touchdown sprint. He outran the defense, the cameras and my cousin Remy's truck. Leavitt finished the half with a 4-yard scoring run with 17 seconds left. Let it simmer.

Head chef: Leavitt, 32 of 45 for a career-high 387 yards and three touchdowns, plus 54 rushing yards and a score, with zero turnovers for a second straight week. Harris caught nine balls for 178 yards. And the defense? Mon Dieu. Byrum Brown ran for 115 yards against Georgia the week before. Against LSU, 21 yards on 19 carries and six sacks, with Davhon Keys, TJ Dottery and Princewill Umanmielen each getting one. LSU outgained Auburn 552 to 271. That's not a game, cher. That's a cooking class.

The burnt rice, with love: a scoreless third quarter, when we napped like Uncle Gaston after Thanksgiving. We'll scrape the pot.

What it means: LSU is 6-2 and 4-2 in the SEC and climbed from No. 18 to No. 15 in the AP poll released Oct. 25. The AP called it the best half the Tigers have played under Lane Kiffin.

Next up: an open date, then Alabama comes to Tiger Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7, time and TV to be announced. I'll be there at dawn with a pot big enough for the whole lot, and I'll feed the Alabama folks too. Hospitality is a Louisiana sacrament. They just won't enjoy dessert.

Laissez les bons temps rouler, and Geaux Tigers!

articles.title: From the Hedges to the Hangover: Auburn Comes Back to Earth Against LSU, 38-17
articles.byline: Lacey Bellamy, The Auburn Fanatic
articles.matchup: LSU 38, Auburn 17 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Jordan-Hare Stadium
articles.text:
Well, hey there, Auburn family. Lacey Bellamy here, back on the porch swing with a glass of sweet tea and, for the first time in a week, no toilet paper in my hair. A week ago we beat No. 1 Georgia between the hedges. Saturday, LSU came to Jordan-Hare and beat us 38-17. Football gives, and football takes back the casserole dish.

Here's how it slipped away. LSU scored on five of its six first-half possessions. We hung in for a while: Alex McPherson tied it 3-3 with a 23-yard field goal, and Byrum Brown punched in a 1-yard touchdown to make it 17-10. Then Jackson Harris caught a 12-yard crossing route and kept running for 70 yards and a touchdown, and Sam Leavitt scored on a 4-yard run with 17 seconds left in the half. Thirty-one to ten at the break. I set down my tea. I did not lift it again for a while.

The other killer was up front. Byrum ran for 115 yards against Georgia. LSU blitzed and spied him all day, and he finished with 21 rushing yards on 19 carries and got sacked six times. LSU outgained us 552 to 271. Honest is honest, y'all.

Heroes still showed up. Byrum completed 15 of 24 passes for 160 yards and didn't throw an interception while getting chased all over the Plains. Keshaun Singleton caught four passes for 64 yards. Tristan Ti'a came in and went 5 for 6 and ran for a 7-yard touchdown with 24 seconds left, because Auburn people don't quit early. Kaleb Harris made nine tackles. The goat, lovingly: our early-down run game, which never got off the porch.

What it means: Auburn is 4-3 and 2-3 in the SEC. Per the AP, it's the first time in Alex Golesh's debut season that we got blown out. Our other two league losses, to Florida and Tennessee, were close fights. One bad afternoon doesn't erase Athens. Nobody is giving that toilet paper back.

Next up: at Ole Miss on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 12:45 p.m. ET on SEC Network, our fourth straight ranked opponent. Halloween in Oxford. I'm going as a Tiger. I always go as a Tiger.

War Eagle, y'all. Swing's still swinging.

Heroes still showed up. Byrum completed 15 of 24 passes for 160 yards and didn't throw an interception while getting chased all over the Plains. Keshaun Singleton caught four passes for 64 yards. Tristan Ti'a came in and went 5 for 6 and ran for a 7-yard touchdown with 24 seconds left, because Auburn people don't quit early. Kaleb Harris made nine tackles. The goat, lovingly: our early-down run game, which never got off the porch.

What it means: Auburn is 4-3 and 2-3 in the SEC. Per the AP, it's the first time in Alex Golesh's debut season that we got blown out. Our other two league losses, to Florida and Tennessee, were close fights. One bad afternoon doesn't erase Athens. Nobody is giving that toilet paper back.
Next up: at Ole Miss on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 12:45 p.m. ET on SEC Network, our fourth straight ranked opponent. Halloween in Oxford. I'm going as a Tiger. I always go as a Tiger.
War Eagle, y'all. Swing's still swinging.

articles.title: Column D Stays Empty: Michigan Holds Indiana to 13 but Falls in Overtime at the Big House
articles.byline: Augustin 'Gus' Hartwell, The Michigan Fanatic
articles.matchup: Indiana 13, Michigan 6 (final, OT), Sat., Oct. 24, Michigan Stadium
articles.text:
I keep a spreadsheet, and every column is a lyric from "The Victors." Column D is "the champions." Saturday afternoon, after Indiana beat us 13-6 in overtime at the Big House, Column D stayed blank, and I spent a long time staring at an empty cell. Gus Hartwell here, maize sweater, heavy heart.

The defense deserves a standing ovation from all 111,276 of us. It held the No. 6 team in the country to two field goals in regulation. Chris Bracy made 13 tackles. Zeke Berry intercepted Josh Hoover and returned it 37 yards, setting up a Trey Butkowski field goal. Smith Snowden got a sack. That's engineering-grade work.

The offense? I ran the numbers twice, hoping for a rounding error. Michigan gained 224 yards and ran for 57. Tommy Carr, starting over Bryce Underwood, lost a fumble on a pitch in the first quarter and threw an interception in the second half. Sacks pushed us out of field-goal range twice, including once after we'd reached the Indiana 1, and we missed two kicks. In the final minute of regulation we got to the Indiana 3, Carr was sacked, and Butkowski tied it 6-6 with a 26-yarder as time expired.

Overtime: Indiana scored on a 4-yard Hoover run. We reached the 13, and Carr's last throw landed in front of Salesi Moa just outside the end zone. Spreadsheet closed. Coffee cold.

Hero: Bracy and the whole defense. Hall of fame effort in a loss. Goat, with all the love an engineer can compute: the red zone. Two trips that deep should equal at least one touchdown. The formula's broken. To his credit, Carr took the blame for both turnovers, and the AP notes he's the grandson of Lloyd Carr. That young man will have better days in this stadium.

What it means: Michigan is 4-3 and 1-3 in the Big Ten. Per the AP, every game this year except UTEP has come down to the last possession. Our cardiologist has asked for season tickets.

Next up: at Rutgers on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 12:30 p.m. ET on BTN. Halloween in Piscataway. I'm dressing as a touchdown so at least one shows up.

Hail to the Victors, even this week. Especially this week.

articles.title: Bucked Off in Cincinnati: Turnovers and Flags Throw Texas Tech, 37-24
articles.byline: Bodie Ratliff, The Texas Tech Fanatic
articles.matchup: Cincinnati 37, Texas Tech 24 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Nippert Stadium
articles.text:
Bodie Ratliff. Lubbock.

Got bucked off. Happens to every rider. Cincinnati 37, Texas Tech 24. First loss of the year.

Here's the ride, short version. We were up 6-3 after a quarter on two Stone Harrington field goals. Then the bronc turned. Cincinnati scored 21 in the second quarter. Three touchdown passes from JC French IV. The last one came after an interception, a 75-yard drive in 27 seconds. Twenty-four to six at the half. That's eight seconds on the clock and you're already in the dirt.

We got back on. Third quarter, Peyton Morgan intercepted a deflected pass and ran it back 53 yards for a touchdown. They flagged it for targeting, then video review overturned it. Score stood. Twenty-four to fifteen. Crowd went quiet. I like it quiet.

Then Cincinnati went 80 yards and scored again. Cole Tabb broke a 58-yard touchdown run with six minutes left. Tabb ran for 173 yards. That boy can ride.

Hero: Harrington, four field goals, long of 48. Morgan, the touchdown. Austin Romaine and Ben Roberts, 11 tackles each. A.J. Holmes Jr., a sack and a half. Kenny Johnson, seven catches for 81. J'Koby Williams busted a 42-yard run.

The goat, and I say it with respect: ball security. Three turnovers. Two lost fumbles, one interception. Three turnovers that led to points. And the yellow flags kept coming, a season high per the AP, from a team that's usually one of the least penalized in the country. You don't win a go-round with a loose rope.

What it means: 6-1, 3-1 in the Big 12. Dropped from No. 8 to No. 13 in the AP poll released Oct. 25. Last year we started 6-0, lost one, then won the rest, including the Big 12 title game, and made the Playoff. Same trail, per the AP. Coach McGuire says we have to win out. I agree. Short speech.

Next up: Arizona at Galaxy Stadium, Saturday, Oct. 31, noon ET, ESPN. Home. Halloween. Guns Up.

Tie the rope tighter. Ride again Saturday.

Bodie. Out.

articles.title: A Five-Way Afternoon: Cole Tabb Runs Wild as Cincinnati Stuns No. 8 Texas Tech 37-24
articles.byline: Lionel 'Skyline' Abernathy, The Cincinnati Fanatic
articles.matchup: Cincinnati 37, Texas Tech 24 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Nippert Stadium
articles.text:
Bearcats, it's Skyline, and I'm ordering a five-way. Everything on it. Extra cheese. Onions and beans. Cincinnati 37, No. 8 Texas Tech 24, at Nippert, on a Saturday that made the whole Clifton neighborhood shake. The AP says it's our first home win over a top-10 team since Nov. 18, 2006, when we beat No. 7 Rutgers. I've charted a lot of games. I've never charted a bigger bowl of chili.

Start with the spaghetti, the foundation: our second quarter. Down 6-3, JC French IV threw three touchdown passes in that quarter alone. Cole Tabb caught a 4-yarder. Malachi Henry caught a 5-yarder with 1:37 left. Then MJ Cannon intercepted Will Hammond, Tabb ripped off a 51-yard run, and French hit tight end Lyviel Waters for 2 yards with five seconds left. Seventy-five yards in 27 seconds. That's a three-way served before you can grab a napkin.

Then the cheese. Tech landed a punch in the third quarter, a 53-yard interception return for a touchdown, to make it 24-15. Nippert got nervous. So the Bearcats answered with a nine-play, 80-yard drive, and French hit Larenzo Fenner for 17 yards and his fourth touchdown pass, a career high. Onions on top.

And the beans: with about six minutes left, Cole Tabb ran 58 yards for a touchdown. Ballgame. Tabb finished with a career-best 173 rushing yards on 16 carries. Five-way, all day.

Hero: Tabb, obviously, and French, 19 of 30 with four touchdowns. Defense gets a big ladle too: Jasper Beeler had 11 tackles, Simeon Coleman had 10 with a sack, and we recovered two fumbles. The goat, lovingly: French's two interceptions, including the one Tech returned for a score. Nobody's perfect. Even chili drips on your shirt sometimes.

The engineer in me loves this note from the AP: we came in averaging 231 rushing yards, had minus-6 in the first quarter thanks to a couple of sacks, and still finished north of 250. That's called correcting the recipe mid-pot.

What it means: Cincinnati is 5-2 and 2-2 in the Big 12, and we earned votes in the AP poll released Oct. 25. A seat at the conference table again.

Next up: No. 6 Utah comes to Nippert on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3:45 p.m. ET on ESPN. Another ranked guest. I'll have the cheese grater ready.

Go Bearcats. Pass the oyster crackers.

articles.title: A Lotta Yikes, a Little N'at: Pitt Runs Into No. 1 Miami, Falls 52-23
articles.byline: Dominic 'Yinz' Bertolucci, The Pittsburgh Fanatic
articles.matchup: Miami 52, Pittsburgh 23 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Hard Rock Stadium
articles.text:
How's it goin', yinz? Dominic "Yinz" Bertolucci, back on my stool down the Strip, whistle around my neck, pierogi going cold. Miami 52, Pitt 23. We played the No. 1 team in the country in its house, and the house won. Coach Narduzzi called it a buzz saw. I'd call it a buzz saw with a jet engine on it.

Let me blow the whistle on how it got away. Miami scored on seven of its first eight possessions. That's a yikes. Malachi Toney caught 16 balls, a Miami school record. That's a double yikes with a side of fries. The real dagger came in the second quarter. Damon Ferguson Jr. ran in a 5-yard touchdown to make it 17-7, and I was up off the stool yellin'. Then Toney caught a 53-yard touchdown, and Miami added another score with 39 seconds left. Thirty-one to seven at the half. Stool, meet seat.

Now the yinz. Holden Geriner got the start at quarterback and threw for 268 yards. He found Blue Hicks, a Miami native, for a 36-yard touchdown in the third quarter. Blue finished with five catches for 149 yards in his hometown, which is a full-on, mill-town, lunch-pail yinz. Geriner also hit Hicks for 53 yards at the end of the half, but Blue got dragged down at the Miami 1 as time ran out. One yard, n'at.

More yinz: Jaeden Moore had two sacks. Cruce Brookins made nine tackles. Corey Dailey came in late and hit Cam Sapp for a 49-yard touchdown with 46 seconds left, because Pitt folks don't leave early. And we got a safety, two points, and I'll take two points.

The goat, and I say it with love like I'm talkin' to my brother-in-law: the run game. Sixty-nine yards on the ground. Gotta get that going, or we're throwin' into the wind all year.

What it means: Pitt is 5-3 and 2-3 in the ACC, losers of three straight. The AP notes Pitt is now 0-14-1 all-time against No. 1, so we've got company in our misery. No shame losing to this Miami team, but the time to turn it around is right now.

Next up: Georgia Tech comes to Acrisure Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 7:30 p.m. ET on ESPN2. Halloween under the lights at home. Wear gold, yinz.

Hail to Pitt. Whistle's dryin' out for next week.

articles.title: Throwbacks and Touchdowns: Malachi Toney's Record 16 Catches Power No. 1 Miami Past Pitt 52-23
articles.byline: Javi 'The Breeze' Castillo, The Miami Fanatic
articles.matchup: Miami 52, Pittsburgh 23 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Hard Rock Stadium
articles.text:
¡Wepa, familia! Javi "The Breeze" Castillo, linen shirt crisp, café cubano hot, and last week's double-overtime nerves finally cooled off. Miami 52, Pitt 23. First game at No. 1 in almost 24 years, and we played it like the old days. Throwback jerseys, swagger on blast, the scoreboard ran out of gas.

Let's talk about Malachi Toney, because the whole stadium did. Sixteen catches, a school record, for 194 yards and three touchdowns. He had 159 receiving yards at halftime, and the AP says that matched Pitt's whole offense for the half. Pitt brought a plan to slow him down. The plan got lost on the way to the Gables.

Play one: a 19-yard touchdown from Darian Mensah to Toney in the first quarter. Play two: Pitt cut it to 17-7, then Toney caught a 53-yarder to the house, and Mensah hit Gavin Mueller for 3 yards with 39 seconds left in the half. Thirty-one to seven. Play three: Mark Fletcher Jr. punched in a 2-yard run in the third quarter, the 33rd rushing touchdown of his career, now No. 2 on Miami's all-time list. Javian Mallory added two scores of his own. That's a lot of noise from the ground floor.

Hero: Toney, the record man. Close second: Mensah, 31 of 37 for 387 yards and four touchdowns, no interceptions. Miami scored on seven of its first eight drives, six touchdowns and a field goal. The goat, with love and a hug: our pass defense, which let Blue Hicks, a Miami native, catch five balls for 149 yards. Hometown kid, I'll forgive. Just this once, I'm feeling big.

The best part? Dozens of members of the 2001 national champions were in the building for their 25th anniversary, and they posed at midfield at halftime. Past and present, side by side. That is what tradition looks like when it shows up in person.

What it means: Miami is 7-0 and 5-0 in the ACC and stayed No. 1 in the AP poll released Oct. 25, ending a three-week run of top teams falling. Per the AP, Miami is now 43-6 all-time as the No. 1 team. Not bad for a balcony crew.

Next up: at North Carolina on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 7:30 p.m. ET on ABC. Halloween night in Chapel Hill. Our costume? The same as always. The team you fear most.

It's all about the U, and the U is all about you. Wepa!

articles.title: Back Past Exit 8A: Rutgers Loses Its Quarterback Early and Falls at Northwestern, 42-14
articles.byline: Vinny Scolari, The Rutgers Fanatic
articles.matchup: Northwestern 42, Rutgers 14 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Ryan Field
articles.text:
Yo. Vinny here.

Last week I was at Exit 9, windows down, joy in the cupholder. This week? I'm back at Exit 8A, where the anxiety lives, sitting in traffic behind a truck full of mattresses. Northwestern 42, Rutgers 14, in Evanston. Ugh.

The big one first, and it ain't a play. Dylan Lonergan, our starting quarterback, took a blow to the head on a scramble 6 minutes and 25 seconds into the game and didn't come back. Get well, kid. That's the only score I care about there.

After that, the turnpike got bumpy. Surace came in and drove us to a 43-yard Dane Pizzaro field goal. Seven to three, fine. Then the sack-fumble at our own 8, Northwestern recovered, and the Wildcats scored on the next snap. Twenty-one to three after one quarter. That's a toll booth with no E-ZPass lane.
