articles.title: Corrections Desk: Northwestern Beat Rutgers by 28, Not 18, and Aidan Chiles Did It Five Ways
articles.byline: Ezra Lindqvist, The Northwestern Fanatic
articles.matchup: Northwestern 42, Rutgers 14 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Ryan Field
articles.text:
Let me begin, as always, with a correction. Last week, I predicted Northwestern would beat Rutgers 37-19. The final was 42-14. My margin was off by 10 points, in the right direction. I'm retracting the prediction and keeping the smile. Ezra Lindqvist, Northwestern Fanatic, reporting from a press box of one.

The lede writes itself: Aidan Chiles had a hand in five touchdowns. He threw three, ran for two, and set a career high with 83 rushing yards. Per the AP, it's his second five-touchdown game this year. My editor would call that burying the lede. I'm putting it on top.

Key play one: the opening drive. Caleb Komolafe ripped off a 30-yard run, and Chiles hit Griffin Wilde for a 13-yard touchdown. Northwestern scored on its first three possessions, which the AP says is becoming a trademark. Key play two: with Rutgers backed up, a sack forced a fumble at the Rutgers 8. Jamaal Johnson recovered, and on the very next snap Chiles found Alex Honig for 8 yards. Twenty-one to three after one quarter. Key play three: Komolafe's 33-yard touchdown run with 1:46 left in the half. Twenty-eight to three. Story filed early.

Hero: Chiles, plus Komolafe with 150 yards on 13 carries, and Wilde with nine catches for 133 yards. The defense earns its own byline: four sacks, two interceptions, with Jalen Lewis and Montae Pate each getting one, and a fourth-down sack by Kobie McKinzie to stop a drive at our 7. Braydon Brus had 10 tackles. The goat, with a gentle red pen: our run defense, which let Antwan Raymond go for 150 yards and a 46-yard touchdown. Also, Chiles threw his first interception of the season. Even great writers need an editor.

A note of care: Rutgers quarterback Dylan Lonergan left in the first quarter after a blow to the head. We wish him a full and speedy recovery.

What it means: Northwestern is 6-1 for the first time since 2020, per the AP, and climbed to a tie for No. 20 in the poll released Oct. 25. Technically bowl-eligible. Coach David Braun isn't talking about that yet. Neither am I. Fine, I am a little.

Next up: at Oregon on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3:30 p.m. ET on Peacock. A Halloween trip to Autzen. I'll fact-check the ducks myself.

Go 'Cats. Correction to follow if needed.

articles.title: Four Pepperoni Rolls and One Big Stop: West Virginia Holds On at TCU, 24-20
articles.byline: Jolene Buckhannon, The West Virginia Fanatic
articles.matchup: West Virginia 24, TCU 20 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Amon G. Carter Stadium
articles.text:
Morning, Mountaineers. Jolene Buckhannon. Rifle team captain, retired. Short sentences only.

West Virginia 24, TCU 20. On the road. In Fort Worth. Take me home.

The pepperoni-roll tally: TCU fumbled four times, per the AP. Four rolls. We recovered two. I ate both. Then Chams Diagne intercepted a pass. That one's a roll with extra cheese.

Three shots decided it.

Shot one. Third quarter, TCU up 13-10. Michael Hawkins Jr. took off for 36 yards and a touchdown. Bullseye.

Shot two. TCU went back up 20-17. Hawkins answered. Thirteen-yard touchdown pass to Cam Cook with 11:28 left. Twenty-four to twenty. Reload.

Shot three. The big one. TCU drove the length of the field. Final minute. They reached our 14. David Afogho came through and hit Jaden Craig as he went to throw. Ball came loose. Ben Cutter fell on it. Thirty-four seconds left. Game over. I fired my imaginary rifle into the Texas sky. Safely. Into a hay bale.

Hero: Hawkins. Two rushing touchdowns, one passing. A Frisco kid, back in his home state. The AP says he turned down TCU out of high school. Good call, son. Cook ran for 90 yards in front of folks from back home too. Geimere Latimer II made 12 tackles and a sack. Afogho and Cutter split the game ball. They can share. It's a big ball.

The goat, with love: our passing game. Seven of 15 for 79 yards. We got outgained by more than 200 yards. TCU's defense is the stingiest in the Big 12, per the AP. Still. We'll work on it.

What it means: 5-3 overall. 2-3 in the Big 12. More wins than all of last season. A defense that got roughed up all year finally held when it counted. That's growth. Coach Rich Rodriguez wore an "Ike" cap to honor his late mentor, Ike Morris. Nice touch. Rest easy, Ike.

Next up: an open week on Oct. 31. Then at Texas Tech on Saturday, Nov. 7, at Galaxy Stadium. Time and TV to come. Three ranked opponents in our last four, per the AP. Load up.

Take me home, country roads. Let's go, Mountaineers.

Jolene. Out.

articles.title: A Steer Through the Gap: TCU's Last-Minute Fumble Hands West Virginia a 24-20 Win
articles.byline: Ryder Galloway, The TCU Fanatic
articles.matchup: West Virginia 24, TCU 20 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Amon G. Carter Stadium
articles.text:
Howdy from the Stockyards, Frog fans. Ryder Galloway, leaning on the fence rail, boots still dusty, shirt still pressed, heart in the dirt. West Virginia 24, TCU 20, at Amon G. Carter. A cattle drive that went right for miles and wrong at the gate.

Let's start with the drive I'll see in my sleep. Down four, final minute, Jaden Craig led us the length of the field. We were at the West Virginia 14 and I had my hat in the air. Then David Afogho came free, hit Craig as he went to throw, and the ball squirted loose. West Virginia's Ben Cutter fell on it with 34 seconds left. One steer through the gap, and the whole herd scattered.

That wasn't the only gap. TCU turned it over on downs at the West Virginia 20 in the fourth quarter and missed a 43-yard field goal in the second. And Michael Hawkins Jr., a Frisco kid who the AP says turned down TCU, ran for two touchdowns and threw for another. That's a cowboy who got away from the ranch.

Now, the good brands on the hide. Craig was terrific, 33 of 47 for 372 yards, and he completed his first 12 passes, the third-longest streak in school history. He went 8 for 8 on a 16-play opening drive that ended with a 6-yard touchdown to tight end Ka'Morreun Pimpton in the back corner. He also ran one in from 2 yards out. Kari Ashley caught six balls for 118 yards and Jordan Dwyer caught 10 for 113. Jamel Johnson made 11 tackles with a sack. We outgained West Virginia by more than 200 yards.

The goat, and I say it like I'd say it to my own ranch hand: ball security. Four fumbles, two lost, plus an interception. Three turnovers, and the last one cost us the game. Coach Sonny Dykes said we shot ourselves in the foot. Hard to argue with the boss.

What it means: TCU is 3-4 and 1-3 in the Big 12. Per the AP, the road team has won the last five in this series, so that's one more for the record book I'd rather burn. The herd needs to regroup fast.

Next up: Kansas comes to Fort Worth on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3:30 p.m. ET on FS1. Halloween at the Carter. Purple everywhere.

Riff ram, bah zee. Ride your lane, Frogs.

articles.title: Water Damage, Again: Baylor's Late Field Goal Blocked in a 25-24 Loss at Kansas
articles.byline: Maggie Whitlock, The Baylor Fanatic
articles.matchup: Kansas 25, Baylor 24 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium
articles.text:
Hey, y'all. Maggie Whitlock here, in the studio with my tape measure, a stack of paint swatches and a "Sic 'Em" throw pillow I'm currently hugging for emotional support. Kansas 25, Baylor 24, in Lawrence. We'd beaten the Jayhawks 14 straight times, per the AP. That streak just came down to the studs.

The final walkthrough, room by room. The foyer looked lovely: down 21-10 going into the fourth, the house was staged and ready to sell. Then Kansas hit a 34-yard touchdown pass on the first play of the quarter and a field goal. Rhett Armstrong gave us a 24-19 lead with a 42-yarder with 2:40 left. Fine. Curtains up.

Then the kitchen flooded. Kansas went 71 yards, and Isaiah Marshall ran it in from 15 yards out on fourth-and-6 with 1:13 left. Kansas went 5 for 8 on fourth down all day. That's a leak we never patched.

And the master bath: DJ Lagway got us to the Kansas 27 in the final minute. Our 45-yard field goal try got blocked by Blake Herold. Per the AP, Kansas had tipped two earlier kicks. Third one got through the drywall. I set the pillow down. I picked it back up.

The good bones, because there are good bones: Devon Jordan stepped in front of a pass to open the second half and returned it 42 yards for a touchdown. Gorgeous. Micah Gifford intercepted one too. Our defense got five sacks, Kyland Reed had one, and Travion Barnes made 13 tackles. Gavin Freeman caught nine passes for 123 yards. Lagway hit Jayden McGowan for an 8-yard touchdown, and McGowan's 51-yard kickoff return set up our first score.

The goat, with a gentle hand on the shoulder: the penalties. Twelve for 116 yards. You can't keep tracking mud across a white rug and expect it to look new.

What it means: Baylor is 4-3 and 2-2 in the Big 12. The Big 12 race is still open, but we've got some repairs to make, and fast.

Next up: a short week. Baylor plays at UCF on Friday, Oct. 30, at 7:30 p.m. ET on ESPN, at the Acrisure Bounce House in Orlando. I'm bringing a fresh swatch of green and gold for Halloween eve.

Sic 'em, Bears. We'll fix the leak.

articles.title: Blocked at the Buzzer: Kansas Snaps a 14-Game Skid Against Baylor, 25-24
articles.byline: Fitz Calloway, The Kansas Fanatic
articles.matchup: Kansas 25, Baylor 24 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium
articles.text:
Rock Chalk, everybody. Fitz Calloway here, and the spreadsheet has a new tab. It's called "Joy." Kansas 25, Baylor 24, in Lawrence. Our first Big 12 win of the year, and the end of a 14-game losing streak against Baylor. The last time we beat the Bears was 2007. In basketball terms, that's like missing 14 straight free throws and finally making one. With your eyes closed.

The comeback, in three possessions. First: down 21-10 to start the fourth quarter, Isaiah Marshall hit Nik McMillan for a 34-yard touchdown on the first play of the quarter. Martin Connington added a 42-yard field goal to make it 21-19. Baylor answered with a field goal of its own with 2:40 left. Twenty-four to nineteen.

Second: Marshall went 71 yards in six plays. On fourth-and-6, he took off and ran it in from 15 yards out with 1:13 left. In basketball terms, that's a four-point play from the logo. I knocked over my laptop. The spreadsheet survived.

Third: Baylor drove to our 27. The Bears lined up a 45-yard field goal. And tackle Blake Herold, who had gotten his hands on two earlier kicks, got the third one clean. Blocked. Ballgame. Herold, my friend, that's a rejection into the third row. Dikembe would wag his finger.

Hero: Herold, obviously. Plus Dylan Edwards, who ran for 156 yards on 30 carries without scoring. Thirty carries! That's a double-double in effort. Marshall accounted for three touchdowns, and Bruhn caught the first of his career. Bam Crouch had 10 tackles and a sack. And our fourth-down tab is glowing: 5 for 8 Saturday, 13 for 26 on the year, per the AP.

The goat, and I'd tell him to his face with a hug: the turnovers. Marshall threw two interceptions, and Devon Jordan returned one 42 yards for a touchdown to open the second half. That's a turnover leading straight to a fast break the other way.

What it means: Kansas is 3-4 and 1-3 in the Big 12, and a two-game slide is over. Coach Lance Leipold said the team needed a win like this. I needed it more. My spreadsheet needed it most.

Next up: at TCU on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3:30 p.m. ET on FS1. Halloween in Fort Worth. I'm going as a blocked kick.

Rock Chalk, Jayhawk. Spite and stats forever.

articles.title: Runway Malfunction: Oregon's Road Streak Ends in a 21-10 Loss at Illinois
articles.byline: Phoenix 'Nix' Wyatt-Aldana, The Oregon Fanatic
articles.matchup: Illinois 21, Oregon 10 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Gies Memorial Stadium
articles.text:
Hi, hello, welcome to the runway. Nix Wyatt-Aldana here, and normally I'd open with my uniform review. Not this week. This week, the outfit does not matter, because Illinois 21, Oregon 10, in Champaign. Per the AP, it's the Ducks' first Big Ten road loss since joining the conference in 2024. Ten straight, and the streak tripped on the catwalk.

The look started strong. Jordon Davison ran it in from 2 yards out in the first quarter, and Gage Hurych kicked a 20-yard field goal late in the second. Ten to nothing. Then, 14 seconds later on the game clock, Aidan Laughery ran 75 yards untouched for a touchdown. That's a heel snapping in the middle of the runway.

The second half was a wardrobe malfunction. Illinois scored on a fake-handoff pass early in the third to go up 14-10. Then Hurych, who was the reigning Big Ten special teams player of the week, missed from 52, from 52 again, and from 39 in the fourth quarter. Collin Dixon's diving 23-yard touchdown catch with 2:29 left ended the show. We outgained Illinois 426 to 314 and lost by 11. That's like designing a gorgeous sneaker and forgetting the laces.

Hero, styled with love: Dylan Raiola, 27 of 41 for 246 yards with no interceptions while throwing to a lot of new faces. Four of our top wide receivers didn't play, per the AP. Dakorien Moore caught nine passes for 70 yards. Davison ran for 92, and Dierre Hill Jr. added 83. Teitum Tuioti had two and a half sacks. The goat, with a gentle hug: the kicking game. Hurych is a great kicker having a rough night. We all have a bad hair day.

And we miss Dante Moore. He sat out a third straight game after a concussion against USC. Get healthy, QB1. The AP notes we've scored 39 points combined in the games he's missed.

What it means: Oregon is 4-3 and 2-2 in the Big Ten. Coach Dan Lanning said everyone needs to look within. Fashion advice I give daily: mirror first, then the runway.

Next up: Northwestern comes to Autzen Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3:30 p.m. ET on Peacock. Halloween in Eugene, the one night a year everybody's in costume. We need a Ducks look that wins.

Sko Ducks. The runway resets Saturday.

articles.title: Class Is in Session: Aidan Laughery's 75-Yard Dash and a Diving Catch Lift Illinois Over Oregon, 21-10
articles.byline: Margery Vandermolen, The Illinois Fanatic
articles.matchup: Illinois 21, Oregon 10 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Gies Memorial Stadium
articles.text:
Good morning, class. Pencils out, slide rules up. Margery Vandermolen here, notes color-coded orange and blue, and today's lesson is called "How to Beat Oregon." Illinois 21, Oregon 10, at Gies Memorial Stadium. Per the AP, the Ducks had won 10 straight Big Ten road games since joining the conference in 2024. Consider that streak graded and returned.

Our first problem set was unpleasant. Down 10-0 late in the first half, Illinois had gained 43 yards. Forty-three! My father's slide rule computed that as "concerning." Then, with 2:15 left in the half, Aidan Laughery took a handoff and ran 75 yards for a touchdown. Untouched. Nobody laid a finger on him. Ten to seven. The whole class sat up straight.

Lesson two: early in the third quarter, freshman Michael Clayton II faked the handoff and hit Christian Abney for a 9-yard touchdown. Fourteen to ten. Illinois never trailed again. Clayton, per the AP, is just the sixth freshman to start at quarterback in program history, filling in for Katin Houser and his broken hand. A big shiny sticker for poise.

The final exam: with 2:29 left, Clayton threw to the corner of the end zone and Collin Dixon laid out for a diving 23-yard touchdown catch. Coach Bret Bielema said he had no idea how Dixon made that catch. Neither do I, and I have a slide rule.

Hero: Laughery, 123 rushing yards on 13 carries. Dixon, six catches for 65 yards. And the defense, which kept Oregon out of the end zone after the first quarter. James Kreutz made nine tackles. Oregon gained 426 yards and scored 10 points. Bend, but never break. That's proper agricultural engineering: let the wind blow the corn sideways, just never let it hit the ground.

The goat, gently, in red pencil: our passing yardage, 89 yards. And a lost fumble. We'll practice the times tables.

What it means: Illinois is 4-3 and 2-2 in the Big Ten, and beat the Ducks in Champaign. Bielema loved the quarterback rotation with Carson Boyd. I'd call it a passing grade with honors.

Next up: at Maryland on Saturday, Oct. 31, at noon ET on FS1. A Halloween field trip. Permission slips are due Friday.

Class dismissed. Oskee-wow-wow, Illini!

articles.title: The Court Rules for the Ground Game: Boston College Runs for 399 Yards in a 49-27 Rout at Georgia Tech
articles.byline: Siobhan Dunleavy, The Boston College Fanatic
articles.matchup: Boston College 49, Georgia Tech 27 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Bobby Dodd Stadium
articles.text:
All rise. The Court of Siobhan Dunleavy is now in session, and I find the defendant, Georgia Tech, guilty on all counts of being run over. Boston College 49, Georgia Tech 27, in Atlanta. Wicked good. Case closed. Actually, no, I love the sound of my own gavel. Let's review the evidence.

Exhibit A: the slow start. Georgia Tech scored on its first two possessions and led 10-0. The Court was displeased. For the second straight week, BC fell behind by double digits early, then rallied, just like the 27-21 win over Pitt. I'd like the record to show I am too old for this.

Exhibit B: the third quarter. Trailing 13-12 at halftime, the Eagles scored touchdowns on their first two possessions after the break. Mason McKenzie faked the handoff up the middle and ran 40 yards right down the Georgia Tech sideline. Bo MacCormack III punched in a 2-yarder to take the lead for good. Then Charlie Comella intercepted a deflected pass, and McKenzie ran it in from the 6. Objection overruled, Atlanta.

Exhibit C: the dagger. Up 35-20 in the fourth, Comella intercepted his second pass of the day and returned it 47 yards for a touchdown. The jury gasped. The jury is me. I gasped.

Hero: the ground game. Three hundred ninety-nine rushing yards. McKenzie ran for 170 and two touchdowns and threw a 25-yard touchdown to Nedrick Boldin Jr. MacCormack ran for 155 yards and three scores, which, per the AP, is more than he had in his previous 13 career games combined. He filled in for Evan Dickens, who was hurt against Pitt and is reportedly out for the season. Get well, Evan. And Comella, two interceptions and a touchdown. Anthony Palano made nine tackles.

The goat, sentenced to community service: the kicking game. One missed field goal and two missed extra points. Practice your PATs, gentlemen. That's a court order.

What it means: BC is 4-3 and 2-2 in the ACC, already doubling the two wins from last year's 2-10 season, and two wins from bowl eligibility. The Court finds this program officially un-dismissed.

Next up: at Duke on Saturday, Oct. 31, at noon ET on The CW. Halloween in Durham. I'll be wearing my robe, which is also my costume.

Court adjourned. Ever to Excel, and go Eagles!

articles.title: Failed Experiment: Boston College Runs Over Georgia Tech on Homecoming, 49-27
articles.byline: Wendell Quist, The Georgia Tech Fanatic
articles.matchup: Boston College 49, Georgia Tech 27 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Bobby Dodd Stadium
articles.text:
Greetings, Jackets. Wendell Quist reporting, mechanical pencil behind my ear, graph paper on the desk and a lab notebook I'd rather not show anybody this week. Boston College 49, Georgia Tech 27, at Bobby Dodd on homecoming. Hypothesis: we contain the run. Result: rejected. Emphatically.

The early data was promising. Georgia Tech scored on its first two possessions. Alberto Mendoza completed a 43-yard pass, ran for 27 more and threw a 4-yard touchdown to Kevin Roche Jr. Aidan Birr added a 32-yard field goal. Ten to nothing. I drew a beautiful upward curve on my graph.

Then the variables changed. Boston College ran the same couple of plays over and over, and we never solved the equation. The Eagles scored on their first two possessions of the second half, including a 40-yard Mason McKenzie run off a fake up the middle. Then a deflected pass turned into an interception, and BC scored again. The decisive vector came in the fourth quarter. Down 35-20, Mendoza's pass was intercepted by Charlie Comella and returned 47 yards for a touchdown. That's a trajectory I didn't want to plot.

The full dataset: Boston College ran for 399 yards. McKenzie had 170 and Bo MacCormack III had 155. Physics, my friends, is about force and mass. Their mass kept generating force. Our tackling did not.

Positive results, recorded honestly: Birr made both his field goals and all three extra points. Dalen Penson caught five passes for 88 yards, including a 30-yard touchdown from sophomore Grady Adamson, who went 7 of 9 for 73 yards. Jordan Allen had four catches for 85. Chris Hewitt Jr. made 10 tackles. Justice Haynes scored from 15 yards out. The goat, with empathy: the run defense. That's where the experiment failed.

What it means: Georgia Tech is 2-5 and 1-3 in the ACC. Per the AP, after an 8-0 start in 2025, the Jackets have lost nine of their last 12. The homecoming crowd let its feelings be known. Coach Brent Key said what we're doing isn't working, across the board. Good scientists accept the data and redesign the experiment.

Next up: at Pitt on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 7:30 p.m. ET on ESPN2. Halloween night at Acrisure Stadium. New trial, new variables, same pencil.

Adjust, retest and rerun. I'm a Ramblin' Wreck from Georgia Tech, and a hopeful engineer. Go Jackets.

articles.title: Wrong Pitch Calls: Undermanned Michigan State Grabs an Early Lead, Then Falls at UCLA 28-10
articles.byline: Shay Kowalczyk, The Michigan State Fanatic
articles.matchup: UCLA 28, Michigan State 10 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Rose Bowl
articles.text:
Alright, gear on. Mask down. Squat. Shay Kowalczyk here, knees crackling like a bowl of cereal, and I'm giving it to you straight from behind the plate. UCLA 28, Michigan State 10, at the Rose Bowl. Six straight losses now. My knees hurt. My heart hurts more.

But first, the inning we won. UCLA fumbled in the first quarter, and Devin Vaught scooped it and took off 56 yards. A few plays later, Kayd Coffman, a third-string quarterback making his first career start, threw a 14-yard touchdown to Kenneth Williams. Seven to nothing, Spartans, in the Rose Bowl. I stood up so fast my shin guards rattled.

Then the pitch calls went wrong. UCLA tied it, went ahead 14-7, and then the big one: on the first drive of the third quarter, Ty Dieffenbach threw a 63-yard touchdown to Brian Rowe Jr. Coach Pat Fitzgerald pointed to that big play to open the half, and he was right. That's a hanging changeup. UCLA scored again for 28-7. In the second and third quarters, UCLA outgained us 280 to 13, per the AP. That's no-hitter territory, from the wrong dugout.

Hero: Vaught, with a fumble recovery, the long return and eight tackles. Nikai Martinez also made eight tackles and recovered a fumble. Coffman got his first career touchdown pass in his first career start, which is a memory nobody can take away. Liam Boyd hit a 46-yard field goal. Leo Hannan came in for the fourth quarter and kept battling.

The goat, with a hand on the shoulder, catcher to pitcher: the offense, 156 yards of offense and 47 on the ground. But honestly, look at the injury list. The Spartans were already without their top two running backs, per the AP. Then Marvis Parrish got hurt on the third play of the game and had to be helped off. Prayers to Marvis. You don't throw a gem with half your staff in the trainer's room.

What it means: Michigan State is 2-6 and 0-5 in the Big Ten, and 0-3 against ranked teams. The open week couldn't come at a better time. Ice the knees. Heal up.

Next up: an open date on Oct. 31, then at Michigan on Saturday, Nov. 7, time and TV to be announced. Rivalry week. Nothing heals like that.

Mask up. Go Green! Go White!

articles.title: Seven Index Cards, Seven W's: UCLA Shakes Off a Slow Open to Beat Michigan State 28-10
articles.byline: Kensington 'Kenzie' Rhee, The UCLA Fanatic
articles.matchup: UCLA 28, Michigan State 10 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Rose Bowl
articles.text:
Okay, everybody, settle in, phones on silent. Thank you for taking this meeting. Kenzie Rhee here, and I have news for the corkboard: card number seven says W. UCLA 28, Michigan State 10, at the Rose Bowl. The Bruins are 7-0 for the first time since 2005, per the AP. My landlord has described the corkboard as "a lot." It is now "a lot, plus one."

Act one was a rough cut. We fumbled, Michigan State's Devin Vaught scooped it up and ran 56 yards, and the Spartans scored on a 14-yard pass to go up 7-0. First time we'd trailed in two weeks. I put my head in my hands. My index cards fluttered.

Then the montage. Jaivian Thomas ran 7 yards to tie it. Wayne Knight plunged in from the 1 for his 12th rushing touchdown of the season, per the AP. Fourteen to seven at the half.

articles.title: Banjo Out of Tune: Tennessee Loses on a Final-Play Field Goal at South Carolina, 27-24
articles.byline: Earl 'Rocky Top' Haskew, The Tennessee Fanatic
articles.matchup: South Carolina 27, Tennessee 24 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Williams-Brice Stadium
articles.text:
Plink-a-plink... plunk. That's my banjo, friends, and this week a string snapped. Earl "Rocky Top" Haskew, out on the cabin porch, staring at the Smokies and trying to make sense of it. South Carolina 27, Tennessee 24, on a field goal with no time left. Last week we whipped Alabama. This week the song ended on a sour note.

It started flat. South Carolina led 14-0 after a quarter. Then the Vols found the melody. DeSean Bishop ran one in from a yard out. DaSaahn Brame ran one in from a yard out. And with 24 seconds left in the half, Mike Matthews scored on an 8-yard run. Twenty-one to seventeen. Cooper Ranvier made it 24-17 with a 37-yard field goal in the fourth.

Then three notes I'd like to un-play. First: up seven, fourth-and-1 at the South Carolina 39 with 3:35 left, we went for it, and MacIntyre got stuffed. Second: LaNorris Sellers stretched the ball to the pylon with 1:17 left to tie it. Third: with 33 seconds left, MacIntyre got strip-sacked, South Carolina recovered, and Malik Orsan hit a 48-yarder as time expired. Their fans stormed the field. I stormed back inside for some sweet tea.

And the penalties. Per the AP, three Tennessee touchdowns came off the board on flags, including two Braylon Staley scoring catches, one from 35 yards and one from 18. That's a whole verse of a song, erased.

Hero: Bishop, a workhorse, 32 carries for 120 yards and a touchdown. Matthews caught five passes and scored. Staley caught six for 56, and he deserves those touchdowns in spirit. Dejuan Lane made eight tackles, Amare Campbell had a sack, and TJ Metcalf intercepted Sellers. Ranvier was perfect. The goat, with a gentle pat: the flag count, which coach Josh Heupel and the whole team will be working on.

What it means: Tennessee is 6-2 and 3-2 in the SEC and fell from No. 11 to No. 16 in the AP poll released Oct. 25. The AP notes it's the Vols' second straight loss at Williams-Brice. Still a lot of football left, and a big one coming.

Next up: an open date, then Kentucky comes to Neyland Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7, time and TV to be announced. Checkerboard end zones, a whole stadium singing. Can't wait.

Rocky Top, you'll always be home sweet home to me. Go Vols.

articles.title: Walk-Off at Williams-Brice: Sellers Stretches, Stewart Strips, Orsan Drills It as South Carolina Stuns No. 11 Tennessee
articles.byline: Beaumont 'Beau' Cheraw, The South Carolina Fanatic
articles.matchup: South Carolina 27, Tennessee 24 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Williams-Brice Stadium
articles.text:
Bum. Bum. Bum. BUMMMMM. Beau Cheraw here, former drumline snare, and my sticks are still vibrating. South Carolina 27, No. 11 Tennessee 24, on a 48-yard Malik Orsan field goal as time ran out. Fans poured onto the field. I poured onto the field. I may still be on the field.

Let's play it back, measure by measure. The intro was gorgeous: LaNorris Sellers threw a 17-yard touchdown to Mazeo Bennett Jr. and ran 31 yards for another. Fourteen to nothing, first quarter. Then the tempo dragged. Tennessee scored 21 in the second quarter, added a field goal, and led 24-17 in the fourth.

The bridge: Tennessee went for it on fourth-and-1 at our 39 with 3:35 left, and our defense stuffed MacIntyre. I hit a rimshot on my car's dashboard.

The crescendo: third-and-goal, 1:17 left. Sellers took on two defenders, stayed on his feet and stretched the ball to the pylon. Review upheld it. Tied 24-24. I lost a drumstick in the stands. Then, with 33 seconds left, Dylan Stewart came around the corner and stripped MacIntyre, and Tomiwa Durojaiye fell on it. We ran the clock to three seconds, and Orsan drilled it. BUMMMMM.

Hero: Sellers, 18 of 32 for 210 yards and a touchdown, plus 96 rushing yards and two scores. Stewart and Durojaiye for the play of the year. Orsan, 2 for 2 with the winner. Fred Johnson made 14 tackles, and Justin Okoronkwo added 10. Bennett caught six passes for 88 yards. The goat, with a gentle cymbal crash: the middle two quarters, when Tennessee outscored us 21-3. We'll fix the tempo in rehearsal.

The sweetest note: per the AP, one of coach Shane Beamer's first moves after the game was hugging his father, Frank Beamer, who just turned 80. Happy birthday, Coach. Hope you liked the present.

What it means: South Carolina is 4-3 and 2-3 in the SEC, and the AP notes this follows a win at then-No. 16 Florida two weeks ago. After a three-game skid, the Gamecocks have their swagger back, and earned votes in the AP poll released Oct. 25.

Next up: at Oklahoma on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 4:15 p.m. ET on SEC Network. Halloween in Norman. I'll bring the snare.

Forever to Thee, and go Gamecocks! Bum. Bum. Bum. BUMMMMM.

articles.title: Floyd Walks Away: Iowa Ties It Late but Falls at Minnesota on a Final-Play Field Goal, 13-10
articles.byline: Orrin Kalvelage, The Iowa Fanatic
articles.matchup: Minnesota 13, Iowa 10 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Huntington Bank Stadium
articles.text:
Pull up a chair on the porch. The one with the cushion. Coffee's in the pot, and I'm going to need a second cup. Orrin Kalvelage here, same black-and-gold sweater as always. Minnesota 13, Iowa 10, on a field goal as time expired, and Floyd of Rosedale is headed north. That bronze pig always did like a road trip. I just wish he'd stayed home.

It got away from us one turnover at a time. Iowa came in with three turnovers all season. Saturday, we threw three interceptions and lost a fumble, and gave up a blocked punt right off the bat. Coach Kirk Ferentz said you can't expect to win a conference game like that, and nobody on this porch is arguing.

Then a penalty stung. In the third quarter, Iowa stopped Minnesota on fourth down, but an offside flag gave the Gophers another chance, and Darius Taylor scored on the next play. Ten to three.

Now, the part I'll tell the grandkids. Down seven, Hank Brown went 98 yards in four plays, and hit Reece Vander Zee for a 37-yard touchdown with 3:46 left. Tied, 10-10. I stood up and the dog barked. Then Minnesota hit a 39-yard pass on third down, and Luke Drzewiecki made it from 46 with no time left. The dog lay back down. So did I.

Hero: the defense, which held Minnesota to 209 yards of offense, the Gophers' season low. Zach Lutmer made 11 tackles, Cam Buffington had 10, Bryce Hawthorne had three tackles for loss, and Deshaun Lee intercepted a pass. Caden Buhr made his field goal. Vander Zee caught four for 69 yards, and Tony Diaz broke a 57-yard catch. The goat, said gently: the run game, 90 yards. And we wish Kamari Moulton well. He left in the second quarter with an injury.

What it means: Iowa is 5-2 and 2-2 in the Big Ten and dropped out of the AP poll released Oct. 25. The quarterback question isn't settled, and the AP says the Playoff hopes took a hit. But I've been on this porch through worse harvests.

Next up: Wisconsin comes to Kinnick Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at noon ET on Fox. We'll turn around and wave to the kids at the children's hospital after the first quarter, like always. That never loses.

Go Hawks. Same sweater next week.

articles.title: Floyd Comes Home: Luke Drzewiecki's Walk-Off Kick Beats No. 15 Iowa, 13-10
articles.byline: Torvald 'Tor' Engebretsen, The Minnesota Fanatic
articles.matchup: Minnesota 13, Iowa 10 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Huntington Bank Stadium
articles.text:
Well, hi there. Come on in, take your boots off, the rug's new and so is the pig. Tor Engebretsen here, hotdish in the oven, and Floyd of Rosedale is coming home to Minnesota. Gophers 13, No. 15 Iowa 10, on a 46-yard field goal as time expired. First time we've had Floyd since 2023, per the AP. Grandpa would've driven the truck straight onto the lake to celebrate, after checking the ice, of course.

Here's how the ice held. Minnesota blocked a punt early, and Luke Drzewiecki hit a 31-yard field goal in the first quarter. Then, in the third quarter, Iowa thought it had stopped us on fourth down, but the Hawkeyes jumped offside. Next play, Darius Taylor ran it in from a yard out. Ten to three.

Iowa tied it with 3:46 left on a 37-yard touchdown pass. My coffee went cold in the thermos. Then the play: third down, 39 seconds left, at our own 33. Drake Lindsey threw deep, Jalen Smith went up and got it for 39 yards. Then Drzewiecki, who joined us in August from New Mexico, lined up from 46 and drilled it. Twelve for 12 on the year. That young man is as reliable as a good ice auger.

Hero: the defense. Coach P.J. Fleck called it one of the best defensive performances he's been around here. Joey Gerlach, TJ Bush Jr. and Matt Kingsbury each intercepted a pass. Zack Harden made 12 tackles and a sack, and John Nestor had 11. Iowa came in averaging 194 rushing yards and got 90. Through three quarters, the Hawkeyes had just 163 yards of offense. The goat, said kindly over a second helping: our offense, 209 yards, a season low. But the hotdish doesn't have to be fancy if it fills you up.

What it means: Minnesota is 5-2 and 2-2 in the Big Ten, and earned votes in the AP poll released Oct. 25. And now, folks, gather close: per the AP, the Gophers hold Floyd of Rosedale, the Little Brown Jug and Paul Bunyan's Axe at the same time for the first time since 1978. The trophy case is full. Grandpa would need a bigger shelf. And no, it is not a pitcher.

Next up: at No. 4 Indiana on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS. Halloween in Bloomington. Bundle up, and bring Floyd's good luck along.

Ski-U-Mah, and Rah, rah, rah for Minnesota!

articles.title: A Tough Switchback: No. 2 BYU Falls at UCF in Double Overtime, 39-31
articles.byline: Bryce Halvorsen-Tuilagi, The BYU Fanatic
articles.matchup: UCF 39, BYU 31 (final, 2OT), Sat., Oct. 24, Acrisure Bounce House
articles.text:
Oh my heck, Cougar Nation. Bryce Halvorsen-Tuilagi here, on the trail up Y Mountain, where the view is fantastic and the Wi-Fi is not, and this week, neither is my mood. UCF 39, BYU 31, in double overtime. Our first loss of the season. Every great ride has a nasty switchback, and Saturday in Orlando was the steepest one.

Bear Bachmeier and Kyler Kasper had us climbing early. Bachmeier hit Kasper for a 27-yard touchdown in the first quarter, and Kasper finished with six catches for 129 yards. Bachmeier ran one in too, and Sione Moa punched in a third-quarter score. When UCF went ahead 24-21, Matthias Dunn drilled a 47-yarder to tie it in the fourth.

Then the ending, which the UCF coach called the weirdest he'd ever seen. Our defense stopped a fourth-and-goal sneak at the 1. Then, after a replay overturned a sack and a flag moved UCF into range, our special teams blocked a 47-yard field goal and time ran out. Overtime! I nearly rode off the trail.

In the first overtime, Bachmeier found Legend Glasker for 28 yards and the lead. UCF tied it on one play. In the second, UCF scored and converted the two. We needed eight and drove to the UCF 4, but the fourth-down pass to Walker Lyons fell incomplete. Brake pads, fully worn.

Hero: Kasper, the big-play man. Bachmeier threw for 257 yards and two touchdowns. Cade Uluave made 10 tackles, and Justin Kirkland had a sack. The goat, offered with a fist bump: the defense on third down, where UCF converted nine times, and coach Kalani Sitake said UCF put us on our heels. He gave them full credit. That's how we do it in Provo.

What it means: BYU is 6-1 and 3-1 in the Big 12 and slid from No. 2 to No. 8 in the AP poll released Oct. 25. But here's the good news, from the AP: a Big 12 title and a Playoff spot are still within reach. Kasper said it's still right there if we win out. Why did the Cougar bring a map to practice? Because the path is still clear. That's a dad joke, and it counts double.

Next up: Arizona State at LaVell Edwards Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3:30 p.m. ET on Fox, then a trip to Utah on Nov. 7. Holy War season is coming.

Rise and shout, the Cougars are out!

Bear Bachmeier and Kyler Kasper had us climbing early. Bachmeier hit Kasper for a 27-yard touchdown in the first quarter, and Kasper finished with six catches for 129 yards. Bachmeier ran one in too, and Sione Moa punched in a third-quarter score. When UCF went ahead 24-21, Matthias Dunn drilled a 47-yarder to tie it in the fourth.

Then the ending, which the UCF coach called the weirdest he'd ever seen. Our defense stopped a fourth-and-goal sneak at the 1. Then, after a replay overturned a sack and a flag moved UCF into range, our special teams blocked a 47-yard field goal and time ran out. Overtime! I nearly rode off the trail.

In the first overtime, Bachmeier found Legend Glasker for 28 yards and the lead. UCF tied it on one play. In the second, UCF scored and converted the two. We needed eight and drove to the UCF 4, but the fourth-down pass to Walker Lyons fell incomplete. Brake pads, fully worn.

Hero: Kasper, the big-play man. Bachmeier threw for 257 yards and two touchdowns. Cade Uluave made 10 tackles, and Justin Kirkland had a sack. The goat, offered with a fist bump: the defense on third down, where UCF converted nine times, and coach Kalani Sitake said UCF put us on our heels. He gave them full credit. That's how we do it in Provo.

What it means: BYU is 6-1 and 3-1 in the Big 12 and slid from No. 2 to No. 8 in the AP poll released Oct. 25. But here's the good news, from the AP: a Big 12 title and a Playoff spot are still within reach. Kasper said it's still right there if we win out. Why did the Cougar bring a map to practice? Because the path is still clear. That's a dad joke, and it counts double.
Next up: Arizona State at LaVell Edwards Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3:30 p.m. ET on Fox, then a trip to Utah on Nov. 7. Holy War season is coming.
Rise and shout, the Cougars are out!

In the second overtime, needing a touchdown and a two-point conversion, BYU reached the UCF 4 before a fourth-down pass fell incomplete.
BYU fell from No. 2 to No. 8 in the Oct. 25 AP poll and hosts Arizona State on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3:30 p.m. ET on Fox, then visits Utah on Nov. 7.

articles.title: Please Remain Seated... Never Mind: UCF Knocks Off No. 2 BYU in Double Overtime, 39-31
articles.byline: Knox Brevard-Stiles, The UCF Fanatic
articles.matchup: UCF 39, BYU 31 (final, 2OT), Sat., Oct. 24, Acrisure Bounce House
articles.text:
Welcome to the Bounce House, everybody! Knox Brevard-Stiles, theme-park ride designer, and my ride-safety gauge just filed a formal complaint. UCF 39, No. 2 BYU 31, in double overtime. Per the AP, it's the first win over a top-5 team in school history. The stands moved. The goalpost moved, too, straight off its base, as the fans stormed the field. Please keep your hands and arms inside the... oh, forget it.

This ride had more loops than anything I've designed. Five lead changes in regulation. Late in the fourth, tied 24-24, we got stopped on a fourth-and-goal sneak at the 1. Then the defense forced a three-and-out, and we got the ball back with 42 seconds left. Keyone Jenkins lost the ball on what was ruled a sack, but replay turned it into an incomplete pass, and BYU drew an unsportsmanlike flag. Then BYU blocked Will Stone's 47-yarder, Stone's helmet came off on the play, and the clock ran out. Coach Scott Frost called it the weirdest ending he'd ever seen. As a professional, I'd have to agree.

Overtime, loop one: BYU scored on a 28-yard pass. Jenkins answered on a single play, 25 yards to Josh Derry. Loop two: Jenkins found tight end Grayson Brousseau for the touchdown, then hit Tyren Hornes for two. BYU needed eight and drove to our 4, but Bear Bachmeier's fourth-down pass fell incomplete. Ride complete. Exit through the gift shop.

Hero: Jenkins, 25 of 41 for 293 yards, three touchdowns and a rushing score in his fifth start filling in for the injured Alonza Barnett III. Frost said our backup is not a backup, and I'd put that on a T-shirt. Hornes caught six passes for 137 yards. Duke Watson ran for 94 yards. Tackett Curtis intercepted a pass, and Jayden Williams made eight tackles. The goat, said gently: that fourth-and-goal sneak, which Frost said should have won it in regulation. But then we wouldn't have had the bonus loops.

What it means: UCF is 4-3 and 2-2 in the Big 12. Per the AP, this is Frost's signature win of his second stint, and our first win over a ranked team since 2023. BYU dropped from No. 2 to No. 8.

Next up: Baylor at the Bounce House on Friday, Oct. 30, at 7:30 p.m. ET on ESPN. Friday night under the lights. Bring earplugs.

Charge On, and Go Knights!

articles.title: Boomer in Starkville: John Mateer Throws Two Touchdowns as Oklahoma Beats Mississippi State, 23-15
articles.byline: Savannah Redbird-Lowe, The Oklahoma Fanatic
articles.matchup: Oklahoma 23, Mississippi State 15 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Davis Wade Stadium
articles.text:
Boomer!

I said, BOOMER!

Savannah Redbird-Lowe here, and yes, I yelled it in Starkville, and yes, about 49,000 Bulldog fans and their cowbells answered back. Oklahoma 23, Mississippi State 15. A road win in the SEC, and I'll take it with both hands and a Schooner ride.

The game turned right before halftime. We led 3-0 on a Tate Sandell field goal when Mississippi State drove to our 6. Then the Bulldogs fumbled, and we recovered. And the Sooners went 96 yards in 14 plays, capped by John Mateer's 36-yard touchdown pass to Isaiah Sategna III. Ten-nothing at the half. Boomer.

Then, three plays into the third quarter, Mateer hit Rocky Beers up the middle for 32 yards. Seventeen-nothing. Sooner.

Hero: Mateer, 22 of 29 for 283 yards and two touchdowns, plus 37 rushing yards. Coach Brent Venables called it an excellent game, and I called it into my neighbor's voicemail. Sategna caught eight passes for 164 yards. And the run game? Per the AP, we came in averaging 92.5 rushing yards a game and ran for 184. Tory Blaylock broke a 47-yarder. On defense, Owen Heinecke made 10 tackles and a sack, David Stone had a sack and a half, Peyton Bowen intercepted a pass, and Taylor Wein recovered a fumble.

The goat, with a big hug: Sandell went 3 for 6 on field goals, and the Bulldogs made it 23-15 with 2:10 left on a 42-yard touchdown and a two-point conversion. Venables said it probably should have been a bigger win. But then we converted back-to-back third downs and ran out the clock, and that's the grown-up way to finish.

What it means: Oklahoma is 4-3 and 2-2 in the SEC, and per the AP, the defense flexed its muscle once again. We wish Mississippi State's quarterback, Kamario Taylor, well after he left in the first quarter.

Next up: South Carolina comes to Memorial Stadium in Norman on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 4:15 p.m. ET on SEC Network. Halloween in Norman. The Sooner Schooner will be dressed up. So will I.

Boomer Sooner! Boomer Sooner! Boomer Sooner!

articles.title: Cowbell's Quiet, Not Silent: Mississippi State Rallies Late but Falls to Oklahoma, 23-15
articles.byline: Wade Pettus, The Mississippi State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Oklahoma 23, Mississippi State 15 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Davis Wade Stadium
articles.text:
Well. Evenin', folks. Wade Pettus here, on the tailgate of my truck outside the feed store, with a stack of receipts I drew plays on all week and a cowbell in my lap. Oklahoma 23, Mississippi State 15. Third straight loss. The bell's been quiet since Saturday. Not silent, mind you. Quiet.

Here's how it slipped. Right before halftime, Puckett drove us to Oklahoma's 6, and we fumbled on the next play. The Sooners went 96 yards the other way, and it was 10-0 at the half. Then they scored three plays into the third quarter. Seventeen to nothing. Coach Jeff Lebby said the Sooners' chunk plays were the difference, and the receipts agree. Per the AP, five passing plays of 15 yards or more made up 191 of Oklahoma's passing yards.

But listen. Then we got fun. Two trick plays back to back, the second one tight end Sam West throwing 18 yards to Camden Capehart for a touchdown. Per the AP, our first touchdown in eight quarters. I rang that bell till the feed store manager came outside. Then, with 2:10 left, Puckett found Sanfrisco Magee for 42 yards and a touchdown, then hit him again for the two. Twenty-three to fifteen. One possession. Oklahoma converted two third downs and ran it out, but we made 'em sweat.

Hero: Fluff Bothwell, 17 carries for 111 yards, and the name alone deserves a bronze statue. Puckett, 17 of 24 for 158 and a touchdown, stepping in. Tyler Lockhart and Fatt Forrest made 10 tackles each, Jaray Bledsoe had a sack, and Kendel Dolby recovered a fumble. The goat, said with love: third down, where we went 1 for 11. That's a receipt I'm tearing up.

And we're thinking of Kamario Taylor, who left in the first quarter after a hit. Lebby said they'd know more early in the week.

What it means: Mississippi State is 4-3 and 2-3 in the SEC. The season isn't over, and the bell is still in my lap.

Next up: at No. 11 Texas on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 7:30 p.m. ET on ESPN. Halloween night in Austin. Bring the bells. All of 'em.

Hail State, and ring 'em loud.

articles.title: Howdy, Heartache: Texas A&M Leads Into the Fourth but Falls at Alabama, 31-20
articles.byline: Colt Wendeborn, The Texas A&M Fanatic
articles.matchup: Alabama 31, Texas A&M 20 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Bryant-Denny Stadium
articles.text:
HOWDY! That's not me yelling, friend. That's the official greeting, and I'll say it even this week. Colt Wendeborn here, petroleum engineering grad and lifelong member of the 12th Man. Alabama 31, Texas A&M 20, in Tuscaloosa. It hurts. But an Aggie stands for the whole game, so let's stand up and look at it.

The start was rough. Less than four minutes in, Marcel Reed was intercepted and Dijon Lee Jr. returned it 39 yards for a touchdown. Coach Mike Elko said afterward that he thought about a quarterback change. And then, friend, Reed went out and played what Elko called probably his best football for the rest of the half. He hit Mario Craver for a 9-yard touchdown, then ran in from 4 yards out for a 14-10 lead. David Olano kicked a 32-yarder before halftime and a 25-yarder in the third. Aggies 20, Tide 17, heading into the fourth. Bryant-Denny got awfully quiet. I may have hummed the War Hymn under my breath.

Then the turn. Fourth-and-1, near midfield, and Reed lost the ball on a sneak. Three plays later, Alabama hit a 38-yard pass to our 5 and scored to take the lead. We had a chance to answer, but Alabama got a sack. Then the Tide scored again. That's the tradition behind the tradition, friend: the fourth quarter is where SEC games get decided.

Hero: the defense held Alabama to 68 rushing yards. Daymion Sanford made eight tackles, Dalton Brooks had seven, and Dezz Ricks intercepted Keelon Russell. Olano was perfect. Craver caught six passes and a touchdown. KJ Edwards ran for 43 yards. The goat, said kindly: ball security. Two interceptions and a fumble against Alabama is a tall order to overcome.

What it means: Texas A&M is 4-4 and 1-4 in the SEC. Per the AP, that's four losses in five conference games after making the Playoff last season. It's tough. But the 12th Man doesn't sit down because the scoreboard says sit. We stand.

Next up: an open date, then at South Carolina on Saturday, Nov. 7, at Williams-Brice Stadium, time and TV to be announced. Two weeks to heal up and get right.

Gig 'em, Aggies. And Howdy, always.

articles.title: Back in the Saddle: Keelon Russell Throws Three Touchdowns as Alabama Ends Its Skid, 31-20 Over Texas A&M
articles.byline: Mary-Kathryn 'MK' Strickland, The Alabama Fanatic
articles.matchup: Alabama 31, Texas A&M 20 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Bryant-Denny Stadium
articles.text:
Well, hello, darlings. Napkins in laps, please. Mary-Kathryn Strickland here, MK to my friends, and Mama is smiling again. Alabama 31, Texas A&M 20, at Bryant-Denny, and our two-game skid is over. I told you a horse teaches you to get right back on. Saturday, the Tide got back on, and rode.

We came out of the gate in style. Less than four minutes in, Dijon Lee Jr. intercepted Marcel Reed and returned it 39 yards for a touchdown. I spilled my sweet tea, and I do not spill sweet tea. But then the Aggies, bless them, came back. Reed ran one in, A&M kicked two field goals, and they led 20-17 heading into the fourth. Mama started fanning herself.

Then came the turn. Texas A&M went for it on fourth-and-1 and Reed lost the ball on a sneak. We took over at midfield. Three plays later, Keelon Russell hit Rico Scott for 38 yards to the A&M 5, and then found Marshall Pritchett for the touchdown. We never trailed again. When the Aggies threatened, Fatutoa Henry, who per the AP was nursing an injury earlier in the week, got home for our first sack of the day. Then Russell found Kaleb Edwards from 8 yards out. Thirty-one to twenty. Pass the pecan pie.

Hero: Russell, 19 of 30 for 311 yards and three touchdowns, two of them in the fourth quarter. And Scott, six catches for 156 yards; coach Kalen DeBoer said Rico came up in a big way. Lee, of course, for that interception return, darling. Chuck McDonald III also got his first career interception, Caleb Woodson made 10 tackles, and the defense held A&M to 278 yards. The goat, with a pat on the hand: Conor Talty, one for three on field goals. Even the best-bred horse stumbles.

What it means: Alabama is 6-2 and 4-2 in the SEC and climbed to No. 10 in the AP poll released Oct. 25. Per the AP, the Tide avoided its first three-game losing streak since 2007, and a Playoff spot is well within reach if we keep winning.

Next up: an open date, and then the big one, at LSU on Saturday, Nov. 7, time and TV to be announced. Death Valley at night, I hope. Mama will bring her pearls.

Roll Tide, darlings. Roll Tide.

articles.title: A Proud First Start, a Tough Harvest: Kansas State Falls at Arizona State, 28-17
articles.byline: Hattie Brandvold, The Kansas State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Arizona State 28, Kansas State 17 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Mountain America Stadium
articles.text:
Well, howdy, Wildcat neighbors. Hattie Brandvold here, on the porch with coffee, a soil probe and a sky going orange over the Flint Hills. Arizona State 28, Kansas State 17, in Tempe. Not every harvest comes in full. But I'll tell you, there was a lot of good grain in this field.

Start with Jacob Knuth. A fifth-year senior, he'd waited a long time for his first career start, and he got it with Avery Johnson sidelined. On our first drive, Knuth threw 7 yards to Jaron Tibbs for a touchdown. In the third quarter, he ran one in from 10 yards out, and we led 17-14. He said afterward it was a moment he'd been waiting for a long time. Coach Collin Klein said he was very proud of him. So am I, son. So am I.

Then the weather turned. On the first play of the fourth quarter, Arizona State freshman Cardae Mack ran 12 yards for the lead. With 6:23 left, he went 11 more for his fourth touchdown. And when we drove late, the Sun Devils sacked Knuth on fourth down. Klein said we lost the battle up front on both sides, and a farmer knows you can't grow much without good ground.

Hero: Knuth, 26 of 41 for 194 yards, a touchdown pass, a touchdown run, and zero turnovers in his first start. Tibbs caught nine passes, Derrick Salley Jr. had six for 63, and Josh Manning caught seven. Jordan Allen had two sacks, and Logan Bartley made 11 tackles. The goat, said over a second cup: fourth downs, where we went 0 for 4. That's four rows left unplanted.

What it means: Kansas State is 4-3 and 1-3 in the Big 12. The Arizona State quarterback carousel spun three times, and we still couldn't catch the ring. But the AP said Knuth performed creditably and protected the ball, and you can build on that.

Next up: at Colorado on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 2 p.m. ET on TNT, at Folsom Field. Halloween in Boulder, with the mountains watching. I'll pack a sweater and the soil probe.

Every Man a Wildcat. Go Cats.

articles.title: Hydrate and Dominate: Freshman Cardae Mack Runs for Four Touchdowns as Arizona State Beats Kansas State, 28-17
articles.byline: Skylar Vanterpool, The Arizona State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Arizona State 28, Kansas State 17 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Mountain America Stadium
articles.text:
Hi, Sun Devils! Skylar Vanterpool here, on a pool float on Tempe Town Lake in spirit, with my 40-ounce water bottle. Take a sip. Okay. Arizona State 28, Kansas State 17! Freshman Cardae Mack ran for four touchdowns, and I ran four laps around my living room, one per touchdown. That's called cross-training.

Here's the workout. Mikey Keene, making his first start, hit Reed Harris for 51 yards on our very first play. Mack scored from 9 yards out to tie it, then from a yard out for a 14-7 lead. Then Keene got hurt in the final minute of the first half and was helped off. We're sending him all the ice packs and good vibes.

The third quarter was a cramp. Kansas State took a 17-14 lead. So coach Kenny Dillingham went to freshman Jake Fette, our third quarterback of the day, who'd thrown two passes all season. Dillingham said the team wanted some energy, and Fette brought it. First play of the fourth quarter: Mack, 12 yards, touchdown. Sun Devils lead. Hydrate! Then, with 6:23 left, Mack took a direct snap and went 11 yards for his fourth touchdown. Twenty-eight to seventeen. And when Kansas State threatened late, another freshman, Julian Hugo, sacked the quarterback on fourth down. Freshmen everywhere! It's like a first-day-of-school photo, but with tackles.

Hero: Mack, 26 carries for 159 yards and four touchdowns. Harris caught six passes for 147 yards. Martell Hughes made 14 tackles, and Owen Long added 10. Per the AP, after giving up 50-plus points in each of its last two Big 12 games, the defense held Kansas State to 84 rushing yards. That's what we call recovery. The goat, with a gentle stretch: the third quarter, when the offense went flat. Nothing a cold water bottle can't fix.

What it means: Arizona State is 4-3 and 2-2 in the Big 12 after a rough week in Lubbock. Dillingham said Fette will start if Keene can't play. Young legs, big hearts.

Next up: at BYU on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3:30 p.m. ET on Fox, at LaVell Edwards Stadium. Halloween in Provo, at altitude, so pack the electrolytes. Take a sip. I'm serious.

Forks up, Sun Devils! Hydrate and dominate!

articles.title: The Model Had Notes: Colorado Leads at Halftime but Falls at Oklahoma State, 57-24
articles.byline: Moss Feldstein, The Colorado Fanatic
articles.matchup: Oklahoma State 57, Colorado 24 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Boone Pickens Stadium
articles.text:
Hey, Buffs. Moss Feldstein here, swinging in my hammock under the Flatirons with a kombucha in one hand and the laptop in the other. The model and I had a long, honest Sunday sunrise talk. Oklahoma State 57, Colorado 24. The model talked. I sipped. Then I sipped a lot.

But first, man, let's appreciate the first half, because it was beautiful. Isaac Wilson threw a 4-yard touchdown to JaQuail Smith, then a 15-yarder to DeAndre Moore Jr. with three seconds left in the first quarter. He ran one in from a yard out. Elliott Arnold drilled a 45-yard field goal. Colorado 24, Oklahoma State 23, at the break, in Stillwater, at their homecoming. The model updated. The model was stoked.

Then the system went chaotic. On the first play of the third quarter, Wilson kept it and fumbled, Oklahoma State recovered at our 24, and two plays later the Cowboys scored to take the lead for good. After that, per the AP, Colorado punted four times and committed three turnovers. Oklahoma State scored 34 straight. In physics, we call that a phase transition. In football, we call it a long night.

Hero: Joseph Williams, nine catches for 135 yards, who kept getting open all night. Moore caught five for 106 and a touchdown. Quanell Farrakhan Jr. had a 51-yard catch. On defense, Gideon Lampron made 14 tackles, Randon Fontenette had 11, and Liona Lefau had 10 plus a sack. Arnold was perfect. The goat, gently: the second half. Zero points. The model ran it twice to be sure. It's zero. We'll find the bug.

What it means: Colorado is 2-5 and 0-4 in the Big 12. There's no hiding from that, and I won't try. But the first half showed the offense can move it on anybody, and there is plenty of signal left in the data set.

Next up: Kansas State comes to Folsom Field on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 2 p.m. ET on TNT. Halloween in Boulder. Ralphie runs, the mountains watch, and I'll be in the stands in a full buffalo costume. Fully peer-reviewed.

Sko Buffs, man. Sko Buffs.

articles.title: Homecoming Rodeo: Oklahoma State Scores 34 Straight After Halftime to Rope Colorado, 57-24
articles.byline: Dusty Lockridge, The Oklahoma State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Oklahoma State 57, Colorado 24 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Boone Pickens Stadium
articles.text:
Howdy, Cowboy family. Dusty Lockridge here, boots on, hat tipped, in a lawn chair on the Strip with an Eskimo Joe's basket in my lap and a grin I can't get off my face. Oklahoma State 57, Colorado 24! America's Greatest Homecoming, and the Cowboys threw the party.

Now, the first half was a bucking bronco. Colorado led 24-23 at the break. Drew Mestemaker hit Miles Coleman for a 47-yard touchdown on the opening drive and Justin Bowick for 14 more, but we kept stalling, and Sam Keltner kept trotting out to kick. Three field goals before halftime. Good kicks. But I wanted touchdowns.

Then came the second half, and friends, that was a clean tie-down run. First play of the third quarter, Colorado's quarterback ran a keeper and fumbled, and safety Quinton Hammonds jumped on it at the Colorado 24. Two plays later, Mestemaker hit tight end Morgan McPhaul from 3 yards out. We led for good. Next drive, Caleb Hawkins ripped off a 39-yard run, and William Mason punched it in. Then Mestemaker found Wyatt Young for 28 yards, Keltner kept splitting the uprights, and Tre Page III finished it with an 18-yard run. Thirty-four to nothing after halftime. Barrier broke clean, roped fast, off the horse before the crowd sat down.

Hero: Mestemaker, 386 yards and four touchdowns. Hawkins ran for 120 and caught five passes for 72. Bowick caught five for 138. And Keltner! Five field goals, a school record, and 18 in a row, which ties Matt Amendola for the program mark, per the AP. LaDainian Fields intercepted two passes, and Ethan Wesloski had two sacks. We piled up 598 yards and 28 first downs. The goat, given a friendly tip of the hat: the first-half red zone, where we kept settling for three. Keltner didn't mind.

What it means: Oklahoma State is 5-2 and 3-1 in the Big 12, and the Cowboys jumped into the AP poll at No. 24 on Oct. 25. Homecoming, a parade, and a ranking. Best week in Stillwater in a while.

Next up: at Iowa State on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 7 p.m. ET on FS1, at Jack Trice Stadium. Halloween night in Ames. Pistol Pete will be in costume, and the costume is Pistol Pete.

Ride 'em, Cowboys. Go Pokes!

articles.title: Hup! Hup! HUP! Virginia Tech Wins at Clemson on Luke Reynolds' Late Touchdown, 20-16
articles.byline: Ruthanne Dellinger, The Virginia Tech Fanatic
articles.matchup: Virginia Tech 20, Clemson 16 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Memorial Stadium (Clemson, SC)
articles.text:
Attention, Hokie Nation! Ruthanne Dellinger reporting, former Corps of Cadets drum major, mace in hand, posture perfect, and knees, frankly, exhausted. Virginia Tech 20, Clemson 16, in Clemson, on Saturday night, in front of more than 80,000 people. Every time our defense made a stop, I jumped and said "hup!" My neighbors in Blacksburg filed a noise report. I filed it in the Lunch Pail.

The march went like this. John Love kicked a 37-yarder in the first quarter. Then, with 1:24 left in the half, Ethan Grunkemeyer found Luke Reynolds from 6 yards out. Ten to three at the half. Hup!

The third quarter was out of step. Clemson kicked a 49-yard field goal, Tait Reynolds ran 16 yards for a touchdown, and Nolan Hauser added a 36-yarder with three seconds left in the quarter. Clemson 16, Tech 10. My mace drooped. Not my posture, though. Never my posture.

Then the fourth quarter, and the band struck up again. Love drilled a 47-yarder with 11:52 left. Sixteen to thirteen. And then, with 1:44 left, Grunkemeyer found Luke Reynolds again, this time from 5 yards out. Twenty to sixteen, Hokies. The defense held on, and I jumped so high I nearly cleared the hedge.

Hero: Luke Reynolds, seven catches and two touchdowns, and he even completed a pass himself, 8 yards. A two-way Reynolds! Grunkemeyer was 20 of 32 for 156 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions. Que'Sean Brown caught five for 69 yards. And the Lunch Pail defense, no names on the backs, but I'll name a few: Jaquez White made 11 tackles and a sack, Kaleb Spencer had nine with two tackles for loss, and Noah Chambers added two more. Zero turnovers for us all night. The goat, given with a respectful salute: the run game, 70 yards. We'll drill it at reveille.

What it means: Virginia Tech is 6-2 with a fourth-quarter comeback win on the road at Clemson, and the Hokies received a vote in the AP poll released Oct. 25. One vote! I'm framing it.

Next up: an open date, then at SMU on Friday, Nov. 6, at 7 p.m. ET on ESPN, at Gerald J. Ford Stadium. Friday night lights in Dallas. I'll bring the mace.

Let's go, Hokies! Hup!

articles.title: A Missed Count Late: Clemson Leads Into the Fourth but Falls to Virginia Tech, 20-16
articles.byline: Dixie-Lynn Pruitt, The Clemson Fanatic
articles.matchup: Virginia Tech 20, Clemson 16 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Memorial Stadium (Clemson, SC)
articles.text:
Well, hey there, y'all. Dixie-Lynn Pruitt here, in my orange rocking chair, Darlene, sipping sweet tea from my orange cup, Beauregard. Darlene isn't rocking this week, sugar. Virginia Tech 20, Clemson 16, at home, on a Saturday night with more than 80,000 of us there. We had this routine nailed until the last few counts.

Let me walk you through the formation. Early on, the Hokies kicked a field goal, and Nolan Hauser answered with a 34-yarder. Then Tech hit a 6-yard touchdown pass late in the half, and we went to the locker room down 10-3. I told Beauregard to stay calm.

Then the third quarter, which, honey, was choreography. Hauser drilled a 49-yarder. Tait Reynolds ran 16 yards for a touchdown, and we led. Then, with three seconds left in the quarter, Hauser kicked a 36-yarder. Clemson 16, Tech 10. Every Tiger hit every count. Darlene was rocking so hard I had to plant my feet.

And then the fourth. Tech kicked a 47-yard field goal with 11:52 left. Then, with 1:44 left, the Hokies threw a 5-yard touchdown pass to their receiver Luke Reynolds. Two Reynoldses on the field, and the wrong one scored last. We couldn't answer. The whole formation looked like a kitchen drawer.

Hero: Hauser, three for three on field goals, including that 49-yarder. Tait Reynolds completed 20 of 26 passes and ran for 63 yards and a touchdown. Tyler Brown caught eight passes, and Gideon Davidson ran for 62 yards. On defense, Will Heldt had two sacks, Corey Myrick made nine tackles, and Sammy Brown had seven. No turnovers for us, either. The goat, sweetly: third down, where we went 3 for 14, and the fourth quarter, when we didn't score. One missed step, and the routine falls apart.

What it means: Clemson is 4-3. That's not the record we wanted, and there's no sugarcoating it. But this team played with grit, and there's football left to play.

Next up: at Florida State on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 7 p.m. ET on ACC Network, at Doak Campbell Stadium. Halloween night in Tallahassee. I'll be dressed as a tiger paw. Darlene's coming.

Go Tigers, y'all.

articles.title: Storm Warning Canceled: Iowa State's Run Game Stalls in a 39-3 Loss at No. 25 Arizona
articles.byline: Twyla Hemmingsen, The Iowa State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Arizona 39, Iowa State 3 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Casino Del Sol Stadium
articles.text:
Good morning, Cyclone Nation, and welcome to the Ames weather center. Here's the honest forecast for last Saturday night in Tucson: clear skies for the home team, and for us, a dry spell. Twyla Hemmingsen here, with my tiny anemometer for emotional support. Arizona 39, Iowa State 3. The anemometer did not spin.

The front came in fast. On the second play of the game, Arizona hit a 71-yard touchdown pass. Next drive, a 6-yard touchdown run. Fifteen to nothing before most folks had found their seats. Kyle Konrardy hit a 40-yard field goal late in the first quarter, and I logged it as a pressure system forming. It did not form. Arizona led 25-3 at halftime.

The key moments came in the first half, too. Per the AP, we crossed Arizona's 40 three times and got only the field goal. We were stopped on a fourth-and-3 at the Wildcats' 22, and we lost a fumble on a pitch while trying to avoid a sack. In the second half, Connor Moberly came in at quarterback, and coach Jimmy Rogers said they were just looking for a spark. Per the AP, we didn't cross midfield after halftime.

Hero: linebacker Sullivan Schlimgen, 15 tackles, a sack and two tackles for loss. That young man was a one-man storm cell. Carson Willich made 10 tackles, and Keyon Washington added eight. Konrardy was perfect. Jaylen Raynor completed eight of 10 passes, and Vince Benetti caught three for 42 yards. The goat, said gently, like a light drizzle: the run game. We'd run for 100 yards in 23 straight games, and Arizona held us to 52. Aiden Flora, one of the nation's top rushers, had 36. Rogers said it was a collective effort, and nobody's pointing fingers. Neither am I.

What it means: Iowa State is 3-4 and 1-3 in the Big 12. That's a tough barometer reading in a first season for a new coach, and I won't pretend otherwise. But storms pass, and fronts change.

Next up: Oklahoma State comes to Jack Trice Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 7 p.m. ET on FS1. Halloween night in Ames. The forecast: cool, crisp, and loud, if we make it that way.

Cyclone Power, everybody. Go State!

articles.title: A Dry Hype Gets Drier: Noah Fifita and the Defense Lead Arizona Past Iowa State, 39-3
articles.byline: Inez Paloverde, The Arizona Fanatic
articles.matchup: Arizona 39, Iowa State 3 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Casino Del Sol Stadium
articles.text:
Hi, hi, hi, Wildcat family! Inez Paloverde here, prickly-pear lemonade in one hand, my old piccolo in the other, and the Catalinas glowing pink behind me. Arizona 39, Iowa State 3! Our first game as a ranked team all season, and the Wildcats played like they'd been ranked forever. It's still warm in Tucson. It's a dry hype.

The piccolo solo started on the second play of the game. Noah Fifita threw it to Isaiah Mizell, and Mizell went 71 yards for a touchdown. Then Henry Gabalis tossed the two-point conversion to Tyler Powell. A trick two-pointer! I squeaked so loud the neighbor's dog joined in. Next drive, Quincy Craig ran it in from 6 yards. Fifteen to nothing. Michael Salgado-Medina banged a 53-yard field goal, and Kedrick Reescano scored from 5 yards out. Twenty-five to three at halftime. Then, in the fourth, Fifita hit Gabalis for a 40-yard touchdown. Gabalis, thrower and catcher!

Hero: Fifita, 27 of 34 for 308 yards and two touchdowns before sitting the rest of the way. Mizell caught eight passes for 134 yards. But the real symphony was the defense. Iowa State came in with a 23-game streak of 100-yard rushing games. We held them to 52 yards on 31 carries. Streak over. Dash Fifita had two sacks, Malcolm Hartzog Jr. split one, Tyrese Boss recovered a fumble, and Cam Chapa made an open-field tackle to stop a fourth-and-3 at our 22. Per the AP, the Cyclones didn't cross midfield in the second half. Coach Brent Brennan called the defense lights out, and I'd play him a fanfare.

The goat, with a gentle trill: the offense got a little sleepy in the second half. Nobody minded. It's a dry hype, not a dry heat.

What it means: Arizona is 6-1 and 3-1 in the Big 12, has won five straight, and moved up to No. 22 in the AP poll released Oct. 25. Per the AP, that's the program's best start since 2014.

Next up: at No. 13 Texas Tech on Saturday, Oct. 31, at noon ET on ESPN. Halloween in Lubbock. I'm packing sunscreen, the piccolo and a whole lot of hope.

Bear Down, Arizona!

articles.title: A Box-Office Bust in Madison: No. 16 USC Falls at Wisconsin, 24-7
articles.byline: Sterling Ashworth-Vance, The USC Fanatic
articles.matchup: Wisconsin 24, USC 7 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Camp Randall Stadium
articles.text:
In a world... where 71,000 people in red jumped around... one team in cardinal and gold... lost the plot.

Good evening. Sterling Ashworth-Vance here, film school graduate, and I'm afraid this week's feature is a disappointment. Wisconsin 24, USC 7, at Camp Randall. Night game, and the critics were not kind. Neither was I. One clapperboard. Generously.

Act One had promise. Down 3-0, Jayden Maiava threw a 4-yard touchdown to Taniela Tupou in the second quarter. USC 7, Wisconsin 3. I cued the swelling strings. Then the plot twist nobody in our writers' room wanted: with less than two minutes left in the first half, Bryan Jackson II, who spent the last two seasons at USC, ran 5 yards for a Wisconsin touchdown. Against us. That's not a twist. That's a sequel nobody ordered.

Act Two dragged. Maiava threw two interceptions in the first half, after coming into the game with three all season, per the AP. In the third quarter, Wisconsin scored a touchdown on fourth-and-2, and then blocked our field goal. Then a 1-yard run in the fourth made it 24-7. Roll credits.

The goat, and I say this with love: the run game. Minus-17 rushing yards. Minus! Coach Lincoln Riley said the team didn't play well enough on any of the three sides of the ball, and didn't coach well enough either. He owned it. I respect a director who owns the edit.

Hero: Tupou, six catches and the touchdown. Maiava threw for 258 yards, and Trent Mosley, Tanook Hines and Kayden Dixon-Wyatt each caught at least four passes. On defense, Desman Stephens II made eight tackles, Luke Wafle had a sack, and Kameryn Crawford had two tackles for loss. They kept us within range for a long time.

What it means: USC dropped out of the AP poll released Oct. 25. A tough review. But every great franchise has a bad installment, and the next one is a blockbuster.

Next up: No. 2 Ohio State comes to the Coliseum on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 7:30 p.m. ET on NBC. Halloween night, prime time, the biggest stage in Los Angeles. If there's ever a night for a comeback story, that's it.

Fight On, Trojans. Fade to cardinal and gold.

articles.title: Oom-Pah Upset! Bryan Jackson Scores Against His Old Team as Wisconsin Stuns No. 16 USC, 24-7
articles.byline: Lars 'Brat' Ellefson, The Wisconsin Fanatic
articles.matchup: Wisconsin 24, USC 7 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Camp Randall Stadium
articles.text:
Oom-pah, oom-pah, oom-pah-pah!

That's the polka break, folks, and this week I did about 40 of them. Lars "Brat" Ellefson here, with a brat on the grill and my knees fully loosened. Wisconsin 24, No. 16 USC 7, under the lights at Camp Randall! That's our second win over a ranked team this year, after the one at Penn State in September. And now the Badgers are ranked, too.

The story writes itself, and it's a good one. Bryan Jackson II spent the last two seasons at USC. Saturday night, against his old team, with less than two minutes left in the first half, he ran 5 yards for a touchdown. His first as a Badger! Wisconsin 10, USC 7. Oom-pah!

Then the dagger, served with mustard. Third quarter, fourth-and-2, and Colton Joseph threw a 16-yard touchdown to Chris Brooks Jr. Seventeen to seven. Late in the third, Junior Poyser blocked a USC field goal. And in the fourth, Ryan Schwendeman plunged in from a yard out. Twenty-four to seven. I polka'd so hard I knocked the brat tongs into the cooler.

Hero: the defense. All of it. USC finished with minus-17 rushing yards. Minus! Sebastian Cheeks had two and a half sacks, Mason Posa had one and a half, and Cooper Catalano made 10 tackles. Cairo Skanes and Bryce West each intercepted a pass in the first half, and Matthew Jung broke up three passes. Per the AP, the defense held USC to 92 yards in the first half. Gavin Lahm made a 33-yard field goal and every extra point. Abu Sama III ran for 71 yards. The goat, with a friendly elbow: our passing game, 58 yards. But Joseph completed 12 of 14, so it was efficient, like a good bratwurst.

What it means: Wisconsin is 5-2 and 3-1 in the Big Ten, and the Badgers entered the AP poll at No. 25 on Oct. 25. Coach Luke Fickell said Jackson showed something special. So did the whole stadium.

Next up: at Iowa on Saturday, Oct. 31, at noon ET on Fox, at Kinnick Stadium. Halloween at noon, with the Heartland Trophy on the mind. I'll pack extra brats.

Oom-pah-pah! On, Wisconsin!

articles.title: A Southern Novel With a Cruel Final Chapter: No. 7 Ole Miss Rallies From 21 Down, Falls at Texas 34-27
articles.byline: Langston Fairbanks, The Ole Miss Fanatic
articles.matchup: Texas 34, Ole Miss 27 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium
articles.text:
Gentle reader, permit me a moment. I am seated on a bench on the Square in Oxford, the courthouse clock is chiming, and my coffee has gone cold, as coffee will when a man has spent a Saturday night riding the full arc of a Southern tragedy. Texas 34, Ole Miss 27. The ending was cruel. But the middle chapters, my friends, were glorious.

Our first half was a slim prologue. Texas led 24-3 at halftime. But there was a spark: facing fourth down late in the half, punter Oscar Bird ran 17 yards on a fake. A punter! Running! Mr. Faulkner himself could not have written it better. Texas held at the goal, but the seed of the plot was planted.

Then the second half, and the novel came alive. On Texas' first possession, Blake Purchase hit Arch Manning from the blind side, and Kam Franklin chased the bouncing ball and recovered it in the end zone. Touchdown, Rebels! Then Trinidad Chambliss found Horatio Fields from 6 yards out. Then, early in the fourth, Fields made a contested catch in the end zone from 27 yards. Twenty-four to twenty-four! Twenty-one points erased. I spilled my coffee on my seersucker and I regret nothing.

Alas. Texas broke a 47-yard run and scored on a fake handoff, and then kicked a field goal. Lucas Carneiro answered with a 39-yarder, and we recovered an onside kick! The final page turned. Chambliss threw to the end zone, and it was intercepted. Fin.

Hero: Franklin, a sack, two tackles for loss and that touchdown. Fields, two scoring catches. Jalyn Crawford intercepted two passes, and Keaton Thomas made eight tackles. Deuce Alexander caught eight passes for 87 yards. The goat, gently: the slow start. And our hearts go out to Kewan Lacy, who left with a shoulder injury, per coach Pete Golding.

What it means: Ole Miss is 5-2 and 3-2 in the SEC and slipped to No. 12 in the AP poll released Oct. 25. Coach Golding said the team believed it could get back in it. It did. That's the kind of character a long season needs.

Next up: Auburn visits Vaught-Hemingway Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 12:45 p.m. ET on SEC Network. Halloween afternoon at home, back in the Grove's embrace.

Until then, gentle reader, refill your cup. Hotty Toddy.

articles.title: Hook 'Em, Hold On: Arch Manning Runs for Two Scores as Texas Survives No. 7 Ole Miss, 34-27
articles.byline: Caro Whitfield, The Texas Fanatic
articles.matchup: Texas 34, Ole Miss 27 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium
articles.text:
Well, hello, y'all. Caro Whitfield, from the Forty Acres, where the Tower is glowing burnt orange, and darling, I needed to see that glow. Texas 34, No. 7 Ole Miss 27. Did we make it harder than it needed to be? Honey, we made it a whole quarterly report. But a win is a win, and this one ended a two-game skid.

The first half was a board meeting where every slide landed. Arch Manning ran one in from 2 yards out. Then he hit Ryan Wingo for a 50-yard touchdown. Michael Terry III ran in from 2 more. And just before halftime, our defense stopped Ole Miss at the goal. Texas 24, Ole Miss 3. I was mentally drafting the press release.

Then the third quarter happened, and the press release went in the shredder. On the first possession of the half, Manning got hit from the blind side, and Ole Miss recovered in the end zone. Then the Rebels threw two touchdowns to Horatio Fields, and it was 24-24 early in the fourth. Per the AP, we set season highs with 14 penalties for 134 yards. Coach Steve Sarkisian said we weren't perfect, and he could recite the penalty yards. So could I.

And then, the comeback within the comeback. Raleek Brown broke a 47-yard run, and Manning faked the handoff and strolled around the end untouched from a yard out. Thirty-one to twenty-four. Gianni Spetic made it 34-24 with a 33-yarder. Ole Miss kicked a field goal and recovered an onside kick, which made my blood pressure a key metric. But on the final play, Jelani McDonald intercepted the pass in the end zone. Hook 'em!

Hero: Brown, 157 rushing yards, and Manning, a touchdown pass and his first two rushing scores of the season. Wingo caught seven passes for 111 yards. McDonald made 12 tackles plus the game-ending interception, and Justin Cryer and Rasheem Biles also intercepted passes. Spetic was perfect. The goat, with my most diplomatic smile: penalties and special teams. We'll address that in the Q4 review.
