articles.title: Six Feet of Snow! Calvin Russell III Wins It in OT as Syracuse Stuns North Carolina, 31-30
articles.byline: Nico Calabrese, The Syracuse Fanatic
articles.matchup: Syracuse 31, North Carolina 30 (final, OT), Sat., Oct. 24, Kenan Stadium
articles.text:
Hey there, Orange Nation. Nico Calabrese here, Central New York born, lake-effect tested, and shovel certified. One foot of snow is a nice play. Three feet is a highlight. Six feet means school's canceled. And folks? After Saturday night in Chapel Hill, cancel everything. Syracuse 31, North Carolina 30, in overtime. Our first ACC win of the year!

It looked like a gray, slushy night for a while. UNC jumped out 10-0, and it was 20-10 heading into the fourth quarter. Then the snow started falling. Steve Angeli, making his first start since September, hit Umari Hatcher for a 76-yard touchdown. Four feet, easy. Twenty to seventeen.

UNC answered with a field goal, and with 1:54 left, Tylik Hill punched in a 3-yard touchdown run. We had the lead... and the extra point missed. Tied at 23. I shoveled my own driveway in frustration, and I live in an apartment.

Overtime. Carolina scored first, a 3-yard touchdown pass to Demon June. Now we needed a touchdown just to keep going. Angeli found Calvin Russell III from 4 yards out. Touchdown! And then, instead of kicking it, we went for two and the win. Angeli to Russell again. Good! Game over! SIX FEET! Schools are closed from Syracuse to Watertown!

Hero: Russell, eight catches for 86 yards plus both scores in overtime. Ahmad Miller carried the ball 30 times for 125 yards and a touchdown, which is the football version of shoveling the whole block. Hatcher had 103 receiving yards on four catches. On defense, Chris D'Appolonia had eight tackles and a sack, and we didn't commit a turnover all night. The goat, with a warm cup of cocoa: that missed extra point. It all worked out, kid.

What it means: Syracuse is 3-4 and 1-4 in the ACC. Coach Fran Brown said the city and the alums have been waiting for this, and that a weight came off their shoulders. Angeli is the fifth quarterback to play for the Orange this year, and he looked great.

Next up: No. 19 SMU comes to the Dome on Saturday, Oct. 31, at noon ET on ESPN2. Halloween in Syracuse. Dress warm, Orange Nation. You know the drill.

Let's Go Orange!

articles.title: Oh, Sugar: North Carolina Falls to Syracuse 31-30 on an Overtime Two-Pointer
articles.byline: Ainsley Pemberton, The North Carolina Fanatic
articles.matchup: Syracuse 31, North Carolina 30 (final, OT), Sat., Oct. 24, Kenan Stadium
articles.text:
Well, hello, darlings. Ainsley Pemberton here, pearls slightly askew, kinesiology PhD in hand, and a heart that is, I confess, a little bruised. Syracuse 31, North Carolina 30, in overtime at Kenan. One point, sugar. One two-point conversion. Let me pour us both a sweet tea.

We started like a debutante's first waltz. Billy Edwards Jr. completed his first 11 passes, flawless footwork, hips square to the target. Jordan Shipp caught a 5-yard touchdown, Rece Verhoff kicked a field goal, and it was 10-0 after one quarter. In the third, on fourth-and-1, Demon June ran 25 yards for a touchdown, the longest run of our season, per the AP. Twenty to ten. I was already picturing the after-party.

And then the fourth quarter. Syracuse hit a 76-yard touchdown pass. We drove deep into their territory but settled for a 22-yard field goal. Then Syracuse scored with 1:54 left, but missed the extra point. Tied at 23. Overtime. Fine. We can do overtime.

We scored first, too! Edwards to June, 3 yards. Touchdown, Tar Heels! But Syracuse answered with a touchdown and then went for two and the win. The pass was complete. Oh, sugar.

Hero: Edwards, a season-high 271 yards and two touchdowns, and Shipp, eight catches for 102 yards. Jelani Thurman added seven catches for 77. Verhoff made all three field goals and every extra point. Derek McDonald made 16 tackles, and Peyton Seelmann had 11 and a sack. And we didn't turn it over once. The goat, with a gentle pat: the red zone in the fourth quarter. A touchdown there and we'd be having a very different tea party.

What it means: North Carolina is 4-3 and 2-2 in the ACC. Coach Bill Belichick said Syracuse made a couple more plays, and that was the difference. Darlings, he's right. One play.

Next up: No. 1 Miami visits Kenan Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 7:30 p.m. ET on ABC. Halloween night, prime time, and the best team in the country. If we want to make a statement, there's no grander ballroom.

Go Heels! And, as always, a gentle word for Duke: hush.

articles.title: A Song in a Minor Key: Vanderbilt Leads Early, Falls at No. 12 Kentucky 34-17
articles.byline: Penelope 'Pippa' Ashcroft, The Vanderbilt Fanatic
articles.matchup: Kentucky 34, Vanderbilt 17 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Kroger Field
articles.text:
Hey, y'all, it's Pippa Ashcroft, back on my bench in Centennial Park in front of the Parthenon, guitar in my lap. Kentucky 34, Vanderbilt 17. I'll be honest with you, darlin': this week's song is in a minor key again. But the first verse? The first verse was a stadium anthem.

Verse one: we owned that first quarter in Lexington. Per the AP, Vandy had the ball for more than 17 minutes of it, converted six of our first eight third downs and outgained Kentucky 142 yards to 14. Brock Taylor kicked a 30-yard field goal, and then Jared Curtis hit Jayvontay Conner for a 3-yard touchdown. Ten to nothing, Commodores! I strummed so hard I broke a string.

Verse two is where the melody turned. Kentucky scored twice in the second quarter, the last one with 21 seconds before halftime, and then again early in the third. Twenty-one to ten. But we came back with a touchdown on fourth and short, Curtis to Ja'Cory Thomas from 34 yards out. Twenty-one to seventeen! The crowd got quiet. That's the bridge, y'all. The bridge is always the best part.

The final verse belonged to Kentucky: two field goals and a short touchdown run. Thirteen straight points.

Hero: Curtis, our freshman quarterback, 27 of 36 for 247 yards and two touchdowns. That's a kid writing his own hit record. Junior Sherrill caught eight passes for 78 yards, and Cole Spence had five catches. On defense, Bryce Cowan made 12 tackles and Nick Rinaldi made 10. The goat, sung with love: the run game, 15 yards all night. And the turnovers, an interception and a lost fumble, didn't help the harmony.

What it means: Vanderbilt is 3-5 and still looking for that first SEC win. Per the AP, there are four games left in the regular season. Four more chances to write the comeback single. I've got the chorus half-finished already.

Next up: an off week on Oct. 31, then at Mississippi State on Saturday, Nov. 7, time to be announced. Plenty of time to tune up.

Anchor Down, y'all. The sad songs are always the setup.

articles.title: Alone at the Top of the SEC! No. 12 Kentucky Rallies Past Vanderbilt, 34-17
articles.byline: Rhett Abernathy-Coyle, The Kentucky Fanatic
articles.matchup: Kentucky 34, Vanderbilt 17 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Kroger Field
articles.text:
Good evening, friends, and welcome back to the paddock. Rhett Abernathy-Coyle here, on my fence rail off Versailles Road, in my lucky seersucker for the eighth straight week, because I do not mess with a streak. And friends? Kentucky 34, Vanderbilt 17. We are 7-1. And per the AP, we are alone in first place in the Southeastern Conference. I read that out loud to my mare, Lady Bluegrass, and she whinnied. I'm counting it as agreement.

It did not start like a coronation. Vanderbilt led 10-0, and per the AP, we had 14 yards in the first quarter. Fourteen! Lady Bluegrass travels farther than that on her way to breakfast. But then, the second quarter. Kenny Minchey found DJ Miller for a 9-yard touchdown. And with 21 seconds left in the half, Willie Rodriguez ran it in from a yard out. Fourteen to ten. Back in stride.

The third quarter, Brennen Ward ran 10 yards for a touchdown. Vandy answered with a 34-yard touchdown pass to make it 21-17, and my seersucker started to sweat. Then Adam Zouagui made a 47-yard field goal and a 32-yarder, and Minchey ran one in from a yard out with 5:11 left. Thirteen straight points to finish it. That's a horse that knows how to close.

Hero: Minchey, 19 of 26 for 203 yards with a touchdown pass and a touchdown run. Rodriguez caught six passes for 67 yards and scored. Kenny Darby had a 44-yard catch. Jovantae Barnes ran for 68 yards. And the defense held Vandy to 15 rushing yards, with an interception from Ty Bryant, a fumble recovery from Tavion Gadson and a sack from Mi'Quise Humphrey-Grace. Zouagui was perfect. The goat, with a gentle pat on the nose: that first quarter. Shake it off, fellas.

What it means: Kentucky clinched a winning SEC record for the third time since 1977, and the AP says we haven't been this close to an SEC title since 1976. We jumped to No. 9 in the AP poll released Oct. 25. Coach Will Stein said this was one of our best games, and he's proud of the team's toughness and fight.

Next up: a well-earned week off on Oct. 31, then at Tennessee on Saturday, Nov. 7, time to be announced. Rest the legs, friends. The stretch run is coming.

Go Big Blue! See you in the paddock.

articles.title: So Close to Orbit: No. 14 Houston Leads Late, Falls at Unbeaten No. 10 Utah 21-13
articles.byline: Yolanda 'Yo' Pacheco, The Houston Fanatic
articles.matchup: Utah 21, Houston 13 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Rice-Eccles Stadium
articles.text:
Mission Control to Coog Nation, do you copy? Yo Pacheco here, engineer by day, film grinder by night, legal pad in hand. Final telemetry from Salt Lake City: Utah 21, Houston 13. We had the rocket on the pad, fueled and climbing, with a lead in the fourth quarter. Then a couple of systems failed. Houston, we have a problem. But what a flight it was.

Stage one, the first half: our defense put a lid on Utah. The Utes had zero points at the break, and Jonathan Dimas kicked a 24-yard field goal. Then stage two. Coming out of halftime, we drove 75 yards in 15 plays and chewed 8:14 off the clock, and Makhi Hughes plunged in from 2 yards out. Houston 10, Utah 0. I wrote "NOMINAL" on my legal pad in all caps.

Utah answered with a touchdown run, and Dimas drilled a 47-yarder. Houston 13, Utah 7. But early in the fourth, Utah took a 14-13 lead on a direct snap. Then our defense delivered: Latreveon McCutchin intercepted Utah's quarterback. Kentrell Webb had an interception, too. Still a one-point game.

Then the anomaly. With 2:15 left, Utah blitzed, sacked Conner Weigman, and recovered the fumble at our 9. One play later, it was 21-13. Weigman drove us to the Utah 23, but four straight passes fell incomplete. Per the AP, it was our only turnover. It came at the worst time.

Hero: Amare Thomas, five catches for 133 yards, tying his season high. That man is a booster rocket. Weigman threw for 282 yards. Dimas made both field goals. Carmycah Glass made 10 tackles. The goat, with full crew support: the fourth quarter. We were close to sticking the landing.

What it means: Houston is 6-2 and 3-2 in the Big 12 and slipped to No. 18 in the AP poll released Oct. 25. The AP says Houston is a few plays away from the top of the conference. I agree. We went toe-to-toe with an unbeaten team in its own stadium.

Next up: an off week on Oct. 31 for repairs and refueling, then Cincinnati visits TDECU Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7, time to be announced.

Coog Nation, stay on frequency. Go Coogs!

articles.title: Send It! Devon Dampier Runs for 150 as No. 10 Utah Rallies Past No. 14 Houston, Stays Perfect
articles.byline: Aspen Mortensen, The Utah Fanatic
articles.matchup: Utah 21, Houston 13 (final), Sat., Oct. 24, Rice-Eccles Stadium
articles.text:
Hey, Utes. Aspen Mortensen here, boots clicked into my old race skis in the living room, because I'm still too fired up to sit down. Utah 21, No. 14 Houston 13. We are 7-0. That's 13 straight wins, the longest active streak in college football, per the AP. Send it, no fear!

But friends, the first half was a course full of ruts. Houston stuffed our run game. Our best drive ended at halftime with a missed field goal after a sloppy snap and hold. Houston led 3-0 at the break, then opened the third with a 15-play touchdown drive. Ten to nothing. Per the AP, Dampier told coach Morgan Scalley not to worry. And then he went out and skied the cleanest run of the night.

Dampier ran for a 22-yard touchdown, accounting for every yard of the drive. Houston kicked a field goal to make it 13-7, but early in the fourth, Wayshawn Parker took a direct snap and bolted 5 yards for the touchdown. Utah 14, Houston 13! First lead of the night.

Then the gate that decided the race. With 2:15 left, Jackson Bennee blitzed and sacked Conner Weigman, the ball popped loose, and Jireh Moe recovered at the Houston 9. On the very next play, Dampier ran it in. Twenty-one to thirteen! Houston drove to our 23, but threw four straight incompletions. Clean through the final gate!

Hero: Dampier. 150 rushing yards, a season high, and two touchdowns, plus 204 passing yards. He threw two interceptions, and that's the goat, with love: a couple of hooked tips. But he crossed the finish first. Bennee had a sack and a forced fumble, Moe recovered it and had a sack of his own, and Trey Reynolds made nine tackles. Creed Whittemore caught four passes for 53 yards.

What it means: Utah is 7-0 and 4-0 in the Big 12, did it in front of its 100th straight sellout, per the AP, and jumped to No. 6 in the AP poll released Oct. 25.

summary.text: No. 10 Utah beat No. 14 Houston 21-13 on Saturday night, Oct. 24, at Rice-Eccles Stadium after trailing 10-0 in the third quarter.
Devon Dampier ran for 150 yards and two touchdowns, including a 9-yard score after Jackson Bennee's sack forced a fumble that Jireh Moe recovered at the Houston 9.
Utah (7-0, 4-0 Big 12) extended the longest active winning streak in college football to 13 games and is one of three unbeaten teams with Miami and UCLA, per the AP.
Utah rose to No. 6 in the Oct. 25 AP poll and plays at Cincinnati on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3:45 p.m. ET on ESPN.
